We must seek the substantive fulfillment of the sovereign’s service to Heaven. Thus, in everything that establishes laws and institutions to regulate affairs from beginning to end, we seek to give the people a secure resting place. Calling this “diligent application” makes it clear that promoting beneficial use and enriching livelihood…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
而脩八政於五事之後者不容已矣此非次三
之疇矣乎龜文之四其數則齊乎巽位於偶也
禹也神而明之遂第其數曰斯疇也其配之以
五紀乎蓋君之八政既脩矣國體所存必因時
而加省焉五紀者天之所以示乎人者也天道
之運不同而曆數之紀在我必動則求端於天
而欽曆象以授民時者悉致其推步之法事則
求合於道而觀天文以察時變者祗順乎氣朔
之常謂之曰協則知制曆明時而考五紀於八
===
政之後者不容緩矣此非次四之疇矣乎是知
厚之以八政則政不失時矣協之以五紀則術
不違天矣二者相須以成變化斯皇極之所由
建也夫嘗考之二而四四而八者八卦之象也
象成于二則爲偶一而三三而九者九疇之數
也數始于一則爲奇故曰紀天地之撰者範之
數盡之矣自夫範錫神禹而箕子發之以告武
王其於次三之疇則言農用八政八政之首則
又先之曰食蓋農爲王業之根本周自后稷以
punctuated: 而脩八政於五事之後者，不容已矣。此非次三之疇矣乎？龜文之四，其數則齊乎巽，位於偶也。禹也神而明之，遂第其數曰：「斯疇也，其配之以五紀乎？」蓋君之八政既脩矣，國體所存，必因時而加省焉。五紀者，天之所以示乎人者也。天道之運不同，而曆數之紀在我。必動則求端於天，而欽曆象以授民時者，悉致其推步之法；事則求合於道，而觀天文以察時變者，祗順乎氣朔之常。謂之曰協，則知制曆明時，而考五紀於八政之後者，不容緩矣。此非次四之疇矣乎？是知厚之以八政，則政不失時矣；協之以五紀，則術不違天矣。二者相須以成變化，斯皇極之所由建也。夫嘗考之，二而四，四而八者，八卦之象也；象成于二，則爲偶。一而三，三而九者，九疇之數也；數始于一，則爲奇。故曰：「紀天地之撰者，範之數盡之矣。」自夫範錫神禹，而箕子發之以告武王，其於次三之疇，則言農用八政；八政之首，則又先之曰食。蓋農爲王業之根本，周自后稷以
translation_en:
…and that cultivating the eight affairs of government after the five personal functions is indispensable. Is this not the third category? As for the fourth marking on the tortoise shell, its number corresponds to Xun, occupying an even position. Yu, comprehending it with spiritual insight, accordingly ordered its number and said: “Should this category not be matched with the five regulators of time?” Once the ruler has cultivated the eight affairs of government, the maintenance of the state requires further scrutiny in accordance with the seasons. The five regulators are the means by which Heaven gives indications to humankind. The movements of Heaven’s way vary, but the ordering of calendrical numbers rests with us. In every undertaking, one must seek its beginnings in Heaven: those who reverently calculate and observe the celestial phenomena to give the people their seasons must fully apply the methods of astronomical calculation. In every affair, one must seek conformity with the Way: those who observe celestial patterns to discern seasonal changes must reverently follow the regular sequence of solar terms and new moons. Calling this “harmonizing” makes clear that establishing the calendar and clarifying the seasons, and examining the five regulators after attending to the eight affairs of government, admit of no delay. Is this not the fourth category? Thus we know that, by giving ample attention to the eight affairs of government, administration will not miss its proper seasons; by harmonizing through the five regulators, its methods will not contravene Heaven. These two depend on one another to accomplish change and transformation; through them the royal ultimate is established.
Now, I have examined this: two becoming four, and four becoming eight, describes the images of the eight trigrams. Since these images are formed from two, they are even. One becoming three, and three becoming nine, describes the numbers of the nine categories. Since these numbers begin with one, they are odd. Hence it is said: “The numbers of the Great Plan fully encompass the ordering of Heaven’s and Earth’s workings.” After the Great Plan was bestowed upon the divine Yu, Jizi expounded it to King Wu. Concerning the third category, he spoke of giving ample attention to the eight affairs of government. At the head of those eight affairs, moreover, he placed food first. Agriculture is indeed the foundation of kingly enterprise. The Zhou, from Hou Ji onward, through…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
農事開國詩書所稱康功田功豳風七月皆是
物也故曰帝王所傳心法之要蓋本諸此噫此
禹疇箕範所以得道統之傳也歟
詩
瑟彼玉瓚黃流在中豈弟君子福祿攸降
高克謙
同考試官教諭廖批篇中發明德福相因之
意詳盡取之
同考試官教諭劉批詞意警飭詠歌文王之
===
德宛然在目是善說詩者
同考試官教諭張批得詩人之旨
考試官學正馮批醇正
考試官學正劉批雅健
詩人咏歌聖君之德必與其德盛而福自至焉
蓋德與福相因者也有是德卽有是福矣文王
以之宜詩人咏歌以彰其盛歟其全意蓋謂惟德
動天惟天眷德必得其福者必有其德者也盍
自我文王觀之彼瑟然之玉瓚黃流必在其中
punctuated:
農事開國，詩書所稱康功、田功、豳風七月，皆是物也。故曰：帝王所傳心法之要，蓋本諸此。噫！此禹疇箕範所以得道統之傳也歟！

詩
瑟彼玉瓚，黃流在中。豈弟君子，福祿攸降。
高克謙

同考試官教諭廖批：篇中發明德福相因之意，詳盡，取之。
同考試官教諭劉批：詞意警飭，詠歌文王之德，宛然在目，是善說詩者。
同考試官教諭張批：得詩人之旨。
考試官學正馮批：醇正。
考試官學正劉批：雅健。

詩人咏歌聖君之德，必與其德盛而福自至焉。蓋德與福相因者也，有是德卽有是福矣。文王以之，宜詩人咏歌以彰其盛歟！其全意蓋謂：惟德動天，惟天眷德，必得其福者，必有其德者也。盍自我文王觀之？彼瑟然之玉瓚，黃流必在其中
translation_en:
…founded its state through agriculture. The achievements in securing the people's well-being and in cultivating the fields praised in the Odes and the Documents, and “The Seventh Month” in the “Airs of Bin,” all concern this. Thus it is said that the essentials of the teaching of the mind transmitted by emperors and kings are rooted here. Ah! Is this not why Yu's Categories and Jizi's Great Plan received the transmission of the succession of the Way?

Odes
“Resplendent is that jade libation ladle; yellow sacrificial wine fills it. The joyful and gracious lord is he upon whom blessings and emoluments descend.”
Gao Keqian

Comment by Associate Examiner Liao, Instructor: “The essay explains fully and exhaustively how virtue and blessings are connected. I select it.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor: “The language and ideas are incisive and disciplined. In celebrating King Wen's virtue, it brings him vividly before our eyes. This is someone skilled at interpreting the Odes.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “It captures the poet's intent.”
Comment by Examiner Feng, Instructor: “Pure and correct.”
Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: “Elegant and vigorous.”

When the poet celebrates the virtue of a sage ruler, he invariably affirms that the ruler's virtue is abundant and that blessings come of themselves. For virtue and blessings are interconnected: where there is such virtue, there will be such blessings. King Wen exemplified this; how fitting that the poet should celebrate him in song to make manifest his abundance! The passage's overall meaning is this: virtue alone moves Heaven, and Heaven cherishes virtue; whoever is assured of receiving such blessings must possess such virtue. Why not consider our King Wen? That resplendent jade libation ladle must have yellow sacrificial wine within it…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
矣是蓋温潤之質自具夫居珍之體而鬱鬯之
薦式用乎美器之陳惟器味之相須而後有廟
之享假必物品之類聚而後裸將之禮成玉瓚
不與黃流期而黃流自注焉況我文王徽柔之
懿著而爲容保之光純一之誠顯而爲順應之
度肅肅之際雝雝寓焉有和樂而無拂戾翼翼
之中亹亹存焉有平易而無險僻信豈弟之君
子也福祿寧不下其躬乎是蓋盛德永貞之下
有以立昭受之基而有命既集之餘誕膺夫聿
===
懷之慶螽斯之錫胤麟趾之肖賢凡所以厚于
身厚于家者福無不備也兔罝之多才漢廣之
弘化凡所以宜于臣宜于民者福罔不極也君
子不與福祿期而福祿自至矣是則天人之相
與也其幾雖微而德福之相須也其理有定詩
人有得於觀感之際其能已於咏歌也哉考之
洪範次九曰嚮用五福威用六極而必先之以
五行五事八政五紀以建皇極而三德稽疑庶
徵因之以見必作德以斂福而福澤不降於淫
punctuated: 矣。是蓋温潤之質，自具夫居珍之體，而鬱鬯之薦，式用乎美器之陳。惟器味之相須，而後有廟之享假；必物品之類聚，而後裸將之禮成。玉瓚不與黃流期，而黃流自注焉。況我文王，徽柔之懿著，而爲容保之光；純一之誠顯，而爲順應之度。肅肅之際，雝雝寓焉，有和樂而無拂戾；翼翼之中，亹亹存焉，有平易而無險僻。信豈弟之君子也，福祿寧不下其躬乎？是蓋盛德永貞之下，有以立昭受之基；而有命既集之餘，誕膺夫聿懷之慶。螽斯之錫胤，麟趾之肖賢，凡所以厚于身、厚于家者，福無不備也；兔罝之多才，漢廣之弘化，凡所以宜于臣、宜于民者，福罔不極也。君子不與福祿期，而福祿自至矣。是則天人之相與也，其幾雖微，而德福之相須也，其理有定。詩人有得於觀感之際，其能已於咏歌也哉？考之《洪範》，次九曰：「嚮用五福，威用六極。」而必先之以五行、五事、八政、五紀，以建皇極，而三德、稽疑、庶徵因之，以見必作德以斂福，而福澤不降於淫
translation_en:
…indeed. Its warm and lustrous substance inherently gives it the character of a vessel fit to hold precious contents [?], while the offering of fragrant sacrificial wine calls for the presentation of a beautiful vessel. Only when vessel and contents complement one another can offerings be presented in the ancestral temple; only when objects of corresponding kinds are brought together can the libation rite be accomplished. The jade libation ladle makes no appointment with the yellow wine, yet the yellow wine naturally pours into it. How much more is this true of our King Wen! His admirable goodness and gentleness shone forth as the glory of his embracing and protecting others; his sincerity, pure and undivided, manifested itself as the measure of his compliant responsiveness. Within his solemn reverence dwelt harmony: there was concord and joy, without opposition or discord. Within his vigilant care abided tireless diligence: there was evenness and ease, without deviousness or perversity. Truly he was an amiable and gracious lord. Could blessings and emoluments fail to descend upon him?

His abundant virtue, enduringly steadfast, established the foundation for his illustrious reception of blessings; once the Mandate had gathered upon him, he received in full the felicity of winning others to his embrace. The bestowal of descendants celebrated in The Locusts (Zhongsi), and the worthy offspring resembling their forebears in The Qilin’s Hoof (Linzhi)—in everything that enriched his person and his household, no blessing was lacking. The abundance of talented men in The Rabbit Net (Tuju), and the far-reaching moral transformation in The Broad Han (Hanguang)—in everything that benefited his ministers and his people, blessings reached their utmost extent. The lord makes no appointment with blessings and emoluments, yet blessings and emoluments arrive of themselves.

Such is the mutual relationship between Heaven and humanity. Though its workings are subtle, the principle by which virtue and blessings depend upon one another is fixed. Having apprehended something through observation and inward response, how could the poet refrain from singing praise? Examining The Great Plan (Hongfan), we find that its ninth division says: “Encourage with the five blessings; overawe with the six extremes of suffering.” Yet these must first be preceded by the five phases, the five personal activities, the eight affairs of government, and the five regulators of time, so as to establish the August Standard. The three virtues, the examination of doubts, and the various verifications follow upon this. This shows that one must cultivate virtue to gather blessings, and that blessings and bounty do not descend upon the licentious …

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
人也周自后稷以來世德作求罔墜厥紹是用
享祚靈長取數以類而應豈直於文王之世一
時歌咏而已哉詩可以觀於此益信
湯孫奏假綏我思成鞉鼓淵淵嘒嘒管聲
既和且平依我磬聲於赫湯孫穆穆厥
聲
汪梯
同考試官教諭廖批斂華就實而意味雋永
必有養之士也録之
===
同考試官教諭劉批以聲之和平為樂之美
良是而詞旨鏗然不露庶幾一倡三嘆者矣
同考試官教諭張批簡嚴得商頌體
考試官學正馮批典重不浮
考試官學正劉批雅蔚
詩人言商王作樂以格先而因詳其樂聲之美
也夫惟樂可以感神也商王有焉其知盡祭之
義者歟此祀成湯之樂也蓋曰通幽明之感者
存乎祭重神明之交者存乎樂我湯孫之祭也
punctuated:
人也。周自后稷以來，世德作求，罔墜厥紹，是用享祚靈長，取數以類而應，豈直於文王之世一時歌咏而已哉？詩可以觀，於此益信。
湯孫奏假，綏我思成。鞉鼓淵淵，嘒嘒管聲。既和且平，依我磬聲。於赫湯孫，穆穆厥聲。
汪梯
同考試官教諭廖批：斂華就實，而意味雋永，必有養之士也。録之。
同考試官教諭劉批：以聲之和平為樂之美，良是，而詞旨鏗然不露，庶幾一倡三嘆者矣。
同考試官教諭張批：簡嚴，得商頌體。
考試官學正馮批：典重不浮。
考試官學正劉批：雅蔚。
詩人言商王作樂以格先，而因詳其樂聲之美也。夫惟樂可以感神也，商王有焉，其知盡祭之義者歟？此祀成湯之樂也。蓋曰：通幽明之感者存乎祭，重神明之交者存乎樂。我湯孫之祭也，
translation_en:
…people. Since Hou Ji, the Zhou had sought to perpetuate virtue through successive generations, never allowing their inherited undertaking to lapse. Thus they enjoyed an enduring heavenly mandate: their allotted fortune responded according to their kind [?]. Could this have been merely a matter of songs sung for a time during King Wen’s reign? That the Odes enable us to observe is made still more credible by this.
“ Tang’s descendant approaches in worship, bringing peace through the fulfillment of our thoughts. The hand drums and drums resound deeply; the pipes sound clear and high. Harmonious and balanced, they accord with our sounding stones. Ah, illustrious is Tang’s descendant; solemn is his music.”
Wang Ti
Comment by Associate Examiner Liao, Instructor: “He restrains ornament and attends to substance, yet the meaning has a lasting savor. He must be a man of cultivated character. Accept this piece.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor: “He locates the beauty of music in the harmony and balance of its sounds. This is quite right. His language and meaning ring out without becoming explicit, approaching the effect of ‘one singer leading and three responding.’”
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “Concise and austere; it captures the style of the Hymns of Shang.”
Comment by Examiner Feng, Instructor: “Classical and dignified, without superficiality.”
Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: “Elegant and rich.”
The poet speaks of the Shang king performing music to bring his ancestors into his presence, and accordingly describes in detail the beauty of its sounds. Music alone can move the spirits, and the Shang king possessed this power. Was he not one who understood fully the meaning of sacrifice? This is the music used in sacrificing to Cheng Tang. Its purport is this: communication between the unseen and visible realms rests in sacrifice; honoring intercourse with the spirits rests in music. At the sacrifice offered by our descendant of Tang…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
旣奏鼓而衎烈祖於迎牲之始矣其方祭之時
也何如哉以祖考不可以徒格也當臭味旣成
而樂奏焉于以舒致愨之義者於是矣斯感通
不難於禋祀也方聲音滌蕩而神享焉所以豫
思成之積者克綏矣夫作樂以格神而樂有弗
諧不可以言美也今則作之堂下者有鞉鼓與
管焉作之堂上者有磬焉眾音迭陳鞉鼓淵淵
而深遠也管聲嘒嘒而清亮也以拊以吹咸優
游而呈其盛律吕相宣和焉而不流於怗懘也
===
平焉而不至於趨數也高下疾徐與玉磬而同
其聲難協者眾聲也而條理不亂難依者磬聲
也而大小克諧由是播是音也爲顒若之孚而
寬仁彰信之治充滿於清明廣大之間者殆彷
彿而可想矣作是樂也爲祖考之薦而制心制
事之德洋溢於終始周旋之際者殆依稀而可
聽矣此於赫之湯孫也厥聲有不穆穆其美矣
乎噫樂之作也旣以感乎神神之格也由克盛
其樂此商人之重祭而尚聲也乎抑祭也者先
punctuated: 旣奏鼓而衎烈祖於迎牲之始矣，其方祭之時也何如哉？以祖考不可以徒格也，當臭味旣成而樂奏焉，于以舒致愨之義者於是矣。斯感通不難於禋祀也，方聲音滌蕩而神享焉，所以豫思成之積者克綏矣。夫作樂以格神，而樂有弗諧，不可以言美也。今則作之堂下者，有鞉鼓與管焉；作之堂上者，有磬焉。眾音迭陳，鞉鼓淵淵而深遠也，管聲嘒嘒而清亮也。以拊以吹，咸優游而呈其盛。律吕相宣，和焉而不流於怗懘也，平焉而不至於趨數也。高下疾徐，與玉磬而同其聲。難協者眾聲也，而條理不亂；難依者磬聲也，而大小克諧。由是播是音也，爲顒若之孚，而寬仁彰信之治充滿於清明廣大之間者，殆彷彿而可想矣。作是樂也，爲祖考之薦，而制心制事之德洋溢於終始周旋之際者，殆依稀而可聽矣。此於赫之湯孫也，厥聲有不穆穆其美矣乎？噫！樂之作也，旣以感乎神；神之格也，由克盛其樂。此商人之重祭而尚聲也乎？抑祭也者，先
translation_en:
…He has already sounded the drums to gladden the illustrious ancestor at the outset, when the sacrificial animal is brought in. What, then, happens during the sacrifice itself? Since the ancestors cannot merely be summoned without further observance, once the aromas and flavors of the offerings are ready, music is performed. Through this, the meaning of offering utmost sincerity is fully expressed. Thus communion with the spirits is not difficult in the pure sacrifice. As the sounds of music wash through the gathering and the spirits partake of the offerings, the thoughts accumulated beforehand in bringing the ancestors to mind can find repose.

Now, when music is made to summon the spirits, if it contains discord, it cannot be called beautiful. Here, however, below the hall there are pellet drums and pipes, while above the hall there are chime stones. The many sounds unfold in succession: the pellet drums resound deeply and far, and the pipes sound clear and bright. Whether struck or blown, all unfold with unhurried ease and display their fullness. The pitch standards complement one another: harmonious, they do not lapse into discord; even, they do not become hurried and overly rapid. High and low, fast and slow, their sounds accord with the jade chime stones. The many sounds are difficult to coordinate, yet their order remains undisturbed; the sound of the chime stones is difficult to follow, yet loud and soft achieve harmony.

Thus, when these sounds are spread abroad, they embody reverent sincerity. A government marked by generosity, benevolence, manifest virtue, and trustworthiness, filling a realm of clarity and breadth, can almost be dimly imagined. When this music is made, it constitutes an offering to the ancestors. The virtue that governs the heart and regulates affairs, overflowing through every movement from beginning to end, can almost be faintly heard. Such is the resplendent descendant of Tang! Could his music fail to possess a solemn and reverent beauty?

Ah! Music is performed to move the spirits; the spirits come because the music has been brought to fullness. Is this why the people of Shang attached such importance to sacrifice and esteemed sound? Yet sacrifice is what the former…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
王所以報本而反始義至重也商人尚聲固重
祭也而温恭有恪傳恭之遠寔有以將之耳使
其不然而徒致飾於鏞鼓管磬焉抑末矣是故
無聲之樂樂之本也綴兆節奏樂之末也辨於
此而後可以語祭矣
春秋
晉荀吳帥師敗狄于大鹵昭公元年
陳錫
同考試官教諭吳批毀車崇卒是荀吳變古
===
法之失處此作能言之而又宥斷制可嘉
考試官學正馮批明白正大
考試官學正劉批純暢
春秋於霸臣之攘夷而譏其取勝之非道也蓋
王者之師以全取勝者也荀吳之敗敵昧於是
矣其能免於春秋之譏歟且太原地在禹服之
内嘗聞宣王薄伐六月以爲功矣今之大鹵固
昔之太原也而狄人門庭之寇不猶昔之玁狁
乎荀吳帥師禦之正合膺懲之義使能以道制
punctuated:
王所以報本而反始，義至重也。商人尚聲，固重祭也，而温恭有恪，傳恭之遠，寔有以將之耳。使其不然而徒致飾於鏞鼓管磬焉，抑末矣。是故無聲之樂，樂之本也；綴兆節奏，樂之末也。辨於此，而後可以語祭矣。
春秋
晉荀吳帥師敗狄于大鹵。昭公元年。
陳錫
同考試官教諭吳批：「毀車崇卒，是荀吳變古法之失處。此作能言之，而又宥斷制，可嘉。」
考試官學正馮批：「明白正大。」
考試官學正劉批：「純暢。」
春秋於霸臣之攘夷，而譏其取勝之非道也。蓋王者之師，以全取勝者也。荀吳之敗敵，昧於是矣，其能免於春秋之譏歟？且太原地在禹服之内，嘗聞宣王薄伐，六月以爲功矣。今之大鹵，固昔之太原也，而狄人門庭之寇，不猶昔之玁狁乎？荀吳帥師禦之，正合膺懲之義，使能以道制
translation_en:
…the kings’ means of repaying their origins and returning to their beginnings: its significance is supremely weighty. In esteeming sound, the people of Shang certainly attached great importance to sacrifice; yet it was their gentle reverence and respectful care, extending reverence far, that truly sustained it. Had this not been so, and had they merely lavished embellishment on great bells, drums, pipes, and chime stones, they would have attended only to peripheral matters. Thus, music without sound is the root of music; the positions of the dancers and the measured rhythms are its peripheral aspects. Only after distinguishing these can one discuss sacrifice.
Spring and Autumn Annals
“Xun Wu of Jin led an army and defeated the Di at Dalu.” First year of Duke Zhao.
Chen Xi
Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor, comments: “Discarding chariots and giving precedence to infantry was where Xun Wu erred in altering the ancient methods. This composition succeeds in explaining this and also exercises discernment [?]. It deserves commendation.”
Examiner Feng, School Director, comments: “Clear, upright, and proper.”
Examiner Liu, School Director, comments: “Pure and fluent.”
When the Spring and Autumn Annals records a hegemon’s minister repelling the barbarians, it censures his use of improper means to achieve victory. For the army of a true king wins victory while preserving things intact. In defeating the enemy, Xun Wu failed to understand this. Could he escape the censure of the Spring and Autumn Annals? Moreover, Taiyuan lay within the territories ordered by Yu. We have heard how King Xuan marched against the enemy and how the ode ‘Sixth Month’ celebrated his achievement. The Dalu of this occasion was indeed the Taiyuan of old. Were not the Di, invading to the very gates, like the Xianyun of former times? Xun Wu’s leading an army to resist them accorded precisely with the principle of chastising offenders. If only he could have secured victory through the proper Way …

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
勝庶幾王者之師矣廼誤聽魏舒之言罔繼吉
甫之烈毀車而徒寧徇嬖以求其法之必行舍
正而譎甘作俑以求其敵之必勝五乘以爲伍
爲五陳以相離焉將謂以什當一可以阨險也
曾何思革車虎賁甲士恭命孰非王者車戰之
法而可以輕毀耶多方以誘之未陳而薄之將
謂以詐爲奇可以襲取也曾何思止齊不愆鼓
陳而戰孰非王者用兵之法而可以他尚耶車
法毀而苟簡之習啓知徼一時之利而不知古
===
制之遂不可復矣變詐興而傾危之俗成知取
目前之捷而不知末流之漸不可制矣聖人以
爲帝王之馭夷狄非制勝之患而惟以道之難
荀吳之敗狄誠是而所以敗之之道則非也故
書敗狄譏之者以此不然均之北伐均之太原
六月也而何今昔功過之不倫若此耶抑此知
聖人之慮遠矣先王古法不容輕易故車戰法
亡天下無全勝之師中國長技晁錯之所爲惜
也井田壞於商鞅封建廢於李斯車戰毀於荀
punctuated: 勝，庶幾王者之師矣。廼誤聽魏舒之言，罔繼吉甫之烈。毀車而徒，寧徇嬖以求其法之必行；舍正而譎，甘作俑以求其敵之必勝。五乘以爲伍，爲五陳以相離焉，將謂以什當一，可以阨險也。曾何思革車虎賁，甲士恭命，孰非王者車戰之法，而可以輕毀耶？多方以誘之，未陳而薄之，將謂以詐爲奇，可以襲取也。曾何思止齊不愆，鼓陳而戰，孰非王者用兵之法，而可以他尚耶？車法毀而苟簡之習啓，知徼一時之利，而不知古制之遂不可復矣。變詐興而傾危之俗成，知取目前之捷，而不知末流之漸不可制矣。聖人以爲帝王之馭夷狄，非制勝之患，而惟以道之難。荀吳之敗狄誠是，而所以敗之之道則非也。故書敗狄，譏之者以此。不然，均之北伐，均之太原，《六月》也，而何今昔功過之不倫若此耶？抑此知聖人之慮遠矣。先王古法不容輕易，故車戰法亡，天下無全勝之師。中國長技，晁錯之所爲惜也。井田壞於商鞅，封建廢於李斯，車戰毀於荀
translation_en:
…victory, his army might have approached the standard of a true king’s army. Instead, he mistakenly heeded Wei Shu’s words and failed to carry on Jifu’s glorious achievements. He destroyed the chariots and made the men fight on foot, willing even to execute a favorite as a warning to ensure that his method was implemented. He abandoned upright methods for deception, willingly setting a pernicious precedent to ensure victory over his enemy. He organized five chariots into a unit and formed five separate battle arrays, supposing that pitting ten against one would enable him to operate in narrow, difficult terrain. But did he ever consider the war chariots, the fierce warriors, and the armored soldiers reverently obeying commands? Were these not all elements of a true king’s methods of chariot warfare? How could they lightly be destroyed? He used numerous devices to lure the enemy and pressed the attack before they had formed their ranks, supposing that deception used as an unconventional tactic would enable him to seize victory by surprise. But did he ever consider halting in orderly ranks without error, beating the drums, and fighting in battle formation? Were these not all elements of a true king’s methods of warfare? How could other methods be preferred?

Once the methods of chariot warfare were destroyed, habits of careless expediency arose. He knew how to seek an immediate advantage but did not realize that the ancient institutions would thereafter become impossible to restore. Once deceit and trickery flourished, treacherous customs took shape. He knew how to secure a victory before his eyes but did not realize that the gradual spread of the resulting abuses would become impossible to control. The Sage held that, when emperors and kings bring the Yi and Di peoples under control, securing victory is not the difficulty; the difficulty lies in doing so according to the Way. Xun Wu was indeed right to defeat the Di, but the means by which he defeated them were wrong. This is why the record’s statement that he “defeated the Di” conveys criticism. Otherwise, both campaigns were northern expeditions, and both took place at Taiyuan—the setting of “The Sixth Month”—so why should the merits and faults of the earlier and later campaigns differ so greatly? From this we recognize how far ahead the Sage thought.

The ancient methods of the former kings must not be lightly altered. Thus, once the methods of chariot warfare disappeared, no army under Heaven could achieve complete victory. This was the superior military skill of the Central States whose loss Chao Cuo lamented. The well-field system was ruined by Shang Yang; the system of enfeoffment was abolished by Li Si; chariot warfare was destroyed by Xun…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
矣使先王成法不復見於後世皆功利欺詐之
徒爲之也考經所書然後知聖人垂訓之大而
慮患之遠矣
夏公會齊侯于夾谷公至自夾谷齊人
來歸鄆讙龜陰田俱定公十年
潘季馴
同考試官教諭吳批三田之歸孔子攝相見
諸行事之實此篇斷案明白蓋嘗究心於魯史者
考試官學正馮批婉而成章
===
考試官學正劉批明粹
春秋序望國化强之績亦惟以禮綏之而已是
可見夾谷會而侵疆歸綏之斯來也禮之感人
有如此夫惟時魯定會齊孔子相事君也能庸
夫執禮之臣臣也克承夫秉禮之緒以故始則
齊臣獻計會夾谷而亂之以兵繼則齊君悔過
歸三田而謝之以質焉聖人序其事若曰玆役
也齊來格而我底績夫非用禮之效歟彼神人
德義禮之大者夫人所固有也舉而詔之不有
punctuated:
矣。使先王成法不復見於後世，皆功利欺詐之徒爲之也。考經所書，然後知聖人垂訓之大，而慮患之遠矣。
夏，公會齊侯于夾谷。公至自夾谷。齊人來歸鄆、讙、龜陰田。俱定公十年。
潘季馴
同考試官教諭吳批：「三田之歸，孔子攝相，見諸行事之實。此篇斷案明白，蓋嘗究心於魯史者。」
考試官學正馮批：「婉而成章。」
考試官學正劉批：「明粹。」
《春秋》序望國化强之績，亦惟以禮綏之而已。是可見夾谷會而侵疆歸，綏之斯來也。禮之感人有如此！夫惟時魯定會齊，孔子相事，君也能庸夫執禮之臣，臣也克承夫秉禮之緒。以故始則齊臣獻計，會夾谷而亂之以兵；繼則齊君悔過，歸三田而謝之以質焉。聖人序其事，若曰：「玆役也，齊來格而我底績，夫非用禮之效歟？」彼神人德義，禮之大者，夫人所固有也。舉而詔之，不有
translation_en:
… so it was. That the established institutions of the former kings were no longer seen in later ages was entirely the work of men devoted to profit and advantage, deception and fraud. Only after examining what the Classic records can one understand the greatness of the Sage’s teachings for posterity and the reach of his foresight concerning future troubles.
“In summer, the duke met the Marquis of Qi at Jiagu. The duke returned from Jiagu. The men of Qi came to return the lands of Yun, Huan, and Guiyin.” All these entries belong to the tenth year of Duke Ding.
Pan Jixun.
Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: “The return of the three tracts of land provides concrete evidence, in actual deeds, of Confucius’s service as acting chief minister. This essay’s judgment is clear; its author has evidently studied the history of Lu attentively.”
Comment by Examiner Feng, Director of Studies: “Graceful and well composed.”
Comment by Examiner Liu, Director of Studies: “Clear and refined.”
The Spring and Autumn Annals recounts the achievement of a prestigious state in transforming a powerful one [?]; this was accomplished simply by pacifying it through ritual propriety. Thus we see that, after the meeting at Jiagu, the encroached-upon territory was returned: pacify them, and they will come. Such is the power of ritual propriety to move people!
At that time, Duke Ding of Lu met the ruler of Qi, and Confucius assisted in conducting the proceedings. The ruler could employ a minister who upheld ritual propriety, and the minister could carry forward the undertaking of adhering to it. Thus, at first, a minister of Qi offered a plan to disrupt the meeting at Jiagu with armed force; subsequently, the ruler of Qi repented of his wrongdoing, returned the three tracts of land, and thereby offered a tangible apology. In recounting these events, the Sage seems to say: “In this undertaking, Qi came into accord with us, and we achieved our purpose. Was this not the effect of employing ritual propriety?”
As for the spirits and human beings, virtue and righteousness [?]—these are the great concerns of ritual propriety, inherently possessed by everyone. If one brings them forward and instructs people in them, would there not be …

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
以啓其良乎裔俘干偪禮之悖者夫人所同惡
也舉而折之不有以格其非乎由是歷階旣對
會好成而我公飲至焉蓋犁彌計沮而優施無
庸其侮也饗禮旣罷鄆讙來而我疆盡復焉蓋
景公悔過而晏嬰自獻其誠也一言而威重于
三軍非幸也順於理也否則齊固强者豈其歡
然納地于魯耶噫斯理也舉而措之將正是四
國而奚有于一齊也三邑而恢復於俄頃非强
也感於禮也否則魯亦危矣豈其肆然得地于
===
齊耶噫斯禮也守而弗失將其爲東周而奚有
于三邑也故聖人于夾谷公至之下書曰齊人
來歸鄆讙龜陰田比於屈完之來而異於濟西
讙闡之歸焉者蓋曰齊人心服而來歸我君用
禮而綏之之績也乃若自序不嫌則以見人物
一身古今一息聖人蓋以天自處也而何避乎
雖然夾谷之績誠偉矣聲色猶存也夫子而得
邦家以及朞月則文武之政具舉而羔豚不飾
男女有別之化無遠弗屆矧乎齊也奚啻幡然
punctuated: 以啓其良乎？裔俘干偪，禮之悖者，夫人所同惡也，舉而折之，不有以格其非乎？由是歷階旣對，會好成而我公飲至焉，蓋犁彌計沮而優施無庸其侮也；饗禮旣罷，鄆讙來而我疆盡復焉，蓋景公悔過而晏嬰自獻其誠也。一言而威重于三軍，非幸也，順於理也。否則，齊固强者，豈其歡然納地于魯耶？噫！斯理也，舉而措之，將正是四國，而奚有于一齊也？三邑而恢復於俄頃，非强也，感於禮也。否則，魯亦危矣，豈其肆然得地于齊耶？噫！斯禮也，守而弗失，將其爲東周，而奚有于三邑也？故聖人于夾谷公至之下書曰：「齊人來歸鄆讙龜陰田。」比於屈完之來，而異於濟西、讙闡之歸焉者，蓋曰齊人心服而來歸，我君用禮而綏之之績也。乃若自序不嫌，則以見人物一身，古今一息，聖人蓋以天自處也，而何避乎？雖然，夾谷之績誠偉矣，聲色猶存也。夫子而得邦家以及朞月，則文武之政具舉，而羔豚不飾、男女有別之化，無遠弗屆，矧乎齊也，奚啻幡然
translation_en:
…thereby awaken their goodness? Foreign captives threatening with weapons [?] violate ritual propriety: this is something everyone alike detests. By confronting and checking it, could one not correct their wrongdoing? Thus, once Confucius had mounted the steps and delivered his reply, amicable relations were established at the meeting, and our duke returned to celebrate with the homecoming drinking ceremony. Li Mi’s scheme had been thwarted, and the entertainer You Shi [?] had no opportunity to inflict his insults. Once the ceremonial entertainment had been called off, Yun and Huan were returned, and our territory was fully restored. Duke Jing had repented of his fault, and Yan Ying had himself demonstrated his sincerity.

That a single utterance should carry greater authority than the Three Armies was no stroke of luck: it accorded with principle. Otherwise, since Qi was certainly powerful, would it have willingly surrendered territory to Lu? Ah! Put this principle into practice, and one could rectify the states of all four quarters; what difficulty would a single Qi present? That three towns were recovered in an instant was not achieved through force: it was the transforming influence of ritual propriety. Otherwise, Lu itself was in peril; could it have obtained territory from Qi so freely? Ah! Uphold this ritual propriety without losing it, and one could create an Eastern Zhou; what would a mere three towns amount to?

Thus, beneath the entry recording the duke’s return from Jiagu, the Sage wrote: “The men of Qi came and returned the lands of Yun, Huan, and Guiyin.” He treated this as comparable to Qu Wan’s coming, but different from the returns of Jixi and of Huan and Chan. The implication is that the men of Qi submitted in their hearts and came to return the lands: this was the achievement of our ruler’s use of ritual propriety to bring them to peace. As for the Sage’s freely recording his own deeds, this shows that people and things form a single body, and past and present share a single breath. The Sage took Heaven as his own standpoint; what, then, need he avoid?

Nevertheless, great indeed as the achievement at Jiagu was, it still involved the force of voice and countenance. Had the Master obtained a state to govern for a full year, the government of Kings Wen and Wu would have been fully instituted. The transforming influence under which lambs and piglets were not deceptively presented for sale [?], and men and women maintained their distinctions, would have reached even the remotest places—how much more so Qi! It would have gone far beyond a sudden…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
悔悟而歸我以三田抑亦翕然丕變而不忍歸
我以女樂矣若之何得政日淺厥施未究兆足
以行而不能三年淹也豈其天之未定而不能
違歟尚賴春秋作而爲國以禮之訓昭焉又聖
人之所以定乎天也
禮記
樂正崇四術立四教順先王詩書禮樂以
造士春秋教以禮樂冬夏教以詩書
邵型
===
同考試官教諭倪批先王教人之意體認眞
切宜錄以式
考試官學正馮批文詞充贍
考試官學正劉批通暢
大臣造士之法取諸古而時其教焉夫詩書禮
樂古之道也大臣脩此以爲時教焉其曲成之
心何至哉昔者先王患士之無教也而羣之太
學焉患教之不刑也而立之樂正焉嘗稽樂正
之教而知其作人之善矣是故士之業於國學
punctuated:
悔悟而歸我以三田，抑亦翕然丕變而不忍歸我以女樂矣。若之何得政日淺，厥施未究，兆足以行而不能三年淹也？豈其天之未定而不能違歟？尚賴《春秋》作，而爲國以禮之訓昭焉，又聖人之所以定乎天也。

禮記
樂正崇四術，立四教，順先王詩書禮樂以造士，春秋教以禮樂，冬夏教以詩書。
邵型

同考試官教諭倪批：先王教人之意，體認眞切，宜錄以式。
考試官學正馮批：文詞充贍。
考試官學正劉批：通暢。

大臣造士之法，取諸古而時其教焉。夫詩書禮樂，古之道也。大臣脩此以爲時教焉，其曲成之心何至哉！昔者先王患士之無教也，而羣之太學焉；患教之不刑也，而立之樂正焉。嘗稽樂正之教，而知其作人之善矣。是故士之業於國學
translation_en:
…repent and return the three tracts of land to us; indeed, they would also undergo a wholehearted and profound transformation and could not bear to send us female musicians. Why, then, was his time in office so brief, his measures not fully carried out? The signs were sufficient for putting his way into practice [?], yet he could not remain for three years. Was it because Heaven’s disposition was not yet settled, and he could not go against it? Fortunately, the Spring and Autumn Annals was composed, making manifest the teaching that a state should be governed through ritual propriety. This, too, was how the Sage gave settled expression to Heaven’s purpose.

Record of Rites
“The Director of Music exalts the four disciplines and establishes the four branches of instruction. Following the former kings’ Poetry, Documents, rites, and music, he trains scholars. In spring and autumn he teaches rites and music; in winter and summer he teaches Poetry and Documents.”
Shao Xing

Comment by Associate Examiner Ni, Instructor: “His understanding of the former kings’ intention in educating people is true and penetrating. This should be recorded as a model.”
Comment by Examiner Feng, Schoolmaster: “The language is ample and rich.”
Comment by Examiner Liu, Schoolmaster: “Clear and fluent.”

The method by which a great minister trains scholars is drawn from antiquity, while his instruction accords with the seasons. Poetry, Documents, rites, and music constitute the Way of antiquity. A great minister cultivates these to provide seasonal instruction. How consummate is his concern to bring each person to fulfillment! Formerly, the ancient kings worried that scholars lacked instruction, and therefore assembled them in the Imperial University. They worried that instruction lacked a model, and therefore appointed a Director of Music over them. Having examined the Director of Music’s teaching, I have come to understand his excellence in nurturing men of talent. Thus, as for scholars pursuing their studies in the state school…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
者莫不欲其成德也則莫不示以入德之路也
而術維四焉不有以崇之人將玩焉而弗從茲
必敬以敷之而昭之爲訓典者儼然示人以可
遵也莫不欲其由道也則莫不啓以脩道之方
也而教維四焉不有以立之人將怠焉而弗率
茲必舉以迪之而樹之爲標準者卓然示人以
可法也若此者豈樂正强爲之哉由先王始也
蓋詩書禮樂作之先王而垂之後世者也溫柔
敦厚取諸詩疏通知遠取諸書而所以章志貞
===
教者率乎舊章而不過恭儉莊敬取諸禮廣博
易良取諸樂而所以振民育德者監乎成憲而
不違自其立之而爲教者立乎此者也而何敢
以自用乎自其崇之而爲術者崇乎此者也而
何敢以反古乎由是順之而造士也仰法乎歲
序而非雜施以亂其心上律乎天時而非躐等
以誣其進時乎春秋而禮樂之教舉焉凡其詔
之儀章詔之音節者於此乎相授受也禮樂無
當於春秋而脩之爲正業者庶其習之專而無
punctuated: 者，莫不欲其成德也，則莫不示以入德之路也，而術維四焉。不有以崇之，人將玩焉而弗從。茲必敬以敷之，而昭之爲訓典者，儼然示人以可遵也。莫不欲其由道也，則莫不啓以脩道之方也，而教維四焉。不有以立之，人將怠焉而弗率。茲必舉以迪之，而樹之爲標準者，卓然示人以可法也。若此者，豈樂正强爲之哉？由先王始也。蓋詩書禮樂，作之先王而垂之後世者也。溫柔敦厚，取諸詩；疏通知遠，取諸書。而所以章志貞教者，率乎舊章而不過。恭儉莊敬，取諸禮；廣博易良，取諸樂。而所以振民育德者，監乎成憲而不違。自其立之而爲教者，立乎此者也，而何敢以自用乎？自其崇之而爲術者，崇乎此者也，而何敢以反古乎？由是順之而造士也，仰法乎歲序，而非雜施以亂其心；上律乎天時，而非躐等以誣其進。時乎春秋，而禮樂之教舉焉。凡其詔之儀章、詔之音節者，於此乎相授受也。禮樂無當於春秋，而脩之爲正業者，庶其習之專而無
translation_en:
…for those studying there, the aim is invariably that they perfect their virtue; thus they are invariably shown the path toward virtue, through four methods. Unless these are accorded due esteem, people will treat them lightly and fail to follow them. They must therefore be reverently expounded and clearly set forth as authoritative teachings, solemnly showing people what they may follow. The aim is invariably that they follow the Way; thus they are invariably instructed in how to cultivate it, through four teachings. Unless these are firmly established, people will grow remiss and fail to observe them. They must therefore be put forward as guides and established as standards, standing prominently before people as models to emulate. Could such arrangements have been arbitrarily devised by the Director of Music? They originated with the former kings.

Poetry, documents, rites, and music were created by the former kings and handed down to later generations. Gentleness and kindness, sincerity and generosity are drawn from the Book of Odes; breadth of understanding and knowledge of the distant past are drawn from the Book of Documents. The means by which aspirations are made manifest and teaching kept correct follow the old institutions without exceeding them. Respectfulness, frugality, dignity, and reverence are drawn from rites; breadth of understanding, an easy disposition, and goodness are drawn from music. The means by which the people are invigorated and virtue nurtured take established institutions as their model without departing from them. What is established as teaching rests upon these: how could one dare rely on one's own judgment? What is exalted as methods likewise rests upon these: how could one dare turn against antiquity?

Following these principles in forming scholars, they take the sequence of the seasons as their model, rather than imparting teachings indiscriminately and confusing students' minds. They conform above to Heaven's seasons, rather than skipping stages and giving a false appearance of progress. In spring and autumn, instruction in rites and music is undertaken. All instruction in ceremonial forms and musical rhythms is then imparted and received. Rites and music have no intrinsic correspondence with spring and autumn; the purpose of cultivating them as the regular course of study is to ensure that students concentrate on their practice and do not…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
廢學焉耳時乎冬夏而詩書之敎興焉凡其迪
之典謨迪之雅頌者於此乎相傳習也詩書無
當乎冬夏而率之爲時敎者庶其養之純而無
廢業焉耳是則立敎惟古則授之者有成法施
敎惟時則學之者有專功先王之世師道立而
善人多者其率用此歟吾于是而知先王之育
材典理非徒備官也而有本焉思齊之詩詠文
王之德詳矣而必以古之人無斁譽髦斯士終
焉則文王崇敎之心可以想見而其得人以隆
===
治化者固其所也雖然周之士非獨上之人養
之士亦知自養焉後世典敎之官作新之術非
不宛然成周品式而何有周之士不終覩耶噫
爲士者可以興矣
德者性之端也樂者德之華也
曹光
同考試官敎諭倪批理明意盡深達作樂之
本者
考試官學正馮批理致精到
punctuated:
廢學焉耳。時乎冬夏，而詩書之敎興焉。凡其迪之典謨、迪之雅頌者，於此乎相傳習也。詩書無當乎冬夏，而率之爲時敎者，庶其養之純而無廢業焉耳。是則立敎惟古，則授之者有成法；施敎惟時，則學之者有專功。先王之世，師道立而善人多者，其率用此歟？吾于是而知先王之育材典理，非徒備官也，而有本焉。《思齊》之詩詠文王之德詳矣，而必以「古之人無斁，譽髦斯士」終焉，則文王崇敎之心可以想見，而其得人以隆治化者，固其所也。雖然，周之士非獨上之人養之，士亦知自養焉。後世典敎之官、作新之術，非不宛然成周品式，而何有周之士不終覩耶？噫！爲士者可以興矣！

德者，性之端也；樂者，德之華也。
曹光
同考試官敎諭倪批：理明意盡，深達作樂之本者。
考試官學正馮批：理致精到。
translation_en:
…so that their studies would not fall into neglect. In winter and summer, instruction in the Odes and Documents flourished. All instruction guiding them through the Canons and Counsels, and through the Elegantiae and Hymns, was transmitted and practiced at these times. The Odes and Documents were not confined to winter and summer; following this arrangement as seasonal instruction was intended to make their cultivation wholehearted and prevent neglect of their work. Thus, when education was established according to antiquity, those who taught had established methods; when instruction was administered according to the seasons, those who learned could apply themselves with undivided effort. In the age of the former kings, the way of teachers was firmly established and good men were numerous: was this not because they generally followed these principles?

From this I understand that the former kings’ cultivation of talent and ordering of affairs [?] were not merely a matter of filling offices, but had a deeper foundation. The ode “Si Qi” (Emulating the Exemplary) praises King Wen’s virtue in detail, yet it must conclude with: “The men of old were tireless; they nurtured these outstanding scholars.” From this we can imagine King Wen’s devotion to education; that he obtained worthy men through whom to enhance good government and moral transformation was its natural result. Nevertheless, the scholars of Zhou were not merely cultivated by those above them: they also knew how to cultivate themselves. In later ages, the officials responsible for education and the methods for renewing its vigor certainly resembled the institutions of the established Zhou order. Why, then, have scholars like those of Zhou never been seen again [?]? Ah! Those who are scholars should bestir themselves!

“Virtue is the manifestation of human nature; music is the flowering of virtue.”

Cao Guang

Comment by Associate Examiner Ni, Instructor: “The principles are clear and the meaning fully expressed. This is someone who profoundly understands the foundation of making music.”

Comment by Examiner Feng, Instructor: “The reasoning is refined and thoroughly developed.”

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
考試官學正劉批古雅
記者原德之所由發而著其爲樂之本也夫樂
非自外至者也性發於德而樂以彰之茲其樂
之所自來者乎記者懼作樂者之忘其本也故
爲之言曰先王之立樂也非作而致其文也此
有由本也樂教行而可以觀德者亦以德爲樂
之本焉爾是故志和行成之謂德德顯於有而
性隱於無宜若不相管矣然有無雖分於二致
而體用實出於一原湛一之本素豫夫妙應之
===
機和順之休悉根於降衷之懿發而中者出之
至靜以洩其精妙用之顯行一全體之呈露也
用而和者本之太虛以呈其象至德之淵微一
性真之發越也要之性者德之藏諸用德者性
之顯諸仁其猶物在中而緒見於外者矣觀德
可以知性不曰性之端乎比物飾節之謂樂樂
滯於器而德凝於道宜若不相通矣然道器雖
判於殊塗而精粗則妙於一體懿德之富有自
涵夫聲氣之元至樂之昭宣實顯乎中和之積
punctuated:
考試官學正劉批：古雅。

記者原德之所由發，而著其爲樂之本也。夫樂非自外至者也，性發於德，而樂以彰之，茲其樂之所自來者乎！記者懼作樂者之忘其本也，故爲之言曰：「先王之立樂也，非作而致其文也，此有由本也。」樂教行而可以觀德者，亦以德爲樂之本焉爾。是故志和行成之謂德。德顯於有，而性隱於無，宜若不相管矣。然有無雖分於二致，而體用實出於一原。湛一之本，素豫夫妙應之機；和順之休，悉根於降衷之懿。發而中者，出之至靜以洩其精，妙用之顯行，一全體之呈露也；用而和者，本之太虛以呈其象，至德之淵微，一性真之發越也。要之，性者德之藏諸用，德者性之顯諸仁，其猶物在中而緒見於外者矣。觀德可以知性，不曰性之端乎？比物飾節之謂樂。樂滯於器，而德凝於道，宜若不相通矣。然道器雖判於殊塗，而精粗則妙於一體。懿德之富有，自涵夫聲氣之元；至樂之昭宣，實顯乎中和之積。
translation_en:
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: “Classical and elegant.”

The author of the Record traces the source from which virtue emerges and makes clear that virtue is the foundation of music. Music does not come from outside us. Our nature manifests itself in virtue, and music gives it expression: is this not the source from which music comes? Fearing that those who made music would forget its foundation, the author therefore said: “When the former kings established music, they did not merely fashion its outward embellishments; it had a source and foundation.” That virtue can be discerned when musical education is put into practice likewise follows simply from virtue’s being the foundation of music. Thus, harmony of purpose and completeness of conduct are called virtue. Virtue manifests itself in what has being, while human nature lies hidden in what has none; they might therefore seem unrelated. Yet although being and nonbeing are distinguished as two aspects, substance and function in fact issue from a single source. The foundation of serene unity inherently contains the capacity for wondrous response; the excellence of harmony and accord is entirely rooted in the goodness of the inner nature bestowed by Heaven. What issues forth and attains due measure emerges from perfect stillness to release its essence: the manifest operation of its wondrous functioning is the disclosure of one complete substance. What functions harmoniously takes the Great Void as its foundation in order to present its forms: the profound subtlety of consummate virtue is the unfolding of the true nature itself. In essence, human nature is virtue concealed in functioning, and virtue is human nature manifested in benevolence. It is like something lying within whose traces appear outside. By observing virtue, one can know human nature. Is virtue not, then, the outward indication of that nature? Bringing things into accord and embellishing their rhythms is called music. Music is lodged in concrete instruments, while virtue is concentrated in the Way; they might therefore seem unconnected. Yet although the Way and concrete instruments are distinguished as separate paths, the subtle and the gross are wondrously united in a single substance. The abundance of excellent virtue naturally contains the wellspring of sound and vital energy; the resplendent expression of consummate music truly makes manifest the accumulated riches of equilibrium and harmony…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
越之聲音以樂其象由之無聲者以奮其光八
音之克諧一德音之播比也形之動靜以治其
飾由之不顯者以發其蘊萬舞之有奕一德輝
之流動也要之盛德寓大樂于無形大樂闡盛
德于有象殆有誠於中而必形于外者矣聞樂
可以知德不曰德之華乎是則德非外鑠性其
本也樂非強作德其本也不能盡性猶難語德
不能成德猶難語樂察于此者樂其可作也巳
嘗聞樂也者和也和也者性之德也求端于和
===
而樂不外是矣觀后夔典樂之教惟本之和德
而不拘拘於戛擊搏拊之間卒之和神人而舞
百獸者胥此焉出則可以知古人作樂之方矣
後世桑間濮上之音七德九功之舞非不侈其
聲容吾不知其德性為何如也廣樂以成教者
盍亦審所尚乎
第貳塲
論
合虛與氣有性之名
punctuated:
越之聲音，以樂其象；由之無聲者，以奮其光。八音之克諧，一德音之播比也。形之動靜，以治其飾；由之不顯者，以發其蘊。萬舞之有奕，一德輝之流動也。要之，盛德寓大樂于無形，大樂闡盛德于有象，殆有誠於中而必形于外者矣。聞樂可以知德，不曰德之華乎？是則德非外鑠，性其本也；樂非強作，德其本也。不能盡性，猶難語德；不能成德，猶難語樂。察于此者，樂其可作也巳。嘗聞樂也者，和也；和也者，性之德也。求端于和，而樂不外是矣。觀后夔典樂之教，惟本之和德，而不拘拘於戛擊搏拊之間。卒之和神人而舞百獸者，胥此焉出，則可以知古人作樂之方矣。後世桑間濮上之音、七德九功之舞，非不侈其聲容，吾不知其德性為何如也。廣樂以成教者，盍亦審所尚乎？
第貳塲
論
合虛與氣，有性之名。
translation_en:
…It issues forth in sounds to give musical expression to its forms; proceeding from what is soundless, it brings forth its radiance. The harmony of the eight classes of instruments is wholly the spreading and blending of virtue’s tones. It takes form in movement and stillness to regulate its adornment; proceeding from what is unseen, it discloses what lies within. The splendor of the myriad dances is wholly the flowing radiance of virtue. In essence, abundant virtue contains great music within the formless, while great music manifests abundant virtue in perceptible forms. Surely, what is genuine within must take form without. By hearing music one can know virtue: is this not what is meant by calling music the flowering of virtue?
Thus virtue is not infused from outside: human nature is its root. Music is not forcibly contrived: virtue is its root. Without fully realizing one’s nature, it is still difficult to speak of virtue; without perfecting virtue, it is still difficult to speak of music. One who understands this can indeed create music. I have heard that music is harmony, and harmony is the virtue of human nature. Seek its beginnings in harmony, and music lies nowhere beyond this.
Consider Hou Kui’s teaching as Director of Music. He grounded it solely in harmonious virtue and did not confine himself to scraping, striking, beating, and tapping instruments. That he ultimately brought spirits and humans into harmony and made the hundred beasts dance all issued from this. Here we can understand the ancients’ method of creating music. As for later ages’ music of Sangjian and Pushang, and their dances of the Seven Virtues and Nine Achievements, these were certainly lavish in sound and spectacle; yet I do not know what their virtue and nature were like. Should those who extend music to accomplish moral instruction not also scrutinize what they esteem?
Second Session
Discourse
Through the conjunction of the void and qi, there is what is called human nature.

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
周詩
同考試官教諭林批作此題者類乏體認此
作謂虛以凝氣氣以涵虛深得張子之旨而氣格
風骨直與兩漢文字齊驅佳士也錄之
考試官學正馮批脩詞爾雅析義精嚴賢
科得子可以稱慶矣
考試官學正劉批文瑩思深獨異諸作
甚哉理氣之不相離也知其所以合一之
妙斯可以言性矣夫理者非離氣而立者
===
也大虛無形氣之本體萬殊之所以一本
也氣者非脫然於是理之外者也其聚其
散流行於大虛之中一本之所以萬殊也
故虛非氣則無所附麗而造化之用息氣
非虛則無所主宰而造化之體毀矣又何
以生人物之萬殊而賦之以性者哉夫惟
虛以凝氣氣以涵虛則造化行而性於是
乎立矣非天下之至妙者乎張子曰合虛
與氣有性之名甚哉張子之善言性也昔
punctuated:
周詩

同考試官教諭林批：作此題者，類乏體認。此作謂虛以凝氣，氣以涵虛，深得張子之旨，而氣格風骨直與兩漢文字齊驅。佳士也，錄之。

考試官學正馮批：脩詞爾雅，析義精嚴。賢科得子，可以稱慶矣。

考試官學正劉批：文瑩思深，獨異諸作。

甚哉，理氣之不相離也！知其所以合一之妙，斯可以言性矣。夫理者，非離氣而立者也。大虛無形，氣之本體，萬殊之所以一本也。氣者，非脫然於是理之外者也。其聚其散，流行於大虛之中，一本之所以萬殊也。故虛非氣，則無所附麗，而造化之用息；氣非虛，則無所主宰，而造化之體毀矣。又何以生人物之萬殊，而賦之以性者哉？夫惟虛以凝氣，氣以涵虛，則造化行，而性於是乎立矣。非天下之至妙者乎？張子曰：「合虛與氣，有性之名。」甚哉，張子之善言性也！昔
translation_en:
Zhou Shi

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: Those who write on this topic generally lack experiential understanding. This essay states that the void serves to concentrate material force (qi), while material force embraces the void, thereby grasping Master Zhang’s meaning profoundly. Its bearing and vigor rank alongside the writings of the two Han dynasties. A fine scholar: admit him.

Comment by Examiner Feng, Instructor: The diction is refined and elegant, and the analysis of meaning precise and rigorous. That this examination has gained a man of your worth is cause for celebration.

Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: The writing is luminous and the thought profound, standing apart from all the other essays.

How utterly inseparable principle (li) and material force are! Only when one understands the subtle way in which they unite as one can one speak of human nature. Principle does not stand apart from material force. The Great Void is formless: it is the fundamental substance of material force, through which the myriad differences have a single root. Material force, in turn, does not exist independently outside this principle. Gathering and dispersing, it circulates within the Great Void: this is how the single root gives rise to myriad differences. Thus, without material force, the void would have nothing to adhere to, and the workings of creation and transformation would cease; without the void, material force would have nothing to govern it, and the substance of creation and transformation would be destroyed. How, then, could it generate the myriad varieties of people and things and endow them with their natures? Only because the void serves to concentrate material force, and material force embraces the void, do creation and transformation proceed and nature thereby become established. Is this not the utmost subtlety under Heaven? Master Zhang said: “Through the union of the void and material force, there is what is called nature.” How well Master Zhang spoke of nature! In former times…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
者聖賢言性至明且切也而孰有辨於易
乎自夫子係易而首發於乾之彖曰各正
性命保合大和夫曰各正則固以理言之
矣而大和之保合者實有以涵畜之則大
虛之理氣化之道其所以妙合而凝者不
可以求端於天耶今夫於穆不已天之所
以為天也曷為以虛言之也蓋天覆於上
块然一氣而已而理之所主至空而明冲
漠無朕雖其流形萬品莫不取足於天之
===
氣而天之所以為天者卒未甞囿於其氣
而氣之本體固自若也夫安得而不謂之
虛至於氣之聚散為寒暑晝夜為雨露霜
雪為山川木石為金水火土皆變化之客
形而陰陽之精未甞不根柢於大虛但氣
有形虛無迹而理之虛者於氣之實者見
之犂然而陳雜然而出是不可以觀道之
所在矣乎以虛為天以理言之謂之天也
以氣化為道以此理之運行非陰陽之二
punctuated: 者，聖賢言性，至明且切也，而孰有辨於《易》乎？自夫子係《易》，而首發於《乾》之彖曰：「各正性命，保合大和。」夫曰各正，則固以理言之矣；而大和之保合者，實有以涵畜之。則大虛之理、氣化之道，其所以妙合而凝者，不可以求端於天耶？今夫於穆不已，天之所以為天也，曷為以虛言之也？蓋天覆於上，块然一氣而已，而理之所主，至空而明，冲漠無朕。雖其流形萬品，莫不取足於天之氣，而天之所以為天者，卒未甞囿於其氣，而氣之本體固自若也。夫安得而不謂之虛？至於氣之聚散，為寒暑晝夜，為雨露霜雪，為山川木石，為金水火土，皆變化之客形，而陰陽之精，未甞不根柢於大虛。但氣有形，虛無迹，而理之虛者，於氣之實者見之，犂然而陳，雜然而出，是不可以觀道之所在矣乎？以虛為天，以理言之謂之天也；以氣化為道，以此理之運行，非陰陽之二
translation_en:
…the sages and worthies spoke of human nature with utmost clarity and precision, yet what offers greater discernment than the Book of Changes? When Confucius appended his explanations to the Changes, he first brought this out in the Commentary on the Judgment of Qian: “Each attains its proper nature and allotted destiny, preserving and uniting in supreme harmony.” The words “each attains its proper” certainly refer to principle; yet the preservation and union of supreme harmony truly provide the means to contain and nurture it. Thus, concerning the principle of the Great Void and the Way of the transformations of qi, may we not seek in Heaven the source of their wondrous union and consolidation?

Now, profound and unceasing activity is what makes Heaven Heaven. Why, then, speak of it in terms of the void? Heaven stretches above us, simply one undivided mass of qi [?]; yet the principle that governs it is utterly empty and luminous, silent and boundless, without a trace. Though its flowing activity gives form to the myriad kinds of things, all drawing their sufficiency from Heaven’s qi, what makes Heaven Heaven has never ultimately been confined within that qi, while the original constitution of qi remains as it is. How, then, could we fail to call it the void?

As for the gathering and dispersal of qi, these produce cold and heat, day and night, rain and dew, frost and snow, mountains and rivers, wood and stone, metal, water, fire, and earth. All are transient forms of transformation, while the vital essence of yin and yang has always been rooted in the Great Void. Qi has form, whereas the void leaves no trace; yet the emptiness of principle manifests itself in the substantiality of qi, distinctly arrayed and emerging in manifold variety. Can we not thereby observe where the Way resides? To identify the void with Heaven is to call it Heaven in terms of principle; to identify the transformations of qi with the Way is because the operation of this principle cannot dispense with the two …

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
端不可也則人物之性又豈外於虛氣之
合也哉自夫性之不明於天下也守空寂
之說者以爲虛即性也不知舉虛而遺氣
將病性於無矣梏於形體之小者以爲氣
即性也不知舉氣而遺虛將滯性於有矣
抑孰知虛氣之相乘固性之所以爲妙者
乎蓋大虛者此理之體指其未形言之也
氣化者此理之用指其未成言之也而虛
之與氣又何以知其合也蓋陰陽氣也形
===
而下者也所以一陰一陽者理也形而上
者也自理之方行而未有所立也使非附
麗於氣則大虛終歸於無物不足以立天
下之有而理之善者不可得而見矣然氣
之方出而未有所成也非大虛者爲之綱
維焉則絪縕雜揉亦將物而不化矣何以
繼善成性者耶自今言之天之生物也惟
人爲最靈其間有血氣知覺爲禽獸者有
無血氣知覺而有生意爲草木者有生意
punctuated: 端不可也，則人物之性又豈外於虛氣之合也哉？自夫性之不明於天下也，守空寂之說者以爲虛即性也，不知舉虛而遺氣，將病性於無矣；梏於形體之小者以爲氣即性也，不知舉氣而遺虛，將滯性於有矣。抑孰知虛氣之相乘，固性之所以爲妙者乎？蓋大虛者，此理之體，指其未形言之也；氣化者，此理之用，指其未成言之也。而虛之與氣，又何以知其合也？蓋陰陽，氣也，形而下者也；所以一陰一陽者，理也，形而上者也。自理之方行而未有所立也，使非附麗於氣，則大虛終歸於無物，不足以立天下之有，而理之善者不可得而見矣。然氣之方出而未有所成也，非大虛者爲之綱維焉，則絪縕雜揉，亦將物而不化矣，何以繼善成性者耶？自今言之，天之生物也，惟人爲最靈。其間有血氣知覺爲禽獸者，有無血氣知覺而有生意爲草木者，有生意
translation_en: …the two poles are indispensable. How, then, could the nature of human beings and other things lie outside the union of emptiness and qi? Ever since nature ceased to be clearly understood in the world, those who adhere to the doctrine of emptiness and stillness have taken emptiness itself to be nature. They do not realize that to uphold emptiness while leaving out qi is to impair their understanding of nature by reducing it to nonbeing. Those confined within the narrow bounds of bodily form take qi itself to be nature. They do not realize that to uphold qi while leaving out emptiness is to constrain nature within being. Yet who understands that the interplay of emptiness and qi is precisely what makes nature wondrous? The Great Void is the substance of this principle, spoken of before it takes form; the transformations of qi are the functioning of this principle, spoken of before it reaches completion. But how do we know that emptiness and qi unite? Yin and yang are qi and belong to what is below form; that by which there is now yin, now yang is principle and belongs to what is above form. When principle is beginning to operate but has not yet established anything, unless it attaches itself to qi, the Great Void will ultimately amount to nothing. It will be insufficient to establish the things that exist in the world, and the goodness of principle will remain invisible. Yet when qi is beginning to emerge but has not yet brought anything to completion, unless the Great Void provides its governing framework, its mingling and intermixing will merely produce things without transformation. How, then, could it continue goodness and complete nature? To speak of this in present terms: among the beings Heaven generates, human beings alone possess the greatest spiritual intelligence. Among these beings, those with blood, qi, and perception are birds and beasts; those without blood, qi, and perception but with vitality are plants and trees; there are those whose vitality…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
已絕而但有形質臭味為枯槁者雖分有
不同其剛柔之異稟屈伸之交禪呼吸升
降之不齊莫非性也而亦莫非氣也使有
氣焉而不本之於虛則氣滯於方而亦不
能自運矣夫惟以至虛之理而合之於氣
化之賾也則理以主氣氣以載理而性之
具於人物者隨所觸而皆應是故其在於
人也仁發為惻隱義發為羞惡禮發為恭
敬智發為是非氣為之也其所以為仁為
===
義為禮為智者其理本至虛也由是達之
於情為喜怒哀樂焉見之於事為視聽言
動思焉秩之於倫為親義序別信焉是皆
性之動也而莫非至虛之理也不然禽獸
至駁也而於君臣父子夫婦兄弟朋友亦
有各得其一曲之明者其孰使之耶又不
然草木至微也而植者自植天機自完其
孰使之耶又不然枯槁之物生意絕矣而
糟粕煨燼變化不窮其孰使之耶信乎理
punctuated: 已絕而但有形質臭味為枯槁者，雖分有不同，其剛柔之異稟、屈伸之交禪、呼吸升降之不齊，莫非性也，而亦莫非氣也。使有氣焉而不本之於虛，則氣滯於方，而亦不能自運矣。夫惟以至虛之理而合之於氣化之賾也，則理以主氣，氣以載理，而性之具於人物者，隨所觸而皆應。是故其在於人也，仁發為惻隱，義發為羞惡，禮發為恭敬，智發為是非，氣為之也。其所以為仁、為義、為禮、為智者，其理本至虛也。由是達之於情，為喜怒哀樂焉；見之於事，為視聽言動思焉；秩之於倫，為親義序別信焉。是皆性之動也，而莫非至虛之理也。不然，禽獸至駁也，而於君臣、父子、夫婦、兄弟、朋友，亦有各得其一曲之明者，其孰使之耶？又不然，草木至微也，而植者自植，天機自完，其孰使之耶？又不然，枯槁之物，生意絕矣，而糟粕煨燼，變化不窮，其孰使之耶？信乎理
translation_en: …has already ceased, leaving only physical form, substance, odor, and taste in withered things. Though their allotted endowments differ—their distinct endowments of hardness and softness, the alternation of contraction and expansion, and the unevenness of breathing, rising, and falling—all are manifestations of nature, and all are also manifestations of qi. If qi existed without being rooted in emptiness, it would become confined to a particular location and could not move of itself. Only when the principle of utmost emptiness is united with the profundities of transformation through qi does principle govern qi and qi bear principle, so that the nature inherent in people and things responds to whatever it encounters. Thus, in human beings, benevolence issues forth as compassion, righteousness as shame and aversion to wrong, ritual propriety as reverence and respect, and wisdom as discernment of right and wrong: qi brings this about. Yet what makes them benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom is their principle, which is fundamentally utmost emptiness. Extended into the emotions, this becomes joy, anger, sorrow, and pleasure; manifested in activities, it becomes seeing, hearing, speaking, acting, and thinking; ordered within human relationships, it becomes affection, righteousness, precedence, distinction, and trustworthiness. These are all movements of nature, and all embody the principle of utmost emptiness. Were this not so, birds and beasts, whose endowments are exceedingly mixed, nevertheless each possess some partial understanding of the relationships between ruler and minister, father and son, husband and wife, elder and younger brothers, and friends: what causes them to do so? Again, were this not so, plants and trees are exceedingly lowly, yet what grows takes root of itself, and its natural workings are complete in themselves: what causes this? Again, were this not so, the vitality of withered things has ceased, yet dregs and ashes undergo endless transformations: what causes this? Truly, principle…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之在天下無空缺不滿之處而隨氣流行
以成人物之性者未嘗止息辟則戸然性
其樞也虛則能闔能闢實有是理而不可
以形求者也氣則闔之闢之有迹可見而
日用不離者也知樞之所以爲樞不外於
闔闢之盡神則知性之所以爲性不外於
理氣之相乘矣理不可見是謂至靜無感
性之淵源一大虛無形氣之本體所自來
也其交感不齊而知識生焉是謂感而遂
===
通性之發見一聚散有形氣之變化所以
行也惟其主於虛是故天命之性一焉而
聖愚賢不肖之分與夫跂行蠕息之類無
有乎弗同無有乎弗具者理也惟其隨於
氣是故氣質之性殊焉而天下之偏者全
者清者濁者厚者薄者邪者正者始紛紛
雜出而不可禦矣是故純粹至善固性也
剛柔純駁亦性也立於無物之先固此性
也行於有物之後亦此性也妙矣哉性之
punctuated: 之在天下，無空缺不滿之處，而隨氣流行以成人物之性者，未嘗止息。辟則戸然，性其樞也。虛則能闔能闢，實有是理而不可以形求者也；氣則闔之闢之，有迹可見而日用不離者也。知樞之所以爲樞，不外於闔闢之盡神，則知性之所以爲性，不外於理氣之相乘矣。理不可見，是謂至靜無感，性之淵源，一大虛無形，氣之本體所自來也。其交感不齊而知識生焉，是謂感而遂通，性之發見，一聚散有形，氣之變化所以行也。惟其主於虛，是故天命之性一焉，而聖愚賢不肖之分，與夫跂行蠕息之類，無有乎弗同，無有乎弗具者，理也。惟其隨於氣，是故氣質之性殊焉，而天下之偏者全者、清者濁者、厚者薄者、邪者正者，始紛紛雜出而不可禦矣。是故純粹至善固性也，剛柔純駁亦性也；立於無物之先固此性也，行於有物之後亦此性也。妙矣哉，性之
translation_en:
…principle exists throughout the world, leaving no place empty or unfilled; flowing along with qi, it constitutes the nature of human beings and other things, never ceasing. By analogy, it is like a door [?], with nature as its pivot. Through emptiness, the door can close and open: this principle truly exists, yet cannot be sought in physical form. Qi is its closing and opening, leaving perceptible traces and inseparable from everyday use. If one understands that what makes a pivot a pivot lies wholly in the wondrous efficacy of opening and closing, then one understands that what makes nature nature lies wholly in the interplay of principle and qi. Principle cannot be seen: this is called utmost stillness, without stimulation. It is the wellspring of nature, one great formless void, from which the fundamental substance of qi derives. Their mutual stimulation varies, and knowledge and awareness arise from it: this is called responding to stimulation and thereby attaining full penetration. It is nature’s manifestation, a single process of gathering and dispersing that possesses form [?], through which the transformations of qi proceed.

Precisely because it is grounded in emptiness, the nature conferred by Heaven is one. Despite the distinctions between sages and fools, the worthy and the unworthy, and among the creatures that creep and crawl, that in which none differs and which none lacks is principle. Precisely because it follows qi, the nature of one’s material endowment differs. Thus the partial and the complete, the clear and the turbid, the substantial and the meager, the deviant and the upright emerge throughout the world in an irrepressible profusion. Hence utter purity and supreme goodness are indeed nature, but firmness and softness, purity and admixture are also nature. What stands before things exist is indeed this nature; what operates after things exist is also this nature. How wondrous is nature’s…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
立名乎虛以主之不滯於有氣以運之不
淪於無其體用之所以一原顯微之所以
無間者乎君子知其所以爲性則盡性之
功奚容於外求乎何者太虛之理本無不
善而氣質所賦鮮有不偏聖人盡性者也
客感客形與無感無形者能一之非強合
之也性之本體如是也然則君子求以盡
乎性者也必深探其天命之原而求其所
謂理又究其形生之後而不梏於氣則虛
===
以廓之而一真自如百物皆通其究也與
太虛同其體氣以實之而良知良能妙用
不窮其究也與氣化同其運人之未始不
天賢之未始不聖也又何盡性之難哉是
非愚言之也形而後有氣質之性善反之
則天地之性存焉故氣質之性君子有弗
性焉張子固嘗言之矣而或者猶病其以
氣語道何哉
表
punctuated:
立名乎！虛以主之，不滯於有；氣以運之，不淪於無。其體用之所以一原、顯微之所以無間者乎！君子知其所以爲性，則盡性之功奚容於外求乎？何者？太虛之理本無不善，而氣質所賦鮮有不偏。聖人盡性者也，客感客形與無感無形者能一之，非強合之也，性之本體如是也。然則君子求以盡乎性者也，必深探其天命之原而求其所謂理，又究其形生之後而不梏於氣。則虛以廓之，而一真自如，百物皆通，其究也與太虛同其體；氣以實之，而良知良能妙用不窮，其究也與氣化同其運。人之未始不天，賢之未始不聖也，又何盡性之難哉？是非愚言之也。「形而後有氣質之性，善反之，則天地之性存焉。故氣質之性，君子有弗性焉。」張子固嘗言之矣，而或者猶病其以氣語道，何哉？

表
translation_en:
…the establishment of the name “nature”! With the void governing it, it does not become mired in being; with qi activating it, it does not sink into nonbeing. Is this not why its substance and function share a single source, and why its manifest and subtle aspects admit no separation? Once the gentleman understands what makes it nature, how could the work of fully realizing nature permit seeking outside oneself? Why is this so? The principle of the Great Void is originally wholly good, whereas the endowment of one's psychophysical constitution is rarely free of partiality. The sage fully realizes nature. He can unify adventitious sensations and forms with that which has neither sensation nor form. This is no forced union: the original substance of nature is inherently thus.

Thus, the gentleman who seeks fully to realize his nature must probe deeply into its source in Heaven's mandate, seeking what is called principle. He must also investigate what follows the emergence of bodily form, without becoming fettered by qi. The void then gives it breadth: the single reality remains freely itself and is in communion with all things. Ultimately, it shares the substance of the Great Void. Qi gives it concrete actuality: innate knowing and innate ability have inexhaustible wondrous functions. Ultimately, it shares the operation of the transformations of qi. The human has never been apart from Heaven, nor the worthy apart from the sage. What difficulty, then, is there in fully realizing nature? This is not merely my own foolish assertion. “Only after bodily form arises is there the nature of the psychophysical constitution. If one is adept at returning, the nature of Heaven and Earth is preserved therein. Thus, there are aspects of the nature of the psychophysical constitution that the gentleman does not accept as his nature.” Master Zhang has indeed already said this. Yet some still fault him for speaking of the Way in terms of qi. Why?

Memorials

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
擬宋以唐介參知政事謝表熙寧元年
陳錫
同考試官教諭吳批事核而精文麗而則深
得表體
考試官學正馮批臣子忠悃之意當如此
考試官學正劉批典麗詳贍
熙寧元年某月某日伏蒙
聖恩除臣參知政事者
鈞衡佐理班聯畫省之榮鼎實叅調位近
紫宸之寵顧叨塵之已甚念辭避之弗容拜
命周章捫心媿汗臣誠惶誠恐稽首頓首竊以
樞機之任式典於平章
密勿之謨尤資乎協賛輪班知印毗
廟論以象三台書
勅齊銜攝
朝揆而列八座名稱實肇於乾德墫位復定
於雍熙睠此崇階宜歸碩望伏念臣性惟
拙戅質本疎庸筮仕平江謬竊理寃之譽
punctuated:
擬宋以唐介參知政事謝表，熙寧元年。
陳錫
同考試官教諭吳批：事核而精，文麗而則，深得表體。
考試官學正馮批：臣子忠悃之意，當如此。
考試官學正劉批：典麗詳贍。
熙寧元年某月某日，伏蒙聖恩除臣參知政事者。
鈞衡佐理，班聯畫省之榮；鼎實叅調，位近紫宸之寵。顧叨塵之已甚，念辭避之弗容，拜命周章，捫心媿汗。臣誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首。竊以樞機之任，式典於平章；密勿之謨，尤資乎協賛。輪班知印，毗廟論以象三台；書勅齊銜，攝朝揆而列八座。名稱實肇於乾德，墫位復定於雍熙。睠此崇階，宜歸碩望。伏念臣性惟拙戅，質本疎庸。筮仕平江，謬竊理寃之譽。
translation_en:
A memorial of thanks composed in the persona of Tang Jie of the Song upon his appointment as Participant in Determining Governmental Matters, first year of Xining [1068].
By Chen Xi.
Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: Its treatment of events is accurate and precise; its language is elegant and conforms to proper standards. It thoroughly captures the form of the memorial.
Comment by Examiner Feng, School Instructor: This is how a subject should express his loyal sincerity.
Comment by Examiner Liu, School Instructor: Classically elegant, detailed, and ample.
On a certain day of a certain month in the first year of Xining, I humbly received Your Majesty’s gracious appointment as Participant in Determining Governmental Matters.
Assisting in governance at the balance beam of state, I join the honored ranks of the painted Secretariat; helping blend the ingredients in the ceremonial cauldron, I occupy a position favored with proximity to the Purple Palace. Reflecting that I have already presumed far too much in occupying office, yet mindful that I am not permitted to decline, I receive the appointment in agitation; searching my heart, I sweat with shame. Your servant is truly apprehensive and fearful, bowing low and knocking his head upon the ground.
I humbly consider that responsibility for the pivotal affairs of state properly rests with the Grand Councilors; yet their diligent and confidential deliberations especially depend upon assistance. Taking turns in custody of the seal, their associates support deliberations at court, mirroring the Three Terraces constellation; placing their signatures alongside one another on imperial edicts, they act for the chief minister and rank among the Eight Seats. The designation originated in the Qiande era, and the rank [?] was again fixed in the Yongxi era. Such an exalted station should surely fall to a man of outstanding reputation.
I humbly reflect that my nature is clumsy and stubborn, my capacities crude and ordinary. Beginning my official career in Pingjiang, I undeservedly acquired a reputation for redressing wrongful judgments.…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
配民昌鬲未寬留檄之憂驟晉臺官遂當
言路恥曲學而阿世屢效狂愚期直道以
事
君自干罪譴荷生成於
大造重以護使之勤仗忠信於危波猶席淸
淮之慶雖險阻艱難備嘗之矣矢沒齒於
江鄕而造次顛沛必於是焉敢貽書於政
府仰
仁皇之寬宥不次甄遷繼
===
英考之采收曲加勉
諭內省竟淪於孤迹何圖亦記於
淵衷起郡符以總憲樞徒爲歲月之積職韜
鈐以扞邊圉祗貽尸素之羞惟大原之奧
區據代朔之重地誤蒙付委靡卽棄捐方
慙有負於北門遽爾超陪乎西掖
恩深莫旣感極何言玆蓋伏遇
〇〇〇〇
道協舜華
punctuated: 配民昌鬲，未寬留檄之憂。驟晉臺官，遂當言路。恥曲學而阿世，屢效狂愚；期直道以事君，自干罪譴。荷生成於大造，重以護使之勤；仗忠信於危波，猶席淸淮之慶。雖險阻艱難備嘗之矣，矢沒齒於江鄕；而造次顛沛必於是焉，敢貽書於政府。仰仁皇之寬宥，不次甄遷；繼英考之采收，曲加勉諭。內省竟淪於孤迹，何圖亦記於淵衷？起郡符以總憲樞，徒爲歲月之積；職韜鈐以扞邊圉，祗貽尸素之羞。惟大原之奧區，據代朔之重地，誤蒙付委，靡卽棄捐。方慙有負於北門，遽爾超陪乎西掖。恩深莫旣，感極何言？玆蓋伏遇〇〇〇〇，道協舜華。
translation_en:
…Serving the people at Changge [?], I had not yet been relieved of the anxiety of being detained by an official summons [?]. Suddenly promoted to a post in the Censorate, I came to bear responsibility for remonstrance. Ashamed to distort learning to flatter the age, I repeatedly offered my rash and foolish views; hoping to serve my sovereign by the upright Way, I brought punishment upon myself. I owed my preservation and restoration to your great creative benevolence, and was further charged with the arduous duty of escorting an envoy. Relying upon loyalty and trustworthiness amid perilous waves, I still enjoyed the blessing of a tranquil Huai River [?]. Though I had experienced dangers and hardships to the full, I vowed to spend my remaining years in my riverside home. Yet even in haste and adversity I remained committed to these principles, and ventured to send a letter to the chief councillors.

I looked up to the benevolent pardon of Emperor Renzong, who selected and promoted me outside the usual order. Subsequently, your late imperial father Yingzong took me into service and graciously bestowed encouragement and instruction. Reflecting upon myself, I thought I had finally sunk into obscurity and isolation; how could I have imagined that I remained in your profound imperial thoughts? Raised from prefectural command to direct the central affairs of the Censorate, I merely accumulated years of service. Charged with military strategy and the defence of the frontier, I brought upon myself only the shame of holding office and drawing a salary without accomplishment. Taiyuan, a strategically sheltered region, occupies the crucial territory of Dai and Shuo. You mistakenly entrusted it to me, yet did not at once cast me aside. Just as I felt ashamed of failing in my responsibilities at the northern gate, I was suddenly advanced beyond the usual ranks to take my place in the western palace offices. Your grace is too profound to recount fully; what words can express the utmost depth of my gratitude?

This, I humbly recognize, is because I have had the good fortune to encounter [four circle marks in the text] you, whose Way accords with the splendour of Shun…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
志恢禹迹
至孝本於天縱
典學務於日新
霈兌澤以阜民尤軫一夫之不獲
極晉明而盡下尚虞片善之或遺謂綸閣之
深嚴難於獨用而政事之繁劇要在並觀
遂令疏逖之蹤亦忝延登之數先時髦而
取
召驚
===
鳳藻於
中天被
睿旨之叮嚀赫
龍光於
黼座論資校考豈云遺直之可稱揣分量能
蓋自
眷私之過厚矧
聖明奮大作之志恐莫裨於賛襄而羣工協勵
翼之休諒無庸於借聽將籲
punctuated: 志恢禹迹，至孝本於天縱，典學務於日新。霈兌澤以阜民，尤軫一夫之不獲；極晉明而盡下，尚虞片善之或遺。謂綸閣之深嚴，難於獨用，而政事之繁劇，要在並觀。遂令疏逖之蹤，亦忝延登之數。先時髦而取召，驚鳳藻於中天；被睿旨之叮嚀，赫龍光於黼座。論資校考，豈云遺直之可稱；揣分量能，蓋自眷私之過厚。矧聖明奮大作之志，恐莫裨於賛襄；而羣工協勵翼之休，諒無庸於借聽。將籲
translation_en:
…Your ambition is to extend Yu’s achievements; Your utmost filial devotion springs from Heaven’s endowment, and in constant study You strive for daily renewal. You abundantly bestow the beneficence of Dui to enrich the people, especially grieving lest even one man fail to find his proper place; You extend the illumination of Jin to reach all below, still fearing that even the smallest good might be overlooked.

You consider that, within the secluded and solemn halls where imperial commands are drafted, it is difficult to rely on one man alone, while the complexity and burdens of government require consideration from several perspectives. Thus even one so distant and obscure as I has been undeservedly included among those invited to advancement. Summoned ahead of the outstanding men of the age, I marvel at Your phoenix-like composition high in the heavens; receiving the earnest admonitions of Your sagacious instructions, I am illuminated by Your dragon-like glory at the throne adorned with the axe pattern.

When my seniority and performance are assessed, how could I be praised as an heir to the upright men of old? When I consider my station and measure my abilities, this can only be attributed to Your excessively generous personal favor. Moreover, Your sagacious Majesty has roused Yourself to undertake great deeds, yet I fear I can contribute nothing to assisting You; and the assembled officials unite in the admirable work of diligent support, so surely there is no need to lend an ear to me. I am about to cry out…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
天而致禱蹐地以靡遑念匪忘身何能報
國敢不淬礪初志湔滌宿愆萑葦必使率由
所期協力堂帖悉與削去惟務格心謨弼
相資竊慕曰都曰俞之盛寅恭匪懈益堅
惟忠惟孝之忱或能自進於尋常庶可仰
酬於萬一伏願
凝神履祉
端穆承休賢才彙進於多方
聲教遹光於前烈矢卷阿之頌遠邁周室之
===
洪基賡喜起之歌永保虞庭之盛治臣某
無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
聞
第叄塲
策
punctuated:
天而致禱，蹐地以靡遑。念匪忘身，何能報國？敢不淬礪初志，湔滌宿愆？萑葦必使率由，所期協力；堂帖悉與削去，惟務格心。謨弼相資，竊慕曰都曰俞之盛；寅恭匪懈，益堅惟忠惟孝之忱。或能自進於尋常，庶可仰酬於萬一。伏願凝神履祉，端穆承休，賢才彙進於多方，聲教遹光於前烈。矢《卷阿》之頌，遠邁周室之洪基；賡喜起之歌，永保虞庭之盛治。臣某無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。

第叄塲
策
translation_en:
…to Heaven in prayer, treading the earth with anxious steps and finding no respite. I reflect that unless I forget myself, how can I repay the state? How could I dare not temper my original resolve and wash away my past faults? Those among the reeds must be brought to compliance, in the hope of concerted effort [?]; all secretariat directives shall be abolished, with the sole aim of rectifying the sovereign’s heart [?]. With counsel and assistance sustaining one another, I humbly aspire to the flourishing age when ruler and ministers exchanged words of approval and assent. Reverent and respectful without slackening, I shall strengthen still further my sincere devotion to loyalty and filial duty. If I can advance beyond the ordinary, perhaps I may repay one ten-thousandth of the favor bestowed upon me.

I humbly wish that Your Majesty may concentrate your spirit and enjoy blessings, and receive good fortune in dignity and serenity; that worthy men of talent may advance together from every quarter; and that your civilizing influence may further illuminate the glorious achievements of your predecessors. Offering the praise of the poem Winding Hills (Juan’e), may you far surpass the great foundations of the house of Zhou; continuing the song of rejoicing and rising to service, may you preserve forever the flourishing rule of Shun’s court. Your servant, So-and-so, gazing toward Heaven and looking up to Your Sageliness, cannot contain his utmost fervor, awe, and trembling. I respectfully submit this memorial to express my thanks and bring them to Your Majesty’s hearing.

Third Session
Policy Essays

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
第一問
周詩
同考試官教諭林批我
皇祖以詩爲教我
皇上妙契真傳子能揚厲無遺其涵濡治化而歌詠太平者耶
考試官學正馮批皇極敷言之訓箕子以
告武王得道統之傳我
皇上心學淵源上符唐虞文武之盛此策敷陳精確必佳士也
考試官學正劉批詩可以興其功用甚大
===
觀子敷颺明悉其今之康衢順則者歟
聖人有至文之著以弘敷言之治必有至
道之凝以立建極之體何言乎文也著作
通於庶政以明教化以一風俗以經緯天
地者也何言乎道也精蘊具於一心以敘
彝倫以章物軌以綱維治理者也文不著
則不能以達政道不凝則不足以敷文夫
惟道以宅心而建其有極則敷之言也自
四達而不悖明徴而無疆矣此聖人所以
punctuated:
第一問
周詩
同考試官教諭林批：我皇祖以詩爲教，我皇上妙契真傳。子能揚厲無遺，其涵濡治化而歌詠太平者耶？
考試官學正馮批：皇極敷言之訓，箕子以告武王，得道統之傳。我皇上心學淵源，上符唐虞文武之盛。此策敷陳精確，必佳士也。
考試官學正劉批：詩可以興，其功用甚大。觀子敷颺明悉，其今之康衢順則者歟？
聖人有至文之著，以弘敷言之治，必有至道之凝，以立建極之體。何言乎文也？著作通於庶政，以明教化，以一風俗，以經緯天地者也。何言乎道也？精蘊具於一心，以敘彝倫，以章物軌，以綱維治理者也。文不著，則不能以達政；道不凝，則不足以敷文。夫惟道以宅心而建其有極，則敷之言也，自四達而不悖，明徴而無疆矣。此聖人所以
translation_en:
First Policy Question
Zhou Shi 周詩

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: Our imperial ancestor used poetry to teach; our reigning emperor wondrously accords with its true transmission. You have extolled this fully, leaving nothing out. Are you one who, steeped in the transforming influence of good government, sings of great peace?

Comment by Examiner Feng, Instructor: Jizi conveyed to King Wu the teaching concerning the Imperial Norm and the promulgation of words, and King Wu received the transmission of the succession of the Way. The profound sources of our reigning emperor’s learning of the mind accord with the flourishing ages of Tang Yao, Yu Shun, King Wen, and King Wu. This policy essay sets forth its arguments precisely and soundly: its author must be a worthy scholar.

Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: Poetry can inspire; its efficacy is very great. Observing how clearly and fully you expound and extol this, might you be a present-day singer on the thoroughfare of Kangqu, celebrating obedience to the established norms?

For the sage to manifest consummate literary expression and thereby extend government through the promulgation of words, he must possess a settled embodiment of the consummate Way, thereby establishing the foundation for setting up the supreme standard. What is meant here by literary expression? It is writing that permeates all affairs of government, illuminates moral instruction, unifies customs, and orders Heaven and Earth. What is meant here by the Way? Its essential profundities are fully present within the single mind, ordering the enduring human relationships, making manifest the standards governing all things, and sustaining orderly government. Unless literary expression is manifest, government cannot be made effective; unless the Way is firmly embodied, literary expression cannot adequately unfold. Only when the Way dwells in the mind and establishes its supreme standard will the words through which it is promulgated naturally reach everywhere without contradiction, furnish manifest proof, and extend without limit. This is how the sage…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
獨觀昭曠之原而弘化於陶鈞之上者也
彼求工於聲律者藝焉爾矣烏足以語聖
人敷言之治哉猗歟休哉茲我
聖祖
皇上昭著作於詩篇妙感孚於道化者皆非淺
見陋聞所得而窺測賛揚者也蓋甞誦典
謨而思堯舜歌雅頌而慕商周則詩之爲
敎其來遠矣自舜命官典樂設敎而曰詩
言志歌永言夫有虞盛時旣以此爲治本
===
又專官以爲之敎其所以育人才養性情
事神祇和上下而體用功效廣大深切者
豈偶然哉其在三代天子巡狩陳詩以觀
民風則載之王制以六詩敎天下則載之
周禮今皆不可槩見而僅存者孔子所刪
三百篇試取而誦之其溫柔敦厚猶能使
千載之下莫不興起則商周所以敷言弘
化者其風旨可想見矣然后夔以四德爲
敎大師以六德爲敎則聖人之躬行於上
punctuated:
獨觀昭曠之原，而弘化於陶鈞之上者也。彼求工於聲律者，藝焉爾矣，烏足以語聖人敷言之治哉！猗歟休哉！茲我聖祖、皇上，昭著作於詩篇，妙感孚於道化者，皆非淺見陋聞所得而窺測賛揚者也。
蓋甞誦典謨而思堯舜，歌雅頌而慕商周，則詩之爲敎，其來遠矣。自舜命官典樂設敎，而曰：「詩言志，歌永言。」夫有虞盛時，旣以此爲治本，又專官以爲之敎，其所以育人才、養性情、事神祇、和上下，而體用功效廣大深切者，豈偶然哉？其在三代，天子巡狩，陳詩以觀民風，則載之《王制》；以六詩敎天下，則載之《周禮》。今皆不可槩見，而僅存者，孔子所刪三百篇。試取而誦之，其溫柔敦厚，猶能使千載之下莫不興起，則商周所以敷言弘化者，其風旨可想見矣。然后夔以四德爲敎，大師以六德爲敎，則聖人之躬行於上
translation_en:
…alone apprehends the source of luminous vastness and extends transforming influence from above, shaping all things as a potter does clay. Those who seek only mastery of tones and prosody possess merely a craft: how could they be qualified to discuss the sage’s governance through the dissemination of his words? Ah, how splendid! Our Sagely Progenitor and His Majesty manifest their literary accomplishment in poems and wondrously evoke a trusting response through the transforming influence of the Way. None of this can be fathomed or adequately praised by those of shallow insight and limited learning.
I have recited the Canons and Counsels and thought of Yao and Shun; I have sung the Odes and Hymns and admired the Shang and Zhou. Poetry’s use in teaching thus has a long history. Shun appointed an official to oversee music and establish instruction, saying: “Poetry expresses intent; song prolongs the words.” In the flourishing age of the lord of Youyu, poetry was already made a foundation of governance, and a dedicated official was further appointed to teach it. Could it be mere accident that its substance, application, and effects were so expansive and profound in nurturing talent, cultivating dispositions and feelings, serving the spirits of heaven and earth, and harmonizing superiors and inferiors? Under the Three Dynasties, when the Son of Heaven made inspection tours, poems were presented so that he could observe the customs of the people: this is recorded in “Royal Regulations.” Teaching all under Heaven through the six kinds of poetry is recorded in the Rites of Zhou. Today these practices can no longer be seen in their entirety; what alone survives is the three hundred poems edited by Confucius. Try taking them up and reciting them: their gentleness, tenderness, sincerity, and generosity can still stir everyone to moral endeavor even a thousand years later. From this we may imagine the spirit and purport of the means by which the Shang and Zhou disseminated their words and extended their transforming influence. Then Kui taught through the four virtues, and the Music Master taught through the six virtues; thus, as for the sage’s personal practice in his exalted position…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
也必有其本獨藝焉已哉今考帝王之詩
莫過於皇極敷言之訓曰無偏無陂遵王
之義無有作好遵王之道無有作惡遵王
之路曰無偏無黨王道蕩蕩無黨無偏王
道平平無反無側王道正直曰會其有極
歸其有極歌咏以協其音反覆以致其意
而又歸宿以要其成則古人作詩之體備
是矣蓋先王之世敬天授時而五行順正
已檢身而五事脩豐財利民而八政舉脩
===
德致祥而五紀協以乂三德則剛柔正直
並用也以明稽疑則龜筮庶謀協同也以
驗庶徵則五氣時若也以徵福極則諸福
咸臻也是惟建其有極矣宜其著之詩篇
以敎天下者莫不是訓是行而歌咏太平
之澤不絕帝之所以帝王之所以王由此
其選也自平王東遷詩廢不講以及漢唐
而下非無作者若漢武帝秋風栢梁之句
唐太宗慶善臨朝之什魏文帝戒盈之賦
punctuated: 也，必有其本，獨藝焉已哉？今考帝王之詩，莫過於皇極敷言之訓，曰：「無偏無陂，遵王之義；無有作好，遵王之道；無有作惡，遵王之路。」曰：「無偏無黨，王道蕩蕩；無黨無偏，王道平平；無反無側，王道正直。」曰：「會其有極，歸其有極。」歌咏以協其音，反覆以致其意，而又歸宿以要其成，則古人作詩之體備是矣。蓋先王之世，敬天授時而五行順，正已檢身而五事脩，豐財利民而八政舉，脩德致祥而五紀協；以乂三德，則剛柔正直並用也；以明稽疑，則龜筮庶謀協同也；以驗庶徵，則五氣時若也；以徵福極，則諸福咸臻也。是惟建其有極矣，宜其著之詩篇以敎天下者，莫不是訓是行，而歌咏太平之澤不絕。帝之所以帝，王之所以王，由此其選也。自平王東遷，詩廢不講，以及漢唐而下，非無作者，若漢武帝《秋風》《栢梁》之句、唐太宗《慶善》《臨朝》之什、魏文帝《戒盈》之賦，
translation_en:
…must have had a foundation in the sages’ own exemplary conduct above. Could this have been merely an accomplishment in the arts? Now, examining the poetry of emperors and kings, nothing surpasses the instruction proclaimed in the section on the August Standard: “Without partiality or deviation, follow the king’s righteousness. Do not indulge personal likes; follow the king’s Way. Do not indulge personal dislikes; follow the king’s road.” It says: “Without partiality or faction, the king’s Way is broad and open. Without faction or partiality, the king’s Way is level and smooth. Without reversal or deflection, the king’s Way is correct and straight.” It says: “Gather at the standard; return to the standard.” Singing harmonizes its sounds; repetition fully conveys its meaning; and a final point of return brings it to completion. Here, then, the ancient manner of composing poetry is fully realized.

In the age of the former kings, reverence for Heaven and the promulgation of the seasons brought the Five Phases into proper order. Rectifying oneself and exercising personal restraint cultivated the Five Activities. Increasing resources and benefiting the people ensured the implementation of the Eight Affairs of Government. Cultivating virtue and bringing about auspicious signs harmonized the Five Regulators of Time. In governing through the Three Virtues, firmness, flexibility, and correctness and straightness were all employed. In clarifying the Examination of Doubts, turtle-shell and milfoil divination agreed with the various counsels. In testing the Various Indications, the five atmospheric influences accorded with their seasons. In verifying Blessings and Extremities, all blessings arrived together. This was indeed to establish the standard. It was fitting that the poems they set forth to teach the world should all teach and put into practice these principles, and that songs celebrating the blessings of great peace should never cease. That emperors became true emperors and kings true kings arose from this—their distinction [?].

Since King Ping’s eastward relocation, poetry fell into neglect and ceased to be studied. Down through the Han and Tang and later ages, there were certainly writers: for example, Emperor Wu of Han’s verses on the Autumn Wind and the Cypress Beam Terrace; Emperor Taizong of Tang’s poems on Celebrating Goodness and Holding Court; and Emperor Wen of Wei’s rhapsody Admonition against Complacency…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
宋太宗宴士之篇不過排比聲偶取贍麗
冲邁之評以求工於一時視帝王所以巍
然煥然者迥不侔矣矧冀其詩敎之興於
天下也哉洪惟我
太祖高皇帝繼天而作創造區夏因造化之盪
滌紹百王之景休
成祖文皇帝光臨璿極脩輯六經繼閎暢於
帝猷顯
休烈於
===
皇範其於堯舜三王之道心融神會身體力行
凡所
垂訓有不言自喻者今觀我
高皇所著如
命儒臣書洪範一篇揭于
座右以備省覽且
親為之註先之五行五事八政五紀所以推皇
極之體也繼之三德稽疑庶徵福極所以
昭皇極之用也而首以叙彛倫保萬民者
punctuated:
宋太宗宴士之篇，不過排比聲偶，取贍麗冲邁之評，以求工於一時，視帝王所以巍然煥然者，迥不侔矣。矧冀其詩敎之興於天下也哉！
洪惟我太祖高皇帝，繼天而作，創造區夏，因造化之盪滌，紹百王之景休。成祖文皇帝，光臨璿極，脩輯六經，繼閎暢於帝猷，顯休烈於皇範。其於堯舜三王之道，心融神會，身體力行，凡所垂訓，有不言自喻者。今觀我高皇所著，如命儒臣書《洪範》一篇，揭于座右，以備省覽，且親為之註。先之五行、五事、八政、五紀，所以推皇極之體也；繼之三德、稽疑、庶徵、福極，所以昭皇極之用也。而首以叙彛倫、保萬民者，
translation_en:
…and Emperor Taizong of Song’s poem on feasting with scholars: these did no more than arrange sounds and parallel phrases, seeking praise for richness, elegance, serene loftiness, and transcendence, in pursuit of literary accomplishment in their own day. They fell far short of that which made the ancient emperors and kings so towering and radiant. How much less could one hope that their poetic teaching would flourish throughout the realm!
We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao arose in succession to Heaven and founded his rule over the Chinese realm. Taking advantage of the cleansing wrought by the transforming powers of nature, he carried forward the glorious accomplishments of the hundred kings. Emperor Chengzu Wen gloriously ascended the imperial throne and revised and compiled the Six Classics, continuing and broadly extending the imperial plans [?] and manifesting splendid achievements in the imperial model. As for the Way of Yao, Shun, and the Three Kings, they comprehended it in heart and spirit and put it into practice in their own persons with all their strength. Among all the teachings they bequeathed, some are understood without words.
Now, examining the writings of our Emperor Gao, we find, for example, that he ordered his Confucian ministers to copy out the chapter “The Great Plan” (Hongfan) and display it beside his seat for his inspection. Moreover, he personally composed a commentary on it. Placing first the Five Phases, the Five Personal Affairs, the Eight Affairs of Government, and the Five Regulators of Time serves to expound the substance of the August Ultimate. Following these with the Three Virtues, the Examination of Doubts, the Various Verifications, and the Blessings and Extremities serves to illuminate the functioning of the August Ultimate. And the fact that it begins with setting the constant human relationships in order and protecting the myriad people…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
非帝王爲治之要道乎我
文皇所著如輯
爲善陰隲
孝順事實二書以
訓天下且各
咏以詩其題放DRU療鶴則有所謂全生不殺
有陰功窮託神人救餘命者也其題躍魚
出鯉則有所謂孝道能敦在稚年舍側出
泉誠異事者也而
===
===
序以一念之善通於神明非推天而驗之人
者乎大哉
皇言郁乎琬琰而皆切於民彜蓋與敷言之訓
相爲經緯非徒延光將來比榮往號而已
也肆天下家傳人誦寡過而歸極淳風熙
洽聲教宣流天下太和者垂百八十餘年
於兹矣迨我
皇上欽明神聖應運
中興恢弘
punctuated: 非帝王爲治之要道乎？我文皇所著，如輯《爲善陰隲》《孝順事實》二書，以訓天下，且各咏以詩。其題放DRU療鶴，則有所謂「全生不殺有陰功，窮託神人救餘命」者也；其題躍魚出鯉，則有所謂「孝道能敦在稚年，舍側出泉誠異事」者也。而序以一念之善通於神明，非推天而驗之人者乎？大哉皇言！郁乎琬琰，而皆切於民彜，蓋與敷言之訓相爲經緯，非徒延光將來、比榮往號而已也。肆天下家傳人誦，寡過而歸極，淳風熙洽，聲教宣流，天下太和者垂百八十餘年於兹矣。迨我皇上欽明神聖，應運中興，恢弘
translation_en:
…is this not the essential Way by which emperors and kings govern? Among the writings of our Emperor Wen are the two compilations, Doing Good and Its Hidden Recompense (Weishan yinzhi) and True Accounts of Filial Obedience (Xiaoshun shishi), intended to instruct all under Heaven. He also celebrated their accounts in verse.
