title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
負奉宣匪人則閭閻反以多事而所收不
償所出又不若凶歲之可支也民何由被
實惠哉宋自紹興以後役煩賦重極力寬
之民病猶未甦也而朱熹上封事有遷延
一分以待蠲放之議者蓋宋初舊法凡催
理官物數及九分諸司卽行停止版曹亦
置不問州縣得其贏餘以相補助貧民亦
得遷延以待蠲除較之虛文無實所謂黃
紙放白紙取者不亦相去遠哉由是觀之
===
人君之治國也猶醫之治病也緩則治其
本亟則治其標今兩浙之民病亦亟矣誠
司牧者所當軫念也顧
國賦旣不可缺則蠲負其可恃乎嘗稽之宋
紹興間因湖秀水災欲除下戶積欠慮恐
侵損歲支輒於內庫撥補似恤民者然湖
秀一隅侵損未多補給尚易若舉天下而
出內帑給之不知當時又將何以處之耶
又嘗稽之唐矣玄宗蠲免七年以前逋負
punctuated: 負，奉宣匪人，則閭閻反以多事，而所收不償所出，又不若凶歲之可支也。民何由被實惠哉？宋自紹興以後，役煩賦重，極力寬之，民病猶未甦也。而朱熹上封事，有遷延一分以待蠲放之議者，蓋宋初舊法，凡催理官物，數及九分，諸司卽行停止，版曹亦置不問。州縣得其贏餘以相補助，貧民亦得遷延以待蠲除。較之虛文無實，所謂黃紙放、白紙取者，不亦相去遠哉？由是觀之，人君之治國也，猶醫之治病也：緩則治其本，亟則治其標。今兩浙之民病亦亟矣，誠司牧者所當軫念也。顧國賦旣不可缺，則蠲負其可恃乎？嘗稽之宋紹興間，因湖秀水災，欲除下戶積欠，慮恐侵損歲支，輒於內庫撥補，似恤民者。然湖秀一隅，侵損未多，補給尚易；若舉天下而出內帑給之，不知當時又將何以處之耶？又嘗稽之唐矣，玄宗蠲免七年以前逋負。
translation_en:
…arrears, and those charged with carrying out the orders are unsuitable men, the common people instead face increased vexations. What they take in does not cover what they must pay out, and they are less able to sustain themselves than in a year of poor harvests. How can the people receive any tangible benefit?

From the Shaoxing era onward under the Song, labor obligations were onerous and taxation heavy. Even strenuous efforts to provide relief failed to alleviate the people's distress. Yet Zhu Xi, in a sealed memorial, proposed allowing payment of the remaining tenth to be deferred pending remission. Under an old rule from the beginning of the Song, whenever collection of payments due to the government reached nine-tenths, the various offices immediately stopped collection, and the Ministry of Revenue likewise left the matter alone. Prefectures and counties could use their surpluses to make up one another's shortfalls, while the poor could defer payment pending remission. Was this not far removed from empty formalities without substance—the practice described as “remitting by yellow paper and collecting by white paper”?

Viewed in this light, a ruler's governance of his country resembles a physician's treatment of illness: when the condition is not urgent, treat its root; when it is acute, treat its symptoms. The distress of the people of Liangzhe is now acute indeed, and those charged with tending them should truly take it to heart. Yet since the state's tax revenues cannot fall short, can remission of arrears be relied upon?

I have examined the precedent from the Shaoxing era of the Song. Following floods in Huzhou and Xiuzhou, the authorities wished to cancel the accumulated arrears of lower-category households. Fearing that this would diminish the funds available for annual expenditure, they allocated funds from the palace treasury to cover the shortfall. This would seem to have been compassionate toward the people. Yet Huzhou and Xiuzhou constituted only one small area: the shortfall was modest, and replenishing the funds was still easy. Had funds been drawn from the palace treasury to cover the whole realm, I do not know how they would have managed it then.

I have also examined the Tang precedent: Xuanzong remitted arrears dating from before the seventh year…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
當時稱爲異數然寬貸之舉止爲貧民若
果貧民欠負盡數免之以蘇疲困亦何不
可但膏脂已竭於無告而惠澤翻及於姦
豪中間雖究已收未收之等亦誰肯自陳
其弊哉善乎宋臣趙善防有云貧民下戶
毎歲二稅但有重納未甞拖欠朝廷蠲放
利歸攬戶鄉胥而小民未甞霑恩乞明詔
自今郊霈惟減次年賦稅其目前殘零務
依數納足則貧民實被寬恩官賦亦易催
===
理此治標之策與朱熹遞延一分之說皆
足以甦民困而善於通變者矣然亦豈可
以常恃也哉王制曰三年耕必有一年之
食九年耕必有三年之食以三十年之通
制國用雖有凶旱水溢民無菜色今不豫
之於粟米狼戾之時而顧行之於十室九
空之日亦無及矣毋亦於所以固邦本者
加之意焉可乎吾浙本水鄉十日之霖大
浸也一月之旱赤土也是故按圖籍以尋
punctuated:
當時稱爲異數，然寬貸之舉止爲貧民。若果貧民欠負，盡數免之以蘇疲困，亦何不可？但膏脂已竭於無告，而惠澤翻及於姦豪，中間雖究已收未收之等，亦誰肯自陳其弊哉？善乎宋臣趙善防有云：「貧民下戶，每歲二稅，但有重納，未甞拖欠。朝廷蠲放，利歸攬戶、鄉胥，而小民未甞霑恩。乞明詔，自今郊霈，惟減次年賦稅，其目前殘零，務依數納足，則貧民實被寬恩，官賦亦易催理。」此治標之策，與朱熹遞延一分之說，皆足以甦民困而善於通變者矣。然亦豈可以常恃也哉？
王制曰：「三年耕，必有一年之食；九年耕，必有三年之食。以三十年之通，制國用，雖有凶旱水溢，民無菜色。」今不豫之於粟米狼戾之時，而顧行之於十室九空之日，亦無及矣。毋亦於所以固邦本者加之意焉，可乎？吾浙本水鄉，十日之霖，大浸也；一月之旱，赤土也。是故按圖籍以尋
translation_en:
…At the time, this was acclaimed as an exceptional act of grace. Yet such measures of relief are intended solely for the poor. If the arrears truly belong to poor households, what objection could there be to remitting them in full to relieve their exhaustion and distress? But the helpless have already been drained of their substance, while the benefits instead reach unscrupulous powerful households. Even if an inquiry distinguishes sums already collected from those not yet collected, who would willingly disclose his own abuses? Well did the Song official Zhao Shanfang 趙善防 [?] say: “Poor households in the lowest category pay the two annual taxes; they suffer repeated collection, but have never fallen into arrears. When the court grants remissions, the benefits go to tax-contracting households and village clerks, while the common people receive none of the grace. I beg that an explicit edict be issued: henceforth, acts of grace accompanying the suburban sacrifices should reduce only the following year’s taxes. All outstanding balances currently due must be paid in full according to the assessed amounts. Then the poor will truly receive generous relief, and government taxes will also be easier to collect.” This expedient for treating the symptoms, together with Zhu Xi’s proposal to defer one portion successively, can relieve the people’s distress and skillfully accommodate changing circumstances. Yet how could such measures be relied upon indefinitely?
The “Royal Regulations” chapter of the Book of Rites says: “Three years of cultivation must yield one year’s food in reserve; nine years of cultivation must yield three years’ food in reserve. Regulate state expenditure over a thirty-year span, and even when severe drought or flooding occurs, the people will show no signs of hunger.” If preparations are not made when grain is abundant, but are attempted only when nine households out of ten stand empty, it is already too late. Might we not devote greater attention to the means of securing the foundation of the state? Our Zhejiang is by nature a region of waterways: ten days of continuous rain bring great inundation; a month of drought leaves the earth bare. Thus, consulting maps and registers to seek …

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
源委之迹懲豪猾以復陂堰之利嚴修築
以固隄防之設時疏濬以續已成之功所
以興其利也而民窮之弊不與焉盖民之
窮在於賦人者無法而賦於人者之不繼
也夫贓吏之侵漁里胥之暴擾冗食之糜
費賄門之未塞所謂賦人者無法也若科
差之不均輸納之重費末技之未抑奢僭
之無度所謂賦於人者之不繼也二者相
因展轉交害如之何不窮且盜也此皆幾
===
之所當察而行之在於得人焉耳使得其
人焉力去今日之弊而新之則賦者有法
而賦於人者不患其不繼亦可以廣先王
預備之政矣不幸而災變生焉度宜以處
之其亦庶乎其有濟也否則蠲除之令雖
行而所以病民者固在也烏足以語圖理
之常道哉雖然朱熹曰爲政者當順五行
脩五事以安百姓今
聖天子脩德召和節財裕民之說每見於
punctuated: 源委之迹，懲豪猾以復陂堰之利，嚴修築以固隄防之設，時疏濬以續已成之功，所以興其利也，而民窮之弊不與焉。盖民之窮，在於賦人者無法，而賦於人者之不繼也。夫贓吏之侵漁、里胥之暴擾、冗食之糜費、賄門之未塞，所謂賦人者無法也。若科差之不均、輸納之重費、末技之未抑、奢僭之無度，所謂賦於人者之不繼也。二者相因，展轉交害，如之何不窮且盜也？此皆幾之所當察，而行之在於得人焉耳。使得其人焉，力去今日之弊而新之，則賦者有法，而賦於人者不患其不繼，亦可以廣先王預備之政矣。不幸而災變生焉，度宜以處之，其亦庶乎其有濟也。否則，蠲除之令雖行，而所以病民者固在也，烏足以語圖理之常道哉！雖然，朱熹曰：「爲政者當順五行，脩五事，以安百姓。」今聖天子脩德召和、節財裕民之說，每見於
translation_en:
…the traces of the waterways’ sources and courses; restraining powerful wrongdoers to restore the benefits of reservoirs and weirs; rigorously undertaking repairs and construction to secure the dikes and embankments; and dredging at appropriate times to sustain what has already been accomplished—these are ways to promote their benefits, but they do not address the ills that impoverish the people. The people’s poverty arises because those who levy taxes lack proper rules, while those taxed by others cannot keep up their payments. The predations of corrupt officials, the violent harassment by village clerks, the wasteful expenditure on superfluous dependents, and the failure to close off avenues for bribery: these are what is meant by those who levy taxes lacking proper rules. Unequal assessments of service obligations, the heavy costs of delivering tax payments, the failure to curb secondary occupations, and unbounded extravagance and overstepping of status: these are what is meant by those taxed by others being unable to keep up their payments. These two conditions feed upon one another, repeatedly compounding the harm. How could people fail to become impoverished and turn to banditry? These are all incipient developments that must be scrutinized; putting remedies into practice depends simply upon obtaining the right people. If the right people are obtained, and they vigorously eliminate today’s abuses and institute reforms, those who levy taxes will have proper rules, and there will be no fear that those taxed by others cannot sustain their payments. This would also extend the former kings’ policies of advance preparation. Should calamities unfortunately arise, one could assess what was appropriate and deal with them, with some hope of providing effective relief. Otherwise, even if orders for tax remission are implemented, the causes of the people’s suffering will remain. How could this suffice as the enduring way to achieve good government?

Nevertheless, Zhu Xi said: “Those who govern should accord with the Five Phases and cultivate the Five Duties, thereby bringing peace to the common people.” Today, the sagely Son of Heaven’s statements on cultivating virtue to summon harmony and economizing on expenditure to enrich the people frequently appear in…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
詔令則中和致而位育之功成矣又何民瘼之
弗蘇哉此固書生之談而非俊傑之識時
也幸與進之
punctuated: 詔令，則中和致而位育之功成矣，又何民瘼之弗蘇哉？此固書生之談，而非俊傑之識時也。幸與進之。
translation_en: …in imperial edicts, then equilibrium and harmony will be attained, and the work of setting Heaven and Earth in their proper places and nurturing all things will be accomplished. What suffering among the people would then remain unrelieved? These are admittedly the words of a mere scholar, rather than the insight of an outstanding man who understands the times. I hope you will nevertheless grant me advancement.

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
浙江鄉試錄後序
凡三年類士而鄉試之事竣
而錄其文與名氏以
獻遵
制也人臣以人事君之義也錄成
前後有序主司者旣選士而
序其事以寓規也士之得與
===
===
兹選蓋古司徒之所論而升
之者歌鹿鳴而燕之則旣待
以古之嘉賓矣而曷以規之
恒情時異則志易以渝勢遷
則塞易以變而况於入官之
始也可不愼歟嘉靖已酉秋
八月浙江鄉試錄成學正劉
punctuated:
浙江鄉試錄後序

凡三年類士而鄉試之，事竣而錄其文與名氏以獻，遵制也，人臣以人事君之義也。錄成，前後有序，主司者旣選士而序其事以寓規也。士之得與兹選，蓋古司徒之所論而升之者。歌《鹿鳴》而燕之，則旣待以古之嘉賓矣，而曷以規之？恒情，時異則志易以渝，勢遷則塞易以變，而况於入官之始也，可不愼歟？嘉靖已酉秋八月，浙江鄉試錄成，學正劉
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Zhejiang Provincial Examination

Every three years, scholars are assembled and examined in the Provincial Examination. When the proceedings are complete, their compositions and names are recorded for presentation to the throne. This observes the imperial regulations and fulfills the duty of a minister to serve his ruler by providing worthy men. Once the record is complete, it has a preface and a postface: having selected the scholars, those presiding over the examination recount the proceedings and use the occasion to offer admonition. The scholars admitted to this selection correspond to those whom the Minister of Education in antiquity assessed and advanced. By singing “The Deer Call” and feasting them, we have already treated them as the honored guests of antiquity. But what admonition should we offer them? In ordinary human nature, aspirations readily shift as times change, and one's disposition [?] readily alters as one's circumstances change. How much more is this so when beginning an official career! Can one fail to exercise caution? In autumn, in the eighth month of the jiyou year [?] of the Jiajing reign (1549), the Record of the Zhejiang Provincial Examination was completed. Instructor Liu…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
鶴翔旣序諸首簡矣繼科不
佞迺復進二三子而申告之
曰爾多士知
朝廷取士之制不越於文矣亦
思其所以取之乎知以文見
錄爲榮矣亦思所以無愧斯
錄乎漢唐取士專以詞賦我
===
朝監其制而於經義論策乎求
之亦惟文是校矣然嘗竊觀
我
太祖高皇帝設科之初卽
詔天下謂慮官非其人願得君子
而用之必經明行脩文質得中
名實相稱者始克登選肆我
punctuated: 鶴翔旣序諸首簡矣，繼科不佞，迺復進二三子而申告之曰：「爾多士知朝廷取士之制不越於文矣，亦思其所以取之乎？知以文見錄爲榮矣，亦思所以無愧斯錄乎？漢唐取士專以詞賦，我朝監其制，而於經義論策乎求之，亦惟文是校矣。然嘗竊觀我太祖高皇帝設科之初，卽詔天下，謂慮官非其人，願得君子而用之，必經明行脩、文質得中、名實相稱者，始克登選。肆我
translation_en: …Liu Hexiang has already written a preface on the opening leaves. I, Jike, unworthy though I am, therefore once more summoned you gentlemen forward and earnestly addressed you: “You scholars know that the court’s system for selecting men proceeds through their writing alone; but have you also considered the purpose for which it selects them? You know that selection on the strength of your writing is an honor; but have you also considered how to be worthy of this selection? The Han and Tang selected men exclusively through poetry and rhapsodies. Our dynasty, taking their system as a precedent, seeks men through interpretations of the Classics, discourses, and policy essays [?]; thus it too judges only their writing. Yet I have ventured to examine how, when our Emperor Taizu Gao first established the examinations, he immediately issued an edict to all under Heaven. He declared that, concerned lest offices be occupied by unsuitable men, he wished to obtain gentlemen of virtue and employ them. Only those who understood the Classics clearly and cultivated their conduct, whose literary refinement and substance were properly balanced, and whose reputations matched their actual qualities could gain selection. Thus our…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
皇上御極敦正文體崇雅黜浮
明詔之頒有曰士大夫學術不正
以致文章政事日趨詭異而聖
賢大學之道不明關係治理要
非細故夫
聖聖相承用人圖治而惟君子是
求惟聖賢大學之道是講謂
===
徒取其文已乎自鄉舉里選
之法廢雖豪傑之士崇德而
勵行不以文進則不能大行
於天下故文也者士君子所
以行道之階耳雖然文外無
道道外無文古三物之教曰
六德六行六藝莫非道也根
punctuated: 皇上御極，敦正文體，崇雅黜浮。明詔之頒有曰：「士大夫學術不正，以致文章政事日趨詭異，而聖賢大學之道不明，關係治理，要非細故。」夫聖聖相承，用人圖治，而惟君子是求，惟聖賢大學之道是講，謂徒取其文已乎？自鄉舉里選之法廢，雖豪傑之士崇德而勵行，不以文進，則不能大行於天下。故文也者，士君子所以行道之階耳。雖然，文外無道，道外無文。古三物之教曰六德、六行、六藝，莫非道也。根
translation_en:
…His Majesty ascended the throne, earnestly rectifying literary style, promoting refinement and rejecting superficiality. A promulgated imperial edict stated: “The learning of scholar-officials is not correct, with the result that their writing and conduct of government grow daily more aberrant, while the Way of the sages and worthies—the Great Learning—remains obscure. This bears upon the ordering of government and is by no means a minor matter.” Sage sovereigns succeed one another, employing men to achieve good government; they seek only exemplary men and attend only to the Way of the sages and worthies—the Great Learning. Can it be said that they merely select men for their writing?

Since the abolition of the system of recommending men from townships and selecting them from villages, even outstanding men who cultivate virtue and diligently improve their conduct cannot put their principles widely into practice throughout the realm unless they advance through writing. Writing is thus the stepping-stone by which gentlemen put the Way into practice. Nevertheless, outside writing there is no Way, and outside the Way there is no writing. The ancient teaching in three categories—the six virtues, six forms of conduct, and six arts—was in every respect the Way. Rooted…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
於心沛而爲辭合華實而一
之是故可以傳可以經世斯
無愧於文無愧於錄矣否則
飾辭以倖進畔於道者也其
如文何始繼科之應聘而至
也嘗自計兩浙爲東南巨藩
自昔以文獻先天下者豈以
===
文之不式爲慮惟明之未至
不免爲靡麗所眩而牝牡驪
黃之外無得焉是則可慮也
爾多士固嘗以此自慮乎盍
亦反其本矣蓋天之所以與
我者古今一而已德行文藝
胥此焉出而何有餘不足之
punctuated:
於心，沛而爲辭，合華實而一之。是故可以傳，可以經世，斯無愧於文，無愧於錄矣。否則，飾辭以倖進，畔於道者也，其如文何？
始繼科之應聘而至也，嘗自計：兩浙爲東南巨藩，自昔以文獻先天下者，豈以文之不式爲慮？惟明之未至，不免爲靡麗所眩，而牝牡驪黃之外無得焉，是則可慮也。爾多士固嘗以此自慮乎？盍亦反其本矣！蓋天之所以與我者，古今一而已，德行文藝胥此焉出，而何有餘不足之
translation_en:
…in the heart, pouring forth as words, uniting outward flowering and inner substance. Thus writing can be transmitted to posterity and can serve to order the world; it then merits being called literature and being included in this record. Otherwise, adorning one's words to seek advancement through mere good fortune is to depart from the Way. What then becomes of writing?
When I, Jike, first arrived in response to the invitation, I reflected: the Two Zhe regions form a great southeastern bulwark and have, since antiquity, led the realm in cultural achievements and learned worthies. Why should I worry that their writing might fail to meet the standards? My concern was only that, through insufficient discernment, I might be dazzled by ornate elegance and perceive nothing beyond such outward features as whether a horse is female or male, black or yellow. This indeed was cause for concern. Have you assembled scholars ever examined yourselves with this concern in mind? Why not return to the root! What Heaven bestows upon us has been the same throughout antiquity and the present. Virtue, conduct, literary accomplishment, and cultivated skills all issue from this. How, then, could there be any talk of excess or deficiency…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
云爾多士其務根極性分以
究其全祇服
聖訓以盡其大敦質實以基政而
恥以名與文勝焉夫然後爲
能反本而道在我矣由是而
時措之以賛翊
治化康理民物業樹而芳流他
日當有仰而稱之曰此聖賢
之實學也此君子之所作用
也而果出於今日浙藩之所
錄焉主司者豈不與有光榮
乎哉願相與圖之
湖廣襄陽府均州儒學學正
馮繼科謹序
punctuated:
云。爾多士其務根極性分，以究其全；祇服聖訓，以盡其大；敦質實以基政，而恥以名與文勝焉。夫然後爲能反本，而道在我矣。由是而時措之，以賛翊治化，康理民物，業樹而芳流。他日當有仰而稱之曰：「此聖賢之實學也，此君子之所作用也，而果出於今日浙藩之所錄焉。」主司者豈不與有光榮乎哉！願相與圖之。
湖廣襄陽府均州儒學學正馮繼科謹序。
translation_en:
…to speak of. You assembled scholars should strive to probe your inherent nature to its roots and comprehend it fully; respectfully follow the sage teachings and realize their full greatness; and cultivate substance and sincerity as the foundation of government, regarding it as shameful for reputation and literary polish to outweigh substance. Only then can you return to the root and possess the Way within yourselves. From this foundation, put it into practice as circumstances require, assisting governance and moral transformation, bringing well-being and order to the people and all things, establishing achievements and leaving a fragrant reputation. In days to come, there will surely be those who look up to you and declare: “This is the genuine learning of the sages and worthies; this is what the gentleman accomplishes in action. And these men indeed came from those selected in Zhejiang’s examination today.” Would not those presiding over the examination share in that honor and glory? I hope we may strive together toward this.
Preface respectfully composed by Feng Jike, Instructor in the Confucian School of Junzhou, Xiangyang Prefecture, Huguang.

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
浙江鄉試錄序
皇上御極二十有八年是爲嘉靖
己酉秋八月浙江鄉試巡按
監察御史李天寵實監臨之
振肅風紀飭厲百執事期得
眞材以副
朝廷求賢盛典時巡鹽御史董
===
威雅崇文教相與協謀而後
從事於是禮聘鶴翔及學正
馮繼科爲考試官教諭張天
敘劉邦聘倪朝惠鄭柱廖言
林紀吳紳廖瑚爲同考試官
其提調則左布政使張烜右
參政高世彥監試則按察使
punctuated:
浙江鄉試錄序

皇上御極二十有八年，是爲嘉靖己酉。秋八月，浙江鄉試，巡按監察御史李天寵實監臨之，振肅風紀，飭厲百執事，期得眞材，以副朝廷求賢盛典。時巡鹽御史董威雅崇文教，相與協謀而後從事。於是禮聘鶴翔及學正馮繼科爲考試官，教諭張天敘、劉邦聘、倪朝惠、鄭柱、廖言、林紀、吳紳、廖瑚爲同考試官。其提調則左布政使張烜、右參政高世彥，監試則按察使
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Zhejiang Provincial Examination

In the twenty-eighth year of His Majesty’s reign, the jiyou year of Jiajing (1549), the Zhejiang Provincial Examination was held in the eighth month, in autumn. Li Tianchong, Regional Inspector serving as Investigating Censor, acted as Supervising Official. He enforced discipline and admonished all personnel, seeking to obtain men of genuine ability in fulfillment of the court’s grand undertaking to recruit worthy men. At that time, Dong Wei, the Salt-control Censor, had long esteemed literary learning and education. They consulted together before proceeding.

Accordingly, He Xiang and Feng Jike, a School Instructor, were courteously invited to serve as Examiners. Zhang Tianxu, Liu Bangpin, Ni Chaohui, Zheng Zhu, Liao Yan, Lin Ji, Wu Shen, and Liao Hu, all School Instructors, served as Associate Examiners. The Proctors were Zhang Xuan, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner, and Gao Shiyan, Right Administration Vice Commissioner. Supervision of the examination was entrusted to the Provincial Surveillance Commissioner …

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
游居敬僉事謝體升其餘百
執事各以期至比入院則綱
凡畢舉法理森密而區畫於
御史者業有成績矣乃合提
學副使雷禮所簡士三千有
奇三校之得士九十人士之
限於
===
制而不能盡錄者多矣猗歟盛哉
事竣錄成以
獻鶴翔乃作而嘆曰浙古揚州
之域其俗淳龐純固兩漢以
還藝文肇見自嚴助方儲輩
以賢良對策褒然舉首自是
奇偉鴻博之士舒英耀華以
punctuated:
游居敬、僉事謝體升，其餘百執事各以期至。比入院，則綱凡畢舉，法理森密，而區畫於御史者業有成績矣。乃合提學副使雷禮所簡士三千有奇，三校之，得士九十人。士之限於制而不能盡錄者多矣。猗歟盛哉！事竣，錄成以獻。
鶴翔乃作而嘆曰：「浙，古揚州之域，其俗淳龐純固。兩漢以還，藝文肇見。自嚴助、方儲輩以賢良對策，褒然舉首，自是奇偉鴻博之士舒英耀華，以
translation_en:
…You Jujing and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Xie Tisheng; all the other functionaries arrived at the appointed time. By the time they entered the examination compound, every major and minor arrangement had been put into effect, and the rules and procedures were rigorous and meticulous. The plans made under the Censor’s direction had already borne fruit. They then assembled the more than three thousand candidates selected by Lei Li, the Surveillance Vice Commissioner overseeing education. After examining them in three sessions, they selected ninety men. Many candidates could not be admitted because of the quota fixed by imperial regulation. Ah, what a splendid occasion! When the proceedings were finished, the record was compiled for presentation to the throne.
Hexiang then rose and exclaimed: “Zhejiang lies within the territory of ancient Yangzhou. Its customs are simple, generous, pure, and steadfast. From the time of the two Han dynasties onward, literary accomplishments began to appear. Beginning with men such as Yan Zhu and Fang Chu, who answered policy questions as candidates recommended for their worthiness and goodness and were acclaimed as foremost, extraordinary men of vast learning thereafter displayed their talents and shone forth in brilliance, in order to…”

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
翊世運者浸浸焉庶矣迨宋
中葉吕祖謙倡道金華與朱
張鼎立一時士人迎風雅化
相與講明聖賢之學而人才
粹然一出于正獨藝焉已哉
我
聖祖龍興東南混一區宇首召浙
===
儒章溢劉基宋濂王禕至建
業贊謀
密勿其所以昭回
典制恢復經常洋洋焉與三代
同風識者已慶遭逢之盛而
文運兆于兩浙矣故士知所
嚮往脩其籩豆之業百八十
punctuated: 翊世運者浸浸焉庶矣。迨宋中葉，吕祖謙倡道金華，與朱、張鼎立一時。士人迎風雅化，相與講明聖賢之學，而人才粹然一出于正，獨藝焉已哉！我聖祖龍興東南，混一區宇，首召浙儒章溢、劉基、宋濂、王禕至建業，贊謀密勿。其所以昭回典制，恢復經常，洋洋焉與三代同風。識者已慶遭逢之盛，而文運兆于兩浙矣。故士知所嚮往，脩其籩豆之業，百八十
translation_en:
…those who helped advance the fortunes of the age grew steadily more numerous. By the middle of the Song dynasty, Lü Zuqian advocated the Way in Jinhua, standing alongside Zhu Xi and Zhang Shi as one of the three great masters of his time. Scholars responded to his influence and were refined by his teaching. Together they discussed and clarified the learning of the sages and worthies, so that men of talent emerged in their purity, all grounded in what was correct. Was this merely literary accomplishment?

Our Sagely Progenitor rose like a dragon in the southeast and united the realm. Among his first acts, he summoned the Zhejiang scholars Zhang Yi, Liu Ji, Song Lian, and Wang Yi to Jianye to assist him diligently in confidential deliberations. Through their efforts, established institutions were illuminated and enduring norms restored, with a flourishing grandeur that shared the spirit of the Three Dynasties. Discerning men already rejoiced in the good fortune of encountering such an age, and the promise of literary flourishing appeared in the Two Zhe regions. Thus scholars knew where to direct their aspirations and cultivated their learning in ritual observances for one hundred and eighty…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
餘年而名臣碩輔倚毗康濟
彬彬然輩出豈雲蒸風從不
然乎哉我
皇上履乾體正仁涵義洽文明泰
和之氣煥乎流曜宇宙間然
且
躬御
===
宸翰
闡明敬一之學以訓厲才賢是
以神化所被薄海內外罔不
翕然丕變況浙爲天下首藩
所以封植而濬發之者視四
國先焉將無道德之士出紹
前烈以茂翊
punctuated: 餘年，而名臣碩輔倚毗康濟，彬彬然輩出，豈雲蒸風從不然乎哉？我皇上履乾體正，仁涵義洽，文明泰和之氣煥乎流曜宇宙間。然且躬御宸翰，闡明敬一之學，以訓厲才賢。是以神化所被，薄海內外，罔不翕然丕變。況浙爲天下首藩，所以封植而濬發之者，視四國先焉。將無道德之士出紹前烈，以茂翊
translation_en:
…years and more, eminent ministers and great counsellors, relied upon to bring peace and succour to the realm, have emerged generation after generation in cultivated abundance. Is this not indeed like clouds gathering and winds following?

Our Emperor follows Heaven and embodies rectitude; his benevolence embraces all, and his righteousness pervades everything. The spirit of cultural brilliance and supreme harmony shines resplendently throughout the universe. Moreover, he personally wields the imperial brush to elucidate the learning of Reverent Unity (jingyi), thereby instructing and encouraging the talented and worthy. Thus, wherever his wondrous transforming influence reaches, throughout the lands within and beyond the seas, all have united in undergoing a profound transformation. Zhejiang, moreover, is the foremost province of the realm: the nurturing and deep cultivation bestowed upon it take precedence over those accorded to the other regions. Surely men of moral attainment will emerge to carry forward the illustrious achievements of their predecessors and lend abundant support to…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
昌運者哉今得其所爲文觀之
言雖人人殊類皆述禮樂明
仁義攄𢹂古今而不詭於孔
孟其所以稱
明詔興致太平於是乎在誠不專
於緣飾詩書用以規進取已
也昔周之文盛矣孔子蓋屢
===
嘆之乃曰如用之則吾從先
進懼夫文之盛而實焉者之
或寡也嘗觀章劉宋王居素
勵志皆正心誠意之學用能
持以自效如符券然兹多士
之呈藝而興也嘗以盛世之
士自命而簡文徴履設未能
punctuated:
昌運者哉？今得其所爲文觀之，言雖人人殊，類皆述禮樂，明仁義，攄𢹂古今，而不詭於孔孟。其所以稱明詔、興致太平，於是乎在，誠不專於緣飾詩書，用以規進取已也。
昔周之文盛矣，孔子蓋屢嘆之，乃曰：「如用之，則吾從先進。」懼夫文之盛，而實焉者之或寡也。嘗觀章劉宋王，居素勵志，皆正心誠意之學，用能持以自效，如符券然。兹多士之呈藝而興也，嘗以盛世之士自命，而簡文徴履，設未能
translation_en:
…to lend ample support to this flourishing age? Now that I have obtained and examined their writings, I find that, although their expressions differ from person to person, they generally expound rites and music, illuminate benevolence and righteousness, and set forth and draw together [?] matters ancient and modern without departing from Confucius and Mencius. Herein lies their means of answering the enlightened imperial edict and bringing about supreme peace. They certainly do not merely embellish their writings with the Odes and the Documents as a means of seeking advancement.
The cultural accomplishments of the Zhou were magnificent, and Confucius repeatedly praised them. Yet he said: “If I were to employ them, I would follow those who came first.” He feared that, amid such flourishing refinement, those possessing its substance might be few. I have observed that Zhang, Liu, Song, and Wang, in their ordinary lives and efforts to strengthen their resolve, all pursued the learning of rectifying the mind and making the intentions sincere. Thus they could uphold it and prove themselves in practice, matching it as precisely as the two halves of a tally. Now these many scholars present their literary accomplishments and rise to prominence, having styled themselves scholars of a flourishing age. Yet if, on scrutinizing their writings and examining their conduct, they should prove unable to…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
如前聞人焉不幾於甘詞紿
進者耶蓋士之始見也必以
贄故挾藝以進者士君子求
見于君之羔雉耳弗工於文
而希進是不飾羔雉以求遇
也使言而不足以成信則飾
羔雉而無恭敬之實矣夫知
===
恭敬之實在於飾羔雉之前
則知自獻其身以成其信者
固不在資言之後矣諸士尚
亦求副其志以信其言追古
名哲而媲美焉斯無媿于是
舉而我
國家無疆之休不端有賴耶是
punctuated: 如前聞人焉，不幾於甘詞紿進者耶？蓋士之始見也，必以贄，故挾藝以進者，士君子求見于君之羔雉耳。弗工於文而希進，是不飾羔雉以求遇也。使言而不足以成信，則飾羔雉而無恭敬之實矣。夫知恭敬之實在於飾羔雉之前，則知自獻其身以成其信者，固不在資言之後矣。諸士尚亦求副其志，以信其言，追古名哲而媲美焉，斯無媿于是舉，而我國家無疆之休，不端有賴耶？是
translation_en: …match those eminent men of earlier times, would they not come close to being men who obtain advancement through deceptive, pleasing words? When a scholar first presents himself, he must bring an introductory gift. Thus, the literary accomplishments he brings to seek advancement are merely the equivalent of the lambs and pheasants that gentlemen present when seeking an audience with their ruler. To hope for advancement without skill in writing is to seek reception without preparing these gifts. If, however, his words cannot establish his trustworthiness, it is as though he had prepared the lambs and pheasants but lacked genuine reverence and respect. Once one understands that genuine reverence and respect must precede the preparation of these gifts, one also understands that offering oneself in service to establish one’s trustworthiness must certainly not come after reliance upon words. May you scholars strive to fulfill your aspirations and make good your words, following the renowned wise men of antiquity and matching their excellence. Then you will have no cause for shame in this selection, and would not the boundless glory of our state depend upon this [?]? This…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
舉也在外綜理則右布政使
馬坤叅政李徵叅議胡宗明
譚棨副使曹汴魏一恭丁湛
僉事俞維屛顧問陳善胡堯
臣防範則都指揮霍子麒梁
鳳周應禎劉恩至有事玆土
則戶部郎中歐禮主事趙世
===
錄工部主事張祥趙介夫南
京戶部主事黎遵訓若叅政
沈繼美副使陳與音以入
賀行亦始事服勞者也於法得
書
直隸廬州府無爲州儒學學
正劉鶴翔謹序
punctuated:
舉也，在外綜理則右布政使馬坤、叅政李徵、叅議胡宗明、譚棨、副使曹汴、魏一恭、丁湛、僉事俞維屛、顧問、陳善、胡堯臣；防範則都指揮霍子麒、梁鳳、周應禎、劉恩。至有事玆土，則戶部郎中歐禮、主事趙世錄、工部主事張祥、趙介夫、南京戶部主事黎遵訓。若叅政沈繼美、副使陳與音，以入賀行，亦始事服勞者也，於法得書。
直隸廬州府無爲州儒學學正劉鶴翔謹序。
translation_en:
…For this examination, those coordinating affairs outside the examination compound were Ma Kun, Right Administration Commissioner; Li Zheng, Administration Vice Commissioner; Hu Zongming and Tan Qi, Administration Assistant Commissioners; Cao Bian, Wei Yigong, and Ding Zhan, Surveillance Vice Commissioners; and Yu Weiping, Gu Wen, Chen Shan, and Hu Yaochen, Surveillance Assistant Commissioners. Security was handled by the Regional Military Commissioners Huo Ziqi, Liang Feng, Zhou Yingzhen, and Liu En. Those serving on official business in this locality included Ou Li, Director in the Ministry of Revenue; Zhao Shilu, Secretary in the same ministry; Zhang Xiang and Zhao Jiefu, Secretaries in the Ministry of Works; and Li Zunxun, Secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue. As for Shen Jimei, Administration Vice Commissioner, and Chen Yuyin, Surveillance Vice Commissioner, although they departed to offer congratulations at court, they too had labored at the outset of the undertaking and, under the prescribed rules, are entitled to be recorded here.
This preface is respectfully written by Liu Hexiang, Instructor in the Confucian School of Wuwei Subprefecture, Luzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region.

punctuated:
直隸大名府濬縣儒學教諭林紀〔貞憲，福建閩縣人，庚子貢士〕。江西饒州府德興縣儒學教諭吳紳〔克服，福建莆田縣人，丁酉貢士〕。福建漳州府平和縣儒學教諭廖瑚〔邦美，廣東海陽縣人，癸卯貢士〕。

浙江等處承宣布政使司經歷司經歷梁景乾〔道行，山西樂平縣人，監生〕。浙江等處提刑按察司經歷司知事高景文〔宗顯，江西饒州衞人，監生〕。

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
金華府蘭谿縣知縣李𢖟〔元韜直隸上海縣人丁未進士〕

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
其疑
惟天聰明惟聖時憲惟臣欽若惟民從乂
次三曰農用八政次四曰協用五紀
弘敷五典式和民則
詩
羔羊之皮素絲五紽退食自公委蛇委蛇
羔羊之革素絲五緎委蛇委蛇自公退
食羔羊之縫素絲五總委蛇委蛇退食
自公
===
如竹苞矣如松茂矣
瑟彼玉瓚黃流在中豈弟君子福祿攸降
湯孫奏假綏我思成鞉鼓淵淵嘒嘒管聲
旣和且平依我磬聲於赫湯孫穆穆厥
聲
春秋
夏六月邢遷于夷儀 齊師宋師曹師城
邢〔僖公元年〕
春王正月公會齊侯宋公陳侯衞侯鄭伯
punctuated:
其疑。

惟天聰明，惟聖時憲，惟臣欽若，惟民從乂。

次三曰農用八政，次四曰協用五紀。

弘敷五典，式和民則。

詩

羔羊之皮，素絲五紽。退食自公，委蛇委蛇。羔羊之革，素絲五緎。委蛇委蛇，自公退食。羔羊之縫，素絲五總。委蛇委蛇，退食自公。

如竹苞矣，如松茂矣。

瑟彼玉瓚，黃流在中。豈弟君子，福祿攸降。

湯孫奏假，綏我思成。鞉鼓淵淵，嘒嘒管聲。旣和且平，依我磬聲。於赫湯孫，穆穆厥聲。

春秋

夏六月，邢遷于夷儀。齊師、宋師、曹師城邢。〔僖公元年〕

春王正月，公會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衞侯、鄭伯
translation_en:
…their doubts.

Heaven is discerning and clear-sighted; the sage takes this as his model; ministers reverently follow it; and the people submit to good order.

The third is the diligent application of the eight measures of government; the fourth is the harmonious application of the five divisions of time.

Spread widely the teachings of the five human relationships, thereby bringing harmony to the people's rules of conduct.

Book of Odes

The lambskin robe, with five skeins of white silk! Retiring from public duty to dine, at ease, at ease. The lambskin hide, with five seams of white silk! At ease, at ease, retiring from public duty to dine. The lambskin's stitching, with five bundles of white silk! At ease, at ease, retiring from public duty to dine.

Like bamboo growing thickly, like pine flourishing.

Splendid is that jade libation ladle, with the golden sacrificial liquor within. Upon the gracious and joyful gentleman descend blessings and emoluments.

Tang's descendant comes forward in worship; grant us peace and fulfill our wishes. The hand drums and great drums sound deeply; the pipes ring clearly. Harmonious and balanced, they accord with the sound of our stone chimes. Ah, illustrious is Tang's descendant; solemn is his music.

Spring and Autumn Annals

In summer, in the sixth month, Xing moved to Yiyi. The armies of Qi, Song, and Cao built walls for Xing. 〔First year of Duke Xi.〕

In spring, in the first month of the royal calendar, the duke met with the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, and the Earl of Zheng…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
論
合虛與氣有性之名
詔誥表內科一道
擬漢令郡國舉孝廉各一人詔元光元年
擬唐以馬周為中書舍人誥貞觀十二年
擬宋以唐介參知政事謝表熙寧元年
判語五條
官員赴任過限
人戶以籍為定
===
致祭祀典神祇
私越冒度關津
脩理橋梁道路
第叁場
策五道
問先王以詩為教其用甚大孔子論詩可
以興今所刪三百篇具在風旨可想見
矣皇極之君以其躬行于上者敷衍為
言使人反復吟咏得其情性之正而天
punctuated:
論
合虛與氣，有性之名。

詔誥表內科一道。
擬漢令郡國舉孝廉各一人詔，元光元年。
擬唐以馬周為中書舍人誥，貞觀十二年。
擬宋以唐介參知政事謝表，熙寧元年。

判語五條
官員赴任過限。
人戶以籍為定。
致祭祀典神祇。
私越冒度關津。
脩理橋梁道路。

第叁場
策五道
問：先王以詩為教，其用甚大。孔子論詩，可以興。今所刪三百篇具在，風旨可想見矣。皇極之君，以其躬行于上者敷衍為言，使人反復吟咏，得其情性之正，而天

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
經十經十二經十三經是數者孰爲最
要而其義果同于史歟世傳三史遠矣
今則槩稱諸史或又益爲十二史十七
史十八史十九史二十一史是數者孰
爲最善而其義果同于經歟學者不明
乎經固不可以治史不明乎史亦不可
以翼經然經學重五教而慎三岐史學
耻五難而貴三長他如五行四時之分
配五志三科之異釋亦嘗究心矣乎諸
===
士皆强學志道以待問者尚茂言之毋
略
問慎擇長吏理人之要術也三代而降吏
治莫盛於兩漢然攷循吏列傳爲史氏
所稱談者西漢自文翁而下僅六人東
漢自衞颯而下僅十二人何循良之不
可多見也豈秉筆者去取之過嚴歟夫
傳以循吏爲名意當時以廉能相雄長
而負鷹鸇之望者固例不得錄也史氏
punctuated:
經、十經、十二經、十三經，是數者孰爲最要，而其義果同于史歟？世傳三史遠矣，今則槩稱諸史，或又益爲十二史、十七史、十八史、十九史、二十一史，是數者孰爲最善，而其義果同于經歟？學者不明乎經，固不可以治史；不明乎史，亦不可以翼經。然經學重五教而慎三岐，史學耻五難而貴三長。他如五行四時之分配、五志三科之異釋，亦嘗究心矣乎？諸士皆强學志道以待問者，尚茂言之，毋略。

問：慎擇長吏，理人之要術也。三代而降，吏治莫盛於兩漢。然攷《循吏列傳》，爲史氏所稱談者，西漢自文翁而下僅六人，東漢自衞颯而下僅十二人，何循良之不可多見也？豈秉筆者去取之過嚴歟？夫傳以循吏爲名，意當時以廉能相雄長，而負鷹鸇之望者，固例不得錄也。史氏
translation_en:
…Classics, the Ten Classics, the Twelve Classics, and the Thirteen Classics: which of these groupings is the most essential, and are their underlying principles indeed the same as those of the histories? The Three Histories have long been transmitted. Nowadays, however, people speak collectively of the various histories, or expand their number to twelve, seventeen, eighteen, nineteen, or twenty-one. Which of these groupings is the best, and are their underlying principles indeed the same as those of the Classics? Scholars who do not understand the Classics certainly cannot study the histories; those who do not understand the histories likewise cannot use them to elucidate the Classics. Yet classical scholarship prizes the Five Teachings and guards against the Three Divergences, while historical scholarship regards the Five Difficulties as shortcomings to be avoided and values the Three Strengths. As for such other matters as the correspondences between the Five Phases and the four seasons, and the differing interpretations of the Five Aims and the Three Categories [?], have you ever investigated these carefully? You gentlemen all study diligently and aspire to the Way, ready to answer questions. Elaborate fully upon these matters; do not be cursory.

Question: Carefully selecting senior local officials is an essential method of governing the people. Since the Three Dynasties, official administration has never flourished more than under the Western and Eastern Han. Yet, examining the Biographies of Exemplary Officials, we find that those praised by the historians number only six in the Western Han, beginning with Wen Weng, and only twelve in the Eastern Han, beginning with Wei Sa. Why were exemplary and benevolent officials so rarely to be found? Could those who wielded the historian’s brush have been too strict in deciding whom to include and exclude? Since these biographies bear the title “Exemplary Officials,” presumably those who at the time vied for preeminence in integrity and ability, but had a reputation for hawklike severity, were as a rule ineligible for inclusion. The historians…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
有除戶調絹綿者有蠲度支鹽鐵者有
免官司債負和買役錢者是皆不能無
經費也何以能不匱歟在當時民亦實
受其惠歟夫積久負欠每年帶納一分
以為便民矣何以有豐年不如凶年之
論民窮賦重盡數蠲除而困猶未甦也
何以有催理九分遷延一分以待蠲放
之說豈膏澤之沛固不足恃歟抑其間
亦有不容槩免者歟今年淫雨為災兩
===
浙特甚遠近洶洶行有艱食之憂苟有
以佐百姓裨
國計使兩全而無害固有位者所樂聞也諸
士目擊時事必籌之熟矣願詳以告我
punctuated: 有除戶調絹綿者，有蠲度支鹽鐵者，有免官司債負、和買役錢者，是皆不能無經費也，何以能不匱歟？在當時，民亦實受其惠歟？夫積久負欠，每年帶納一分，以為便民矣，何以有豐年不如凶年之論？民窮賦重，盡數蠲除，而困猶未甦也，何以有催理九分、遷延一分以待蠲放之說？豈膏澤之沛固不足恃歟？抑其間亦有不容槩免者歟？今年淫雨為災，兩浙特甚，遠近洶洶，行有艱食之憂。苟有以佐百姓、裨國計，使兩全而無害，固有位者所樂聞也。諸士目擊時事，必籌之熟矣，願詳以告我。
translation_en:
…There were those who abolished household levies of silk cloth and silk floss, those who remitted fiscal imposts on salt and iron, and those who waived debts owed to government offices, compulsory purchase obligations, and service payments. All these measures involved revenue needed for government expenditure; how could they avoid a shortfall? Did the people at the time actually receive the benefits?

As for long-standing arrears, collecting one tenth each year along with current payments was considered a convenience to the people. Why, then, was it said that a year of plenty was worse than a year of dearth? When the people were impoverished and taxes burdensome, even remission of the full amount did not relieve their distress. Why, then, was there talk of pressing for collection of nine tenths while delaying the remaining tenth to await remission? Could it be that even abundant imperial beneficence could not be relied upon? Or were there obligations among these that could not properly be remitted indiscriminately?

This year, prolonged rains have caused disaster, especially severe in the two Zhe regions. Near and far, people are alarmed, and food shortages are impending. If there are means to aid the common people and benefit state finances, securing both without injury to either, those in office would certainly welcome hearing them. You gentlemen have witnessed current affairs firsthand and must have considered them thoroughly. I ask you to explain them to me in detail.

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
可作哲矣人不能無聽也惟聰而後能聽遠必
思去其壅焉而聰可作謀矣色見於面而或失
則厲則思溫焉使卽之而可親也貌著於身而
或失則慢則思恭焉使望之而可象也以言者
尚其忠不忠則欺必思由衷之誠而言爲有物
矣以事者尚其敬不敬則肆必思主一之實而
事爲有則矣明不至則疑生而疑不可蓄也則
思致師友之助而辨之有弗明乎心不平則忿
生而忿不可逞也則思爲身親之累而懲之有
===
弗力乎人情莫不欲得而欲不可從也則思以
定其取舍之極而務協於義焉又豈肯苟得而
已乎夫是九者而愼思之則事必研諸慮固非
罔焉而無所于求思不出乎身亦非泛焉而無
益于得君子作聖之功固如是哉雖然君子固
不可無思而思亦不可過也思而過焉則强探
苦索而於視聽言動之間問難取與之際反將
有所惑而不得其當者矣故思者人心之用而
無思者又人心之本體也易不云乎天下何思
punctuated:
可作哲矣。人不能無聽也，惟聰而後能聽遠，必思去其壅焉，而聰可作謀矣。色見於面，而或失則厲，則思溫焉，使卽之而可親也；貌著於身，而或失則慢，則思恭焉，使望之而可象也。以言者尚其忠，不忠則欺，必思由衷之誠，而言爲有物矣；以事者尚其敬，不敬則肆，必思主一之實，而事爲有則矣。明不至則疑生，而疑不可蓄也，則思致師友之助，而辨之有弗明乎？心不平則忿生，而忿不可逞也，則思爲身親之累，而懲之有弗力乎？人情莫不欲得，而欲不可從也，則思以定其取舍之極，而務協於義焉，又豈肯苟得而已乎？夫是九者而愼思之，則事必研諸慮，固非罔焉而無所于求；思不出乎身，亦非泛焉而無益于得。君子作聖之功，固如是哉！
雖然，君子固不可無思，而思亦不可過也。思而過焉，則强探苦索，而於視聽言動之間、問難取與之際，反將有所惑而不得其當者矣。故思者，人心之用，而無思者，又人心之本體也。《易》不云乎：「天下何思
translation_en:
…can thus become wisdom. People cannot do without hearing; only with keen hearing can they hear what is distant. They must therefore think of removing whatever obstructs it, so that keenness of hearing can become sound deliberation. Expression appears in the face, and when it goes awry it becomes harsh; one must therefore think of warmth, so that others find one approachable when they draw near. Demeanor manifests itself in the person, and when it goes awry it becomes disrespectful; one must therefore think of reverence, so that others find one worthy of emulation when they look upon one. In speaking, what matters is sincerity; without sincerity there is deception. One must therefore think of truthfulness that comes from the heart, so that one’s words have substance. In acting, what matters is attentiveness; without attentiveness there is heedlessness. One must therefore think of genuinely maintaining singleness of purpose, so that one’s actions follow a standard. When understanding falls short, doubts arise, and doubts must not be allowed to accumulate. If one thinks of seeking help from teachers and friends, can one fail to clarify them through discrimination? When the heart is unsettled, anger arises, and anger must not be indulged. If one thinks of the trouble it brings upon oneself and one’s parents, can one fail to exert oneself in restraining it? Everyone naturally desires gain, yet desire must not be followed unchecked. One must therefore think of establishing the ultimate standard for what to accept and what to reject, striving to accord with righteousness. How, then, could one be content merely to obtain something by improper means? If one reflects carefully upon these nine matters, every affair will be examined in thought: one will certainly not be bewildered, with nothing to seek. Such reflection does not stray beyond oneself, nor is it so diffuse as to contribute nothing to attainment. Such indeed is the work by which the gentleman becomes a sage!
Nevertheless, although the gentleman cannot dispense with reflection, reflection must not be excessive. If it goes too far, one probes forcibly and searches painfully; amid seeing, hearing, speaking, and acting, and in questioning, disputation, taking, and giving, one will instead become confused and fail to arrive at what is appropriate. Thus reflection is the functioning of the human heart-mind, while the absence of reflection is its original substance. Does not the Book of Changes say: “What does all under Heaven have to think about…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
其化功之相似者耳若論其極則聖人者蓋有
出入造化而爲天地立心者也使天地而非至
誠以相之則無以成其能而造化不幾於息乎
故無心成化者天地也順事無情者聖人也此
裁成輔相所以賛化育之所不及而得一以清
寧者凡以中和之所致也不然何以曰聖人天
地之用
君子深造之以道欲其自得之也
邵畯
===
同考試官教諭廖批講自得處親切有味
同考試官教諭鄭批觀子之文幾於自得者
考試官學正馮批舂容可誦
考試官學正劉批說理明盡
大賢論君子學循其序者欲會理於其心也夫
理得於心其機固不容强也君子造之深而必
以道者非有見於此哉孟子之意蓋曰天下之
理本具於一心人之爲學亦求有得於心而已
奚不觀之君子乎君子見天下之道無終窮而
punctuated:
其化功之相似者耳。若論其極，則聖人者蓋有出入造化而爲天地立心者也。使天地而非至誠以相之，則無以成其能，而造化不幾於息乎？故無心成化者，天地也；順事無情者，聖人也。此裁成輔相所以賛化育之所不及，而得一以清寧者，凡以中和之所致也。不然，何以曰聖人天地之用？

君子深造之以道，欲其自得之也。
邵畯

同考試官教諭廖批：講自得處親切有味。
同考試官教諭鄭批：觀子之文，幾於自得者。
考試官學正馮批：舂容可誦。
考試官學正劉批：說理明盡。

大賢論君子學循其序者，欲會理於其心也。夫理得於心，其機固不容强也。君子造之深而必以道者，非有見於此哉？孟子之意蓋曰：天下之理，本具於一心；人之爲學，亦求有得於心而已。奚不觀之君子乎？君子見天下之道無終窮而
translation_en:
…merely the similarity of their transformative achievements. If we discuss their ultimate attainment, however, the sage moves within and beyond the processes of creation and establishes a mind for Heaven and Earth. If Heaven and Earth lacked utmost sincerity to assist them, they would have no means of fulfilling their capacities; would creation not then come close to ceasing? Thus, Heaven and Earth accomplish transformation without conscious intent; the sage responds to affairs without personal feelings. By shaping and completing, assisting and supporting, the sage supplements what transforming and nurturing cannot accomplish, attaining unity and thereby clarity and tranquility. All this is brought about by equilibrium and harmony. Otherwise, why say that the sage is the functioning of Heaven and Earth?

“The gentleman pursues profound attainment by following the Way, wishing to grasp it for himself.”
Shao Jun

Associate Examiner Liao, Instructor, comments: “The discussion of grasping it for oneself is intimate and meaningful.”
Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: “Judging by your writing, you have nearly grasped it for yourself.”
Examiner Feng, School Rector, comments: “Unhurried and ample in expression, it rewards recitation.”
Examiner Liu, School Rector, comments: “The exposition of principle is clear and exhaustive.”

The great worthy explains that the gentleman follows the proper sequence in learning because he wishes to apprehend principle within his own mind. For when principle is grasped in the mind, the workings by which this happens certainly cannot be forced. Is it not an insight into this that leads the gentleman to pursue profound attainment necessarily by following the Way? Mencius’s meaning is, in essence: The principles of all under Heaven are inherently present within the single mind; in learning, one seeks only to grasp them within one’s own mind. Why not look to the gentleman? The gentleman sees that the Way of all under Heaven has neither end nor limit, and…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
其學也有成法志向期於上達夫固進進不已
矣而先後之有等必積累以崇其功德業貴於
大成夫固乾乾匪懈矣而始終之不紊必漸次
以致其力時敏而持之以遜志之益所以求精
其義者蓋安其節焉而不蹈夫雜施之病果行
而主之以育德之心所以求踐其實者蓋循其
方焉而不徇夫欲速之私夫是之謂深造以道
也而其心何以哉蓋至理在我本不可以致思
將由此以存之使持循有地而功要於專一者
===
自神悟於畜極之餘亦不可以助長將由此以
順之使據守有基而業定於有恒者自化融於
默成之後其知也非强探也優游以需其進而
日游息焉殆理與心涵極於聞見之俱泯者矣
其行也非矯拂也積久以俟其至而日涵濡焉
殆心與理一極於表裏之俱徹者矣此君子欲
其自得所以深造必以道也不然速成亦可以
自幸而奚必漸進之若是耶吁學者于是而默
會焉亦可以自得於心矣抑是學也吾嘗於顔
punctuated: 其學也有成法。志向期於上達，夫固進進不已矣，而先後之有等，必積累以崇其功；德業貴於大成，夫固乾乾匪懈矣，而始終之不紊，必漸次以致其力。時敏而持之以遜志之益，所以求精其義者，蓋安其節焉，而不蹈夫雜施之病；果行而主之以育德之心，所以求踐其實者，蓋循其方焉，而不徇夫欲速之私。夫是之謂深造以道也。而其心何以哉？蓋至理在我，本不可以致思，將由此以存之，使持循有地，而功要於專一者，自神悟於畜極之餘；亦不可以助長，將由此以順之，使據守有基，而業定於有恒者，自化融於默成之後。其知也，非强探也，優游以需其進，而日游息焉，殆理與心涵，極於聞見之俱泯者矣；其行也，非矯拂也，積久以俟其至，而日涵濡焉，殆心與理一，極於表裏之俱徹者矣。此君子欲其自得，所以深造必以道也。不然，速成亦可以自幸，而奚必漸進之若是耶？吁！學者于是而默會焉，亦可以自得於心矣。抑是學也，吾嘗於顔
translation_en:
…his learning follows established methods. His aspirations aim at reaching higher understanding, and he certainly advances without ceasing. Yet because earlier and later stages have their proper order, he must build up his achievement through accumulation. In cultivating virtue, he prizes great accomplishment, and he certainly strives tirelessly. Yet to preserve order from beginning to end, he must apply his efforts by gradual stages. Diligent in timely study, he sustains it with the benefit of a humble disposition. In seeking thereby to refine his understanding of what is right, he rests content with the proper stages and avoids the fault of indiscriminate application. Resolute in conduct, he directs it with a mind intent on nurturing virtue. In seeking thereby to put its substance into practice, he follows the proper methods and does not indulge a selfish desire for quick results. This is what is called advancing deeply through the proper Way.

And what is the intention in his heart [?]? The utmost principle resides within oneself; it cannot originally be reached merely by deliberate thought. Through this approach he will preserve it, giving his sustained practice firm ground. When his effort is concentrated on single-minded application, profound understanding will arise spontaneously once accumulation has reached its fullness. Nor can its growth be forced. Through this approach he will follow its natural course, giving his steadfast adherence a foundation. When his undertaking is secured through constancy, transformation and integration will arise spontaneously after silent maturation.

His knowing is no forced probing: at ease, he waits for its advance and daily dwells and rests within it. Principle and mind become so deeply immersed in one another that distinctions derived from hearing and seeing alike disappear. His conduct is no coercive correction: through long accumulation he awaits its consummation and daily lets himself be steeped in it. Mind and principle become one, reaching the point where both outward and inward are thoroughly transparent. It is because the gentleman wishes to attain understanding for himself that his deep advancement must follow the proper Way. Otherwise, he could congratulate himself on quick accomplishment; why would he need to advance gradually in this manner? Ah! If learners silently comprehend this, they too can attain understanding within their own hearts. As for this learning, I have found illumination in Yan…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
曾而有得焉觀其卓爾之見本於博約之兼進
而一貫之唯非眞積力久何以得此孟子私淑
於曾子者也故於此章發之而美大聖神之極
又不越乎善信之間皆自得之眞也不然卽心
見性竊附於自得者不幾於執似以失其眞耶
此又學者之所當深辨
易
貞固足以幹事
周詩
===
同考試官敎諭林批貞固二字總是說智發
明精確者無踰此篇
考試官學正馮批簡明
考試官學正劉批理精辭健
君子全天德之智而致用之本立矣蓋事無定
用而智之在我者其本也君子知正而固守之
有不足以爲事之幹乎文言申乾彖傳之意蓋
曰人性之智也固得於天道之貞也君子法天
以成其智其惟貞固乎蓋天下之道正而已矣
punctuated:
曾而有得焉。觀其卓爾之見，本於博約之兼進，而一貫之唯，非眞積力久，何以得此？孟子私淑於曾子者也，故於此章發之，而美大聖神之極，又不越乎善信之間，皆自得之眞也。不然，卽心見性，竊附於自得者，不幾於執似以失其眞耶？此又學者之所當深辨。
易
貞固足以幹事
周詩
同考試官敎諭林批：「貞固二字，總是說智，發明精確者，無踰此篇。」
考試官學正馮批：「簡明。」
考試官學正劉批：「理精辭健。」
君子全天德之智，而致用之本立矣。蓋事無定用，而智之在我者，其本也。君子知正而固守之，有不足以爲事之幹乎？文言申乾彖傳之意，蓋曰：人性之智也，固得於天道之貞也。君子法天以成其智，其惟貞固乎？蓋天下之道，正而已矣。
translation_en:
…and Zeng, I have gained an understanding of this. Consider how Yan’s vision of what stood loftily before him was rooted in advancing both broad learning and restraint through ritual. As for Zeng’s assent to the single thread running through the Way, how could he have attained this without genuine accumulation and prolonged effort? Mengzi learned indirectly from Zengzi’s legacy. Thus he expounded this in the present chapter. Even the highest attainments of being admirable, great, sagely, and spiritually unfathomable do not extend beyond goodness and sincerity: all are genuine instances of attaining understanding for oneself. Otherwise, would those who speak of perceiving one’s nature immediately within the mind and presumptuously associate this with self-attainment not come close to grasping a semblance and losing the truth? This, too, is something students must distinguish carefully.
Book of Changes
“Correctness and firmness suffice to manage affairs”
Zhou Shi
Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: “The two words ‘correctness’ and ‘firmness’ both concern wisdom. No essay surpasses this one in the precision of its elucidation.”
Examiner Feng, School Director, comments: “Concise and clear.”
Examiner Liu, School Director, comments: “Refined in reasoning and vigorous in expression.”
The gentleman fully realizes the wisdom belonging to Heaven’s virtue, and thereby establishes the foundation for putting it into practice. Affairs have no fixed requirements for action; the wisdom within us is their foundation. When the gentleman knows what is correct and firmly holds to it, could this fail to provide the mainstay for managing affairs? The Commentary on the Words of the Text elaborates the meaning of the Commentary on the Judgment for the Qian hexagram. Its point is that the wisdom of human nature is indeed derived from the correctness of Heaven’s Way. In taking Heaven as his model to perfect his wisdom, surely the gentleman relies upon correctness and firmness! For the Way of all under Heaven is simply correctness.

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
不在乾而在君子矣盡性之功其至矣乎雖然
此偏言智之一事耳專言之則智也者固合四
德而無不該者也學必先明諸心知所往而後
力行以求至言有序也大學論誠正以極於治
平必先諸格致而孟子亦以始條理爲智之事
非是之謂乎眞妄之際其幾甚微察之不精其
不以姑息爲仁殘忍爲義而繁縟爲禮者幾希
矣故知智之該乎四德而功之所當先也不然
何以曰進學則在致知
===
夫易廣矣大矣以言乎遠則不禦以言乎
邇則靜而正以言乎天地之間則備矣
陸夢熊
同考試官教諭林批形容易之廣大處渾融
典雅蓋邃於易者
考試官學正馮批有見者機軸自別
考試官學正劉批精潔
大傳贊易理之廣大隨在而無不足也蓋易者
理之所寓也舉遠近上下而理無不足焉其廣
punctuated:
不在乾而在君子矣。盡性之功，其至矣乎！雖然，此偏言智之一事耳。專言之，則智也者，固合四德而無不該者也。學必先明諸心，知所往，而後力行以求至，言有序也。《大學》論誠正以極於治平，必先諸格致，而《孟子》亦以始條理爲智之事，非是之謂乎？眞妄之際，其幾甚微，察之不精，其不以姑息爲仁、殘忍爲義，而繁縟爲禮者，幾希矣。故知智之該乎四德，而功之所當先也。不然，何以曰：「進學則在致知」？

夫《易》，廣矣，大矣！以言乎遠，則不禦；以言乎邇，則靜而正；以言乎天地之間，則備矣。
陸夢熊
同考試官教諭林批：「形容《易》之廣大處，渾融典雅，蓋邃於《易》者。」
考試官學正馮批：「有見者，機軸自別。」
考試官學正劉批：「精潔。」

《大傳》贊《易》理之廣大，隨在而無不足也。蓋《易》者，理之所寓也。舉遠近上下，而理無不足焉。其廣
translation_en:
…lies not in Qian but in the gentleman. Has the work of fully realizing one’s nature not reached its utmost here? Nevertheless, this speaks of wisdom only in one particular respect. Taken in its comprehensive sense, wisdom embraces all four virtues, leaving nothing outside its scope. In learning, one must first attain clarity in one’s mind and know where one is going, and then practice earnestly to reach that destination: this means that there is a proper sequence. The Great Learning discusses making intentions sincere and rectifying the mind, culminating in ordering the state and bringing peace to the world, but necessarily places investigating things and extending knowledge first. The Mencius likewise treats beginning the ordered sequence as the work of wisdom. Is this not what is meant? At the boundary between truth and delusion, the incipient distinction is exceedingly subtle. Unless one examines it precisely, scarcely anyone can avoid mistaking indulgence for benevolence, cruelty for righteousness, and elaborate formalities for ritual propriety. Thus we know that wisdom embraces the four virtues and that work upon it must come first. Otherwise, why say, “Advancement in learning lies in extending knowledge”?

“How broad and great is the Book of Changes! Speaking of what is distant, it knows no bounds; speaking of what is near, it is still and correct; speaking of what lies between Heaven and Earth, it encompasses everything.”
Lu Mengxiong
Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: “His portrayal of the breadth and greatness of the Book of Changes is harmonious, integrated, and classically elegant. He must be deeply versed in the Changes.”
Examiner Feng, School Instructor, comments: “A writer with insight naturally has a distinctive approach.”
Examiner Liu, School Instructor, comments: “Refined and clean.”

The Great Commentary praises the breadth and greatness of the principles of the Book of Changes: wherever they are found, they lack nothing. For the Changes is where principle resides. Taking together the distant and the near, what is above and what is below, principle is nowhere deficient. Its breadth…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
大也爲何如哉大傳之意蓋曰易之爲書也有
卦爻以立其體孰不以爲法象云爾矣有變占
以顯其用亦孰不以爲卜筮云爾矣然妙道精
義之所存實充周而不窮貫通而無間其諸廣
大矣乎何以言之彼遠有所禦則其勢有限謂
之廣大未也易則充足有餘言乎遠而其理周
焉放諸千萬里而莫知其止也行乎千萬世而
莫知其終也流動貫徹蓋窮其所至而無有底
極者矣夫孰得而禦之邇有所遺則其機易息
===
謂之廣大亦未也易則萬一各正言乎邇而其
理存焉索諸几席而無物不有也察諸瞬息而
無時不然也絪縕詳密蓋不待安排而自無滲
漏者矣有不靜而正乎至於天地之間卑高散
殊至不可齊也一有弗備其道窮矣又何以爲
廣大乎易則峻極之體察兩間而無外發育之
神普萬物而不遺在天成象易理昭著於上也
在地成形易理呈露於下也充塞乎天地之間
而何有於不備乎夫曰遠曰邇曰天地之間天
punctuated: 大也，爲何如哉？大傳之意蓋曰：易之爲書也，有卦爻以立其體，孰不以爲法象云爾矣？有變占以顯其用，亦孰不以爲卜筮云爾矣？然妙道精義之所存，實充周而不窮，貫通而無間，其諸廣大矣乎！何以言之？彼遠有所禦，則其勢有限，謂之廣大，未也。易則充足有餘，言乎遠而其理周焉。放諸千萬里而莫知其止也，行乎千萬世而莫知其終也，流動貫徹，蓋窮其所至而無有底極者矣。夫孰得而禦之？邇有所遺，則其機易息，謂之廣大，亦未也。易則萬一各正，言乎邇而其理存焉。索諸几席而無物不有也，察諸瞬息而無時不然也，絪縕詳密，蓋不待安排而自無滲漏者矣。有不靜而正乎？至於天地之間，卑高散殊，至不可齊也。一有弗備，其道窮矣，又何以爲廣大乎？易則峻極之體察兩間而無外，發育之神普萬物而不遺。在天成象，易理昭著於上也；在地成形，易理呈露於下也。充塞乎天地之間，而何有於不備乎？夫曰遠，曰邇，曰天地之間，天
translation_en:
…how great, then, is its vastness? The meaning of the Great Commentary is roughly this: as a book, the Changes has hexagrams and lines that establish its substance. Who would not regard these as merely patterns and images? It has transformations and prognostications that manifest its function. Who would not likewise regard these as merely divination by turtle shell and milfoil stalks? Yet the subtle Way and refined principles lodged within it truly fill everything without exhaustion and penetrate everything without interruption. Surely it is vast and great!

How can this be explained? If something encounters an obstruction in reaching far, its scope is limited; it cannot yet be called vast and great. The Changes, however, possesses abundant fullness: speaking of the distant, its principles encompass everything. Extend it over thousands upon thousands of li, and no one knows where it stops; carry it through thousands upon thousands of generations, and no one knows where it ends. Flowing and penetrating throughout, it reaches everywhere without any ultimate limit. Who could obstruct it? If something leaves anything out nearby, its animating impulse is easily brought to a halt; it likewise cannot yet be called vast and great. In the Changes, however, the myriad and the one each find their proper order [?]: speaking of the near, its principles are present there. Seek them among tables and mats, and there is no object in which they are absent; examine them from instant to instant, and there is no moment when this is not so. Interwoven, intricate, and close-knit, they naturally leave no gaps without requiring deliberate arrangement. Could they fail to be still and correct?

As for what lies between Heaven and Earth, the low and the high are dispersed and differentiated, utterly impossible to make uniform. If even one thing were not encompassed, its Way would reach its limit; how, then, could it be vast and great? But the supremely lofty substance of the Changes is manifest throughout the space between the two, leaving nothing outside it; its numinous power of generation and nurture extends universally to the myriad things, omitting none. In Heaven it forms images: the principles of the Changes shine clearly above. On Earth it forms shapes: the principles of the Changes appear openly below. Filling the space between Heaven and Earth, how could it fail to encompass anything? Now, it speaks of the distant, the near, and what lies between Heaven and Earth. Heaven…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
比德者矣何也臣之心同秉此理之公者也君
以天之心爲心矣臣寧不以君之心爲心乎言
有民也以從上爲欲者也夫惟人君之心與天
無二矣是以表儀所樹庶民興焉從厥攸好而
相忘于天則之安錫汝保極而同歸于化中之
盛以順天之心順君無有淫朋者矣何也民之
心同具此理之公者也君旣以天之理自處矣
民孰敢自以其心爲心乎吁聖人至公至神之
化如此憲天以爲治者尚加之意哉大抵天聰
===
明自我民聰明天人一理通達無間者也人君
不以民視民而以天視之則憲天之道當無不
盡矣而傳說告高宗又推本於惟厥攸居之一
言乃知心爲政事之本所以端天下臣民之極
也其旨深哉後之人有岐爲天職天政天養天
情天功之說者其亦未聞大道之要者歟
次三曰農用八政次四曰協用五紀
邵晙
同考試官教諭廖批題旨博大講究精詳大□
punctuated:
比德者矣。何也？臣之心，同秉此理之公者也。君以天之心爲心矣，臣寧不以君之心爲心乎？言有民也，以從上爲欲者也。夫惟人君之心與天無二矣，是以表儀所樹，庶民興焉，從厥攸好而相忘于天則之安，錫汝保極而同歸于化中之盛。以順天之心順君，無有淫朋者矣。何也？民之心，同具此理之公者也。君旣以天之理自處矣，民孰敢自以其心爲心乎？吁！聖人至公至神之化如此，憲天以爲治者尚加之意哉！大抵天聰明，自我民聰明，天人一理，通達無間者也。人君不以民視民而以天視之，則憲天之道當無不盡矣。而傳說告高宗，又推本於惟厥攸居之一言，乃知心爲政事之本，所以端天下臣民之極也。其旨深哉！後之人有岐爲天職、天政、天養、天情、天功之說者，其亦未聞大道之要者歟？

次三曰農用八政，次四曰協用五紀。
邵晙
同考試官教諭廖批：題旨博大，講究精詳，大□
translation_en:
…are those who accord with him in virtue. Why is this? The hearts of ministers alike partake of the impartiality of this principle. Since the ruler takes Heaven’s heart as his own, how could ministers fail to take the ruler’s heart as theirs? As for the people, their desire is to follow those above them. Precisely because the ruler’s heart is at one with Heaven, wherever he establishes an example, the common people are stirred to emulate it. Following what he cherishes, they rest so naturally within Heaven’s norms that they cease to be conscious of them. “Bestow upon them your preservation of the supreme standard,” and all alike attain the flourishing condition of transformation through the mean. With the same hearts that follow Heaven, they follow the ruler, and there are no wayward cliques. Why is this? The hearts of the people alike possess the impartiality of this principle. Since the ruler conducts himself according to Heaven’s principle, who among the people would dare make his own heart his sole guide? Ah! Such is the utterly impartial and wondrous transforming influence of the sage. Let those who model their government on Heaven give further thought to this! In general, “Heaven’s hearing and sight derive from the hearing and sight of our people.” Heaven and humanity share one principle, communicating without any separation. If the ruler regards the people as Heaven, then he will fully realize the way of taking Heaven as his model. Moreover, in his admonition to Gaozong, Fu Yue traced matters back to their root in the single statement, “It depends on where one’s heart abides.” Thus we know that the heart is the foundation of government and the means of setting aright the supreme standard for all ministers and people under Heaven. How profound this meaning is! Might those of later ages who divided it into separate accounts of Heaven’s offices, Heaven’s government, Heaven’s nurture, Heaven’s dispositions, and Heaven’s accomplishments likewise have failed to hear the essentials of the Great Way?

“Third: diligently employ the eight affairs of government. Fourth: harmoniously employ the five regulators of time.”
Shao Jun
Associate Examiner Liao, Instructor, comments: “The purport of the topic is broad and comprehensive; the examination of it is precise and detailed; greatly [?]…”

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之優者
同考試官教諭鄭批發揮敬天勤民之義非
理學不能道此
考試官學正馮批說理明暢
考試官學正劉批得旨
聖人第疇之列于三四者取夫勤民敬天之義
焉蓋八政五紀均之爲君道也人君位天人之
兩間而厚之協之豈非治天下之大法也哉箕
子述洪範九疇以告武王若曰隱者理也顯者
===
象也而變化于聖人之心禹旣第之以五行五
事之疇矣龜文之三其數則出乎震位於奇也
禹也默而契之因第其數曰斯疇也其配之以
八政乎蓋民之五事旣具矣民生所資必賴政
而後生焉八政者人之所以因乎天者也厚民
之意本于天而有相之道存乎我必體惟天惠
民之心而凡因天時以興地利者先重夫小人
之依求惟辟奉天之實而凡定法制以要始終
者皆欲奠斯民之麗謂之曰農則知利用厚生
punctuated:
之優者。
同考試官教諭鄭批：發揮敬天勤民之義，非理學不能道此。
考試官學正馮批：說理明暢。
考試官學正劉批：得旨。
聖人第疇之列于三四者，取夫勤民敬天之義焉。蓋八政五紀，均之爲君道也。人君位天人之兩間，而厚之協之，豈非治天下之大法也哉？箕子述洪範九疇以告武王，若曰：隱者理也，顯者象也，而變化于聖人之心。禹旣第之以五行五事之疇矣。龜文之三，其數則出乎震，位於奇也。禹也默而契之，因第其數曰：斯疇也，其配之以八政乎？蓋民之五事旣具矣，民生所資，必賴政而後生焉。八政者，人之所以因乎天者也。厚民之意本于天，而有相之道存乎我。必體惟天惠民之心，而凡因天時以興地利者，先重夫小人之依；求惟辟奉天之實，而凡定法制以要始終者，皆欲奠斯民之麗。謂之曰農，則知利用厚生
translation_en:
…among the superior ones.
Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: “It develops the meaning of revering Heaven and diligently caring for the people. Without learning in the principles, one could not articulate this.”
Examiner Feng, School Instructor, comments: “The exposition of principle is clear and fluent.”
Examiner Liu, School Instructor, comments: “It grasps the purport.”
In placing these categories third and fourth, the sage drew upon the meaning of diligently caring for the people and revering Heaven. For the eight affairs of government and the five regulators of time alike constitute the way of the ruler. Standing between Heaven and humanity, the ruler enriches the people’s livelihood and harmonizes the regulators of time: are these not great methods for governing all under Heaven? Jizi expounded the nine categories of the Great Plan to instruct King Wu, as though saying: What is hidden is principle; what is manifest is its configuration; their transformations take place within the sage’s mind. Yu had already arranged the categories of the five agents and the five personal activities. As for the three in the markings on the tortoise shell, its number emerges in the position of the trigram Zhen and occupies an odd-numbered place. Yu silently apprehended its significance and accordingly assigned its numerical order, saying: “Should this category not be matched with the eight affairs of government?” For once the people possess the five personal activities, the resources on which their livelihood depends must rely on government before they can be produced. The eight affairs of government are the means by which humanity follows Heaven. The intention to enrich the people’s livelihood originates in Heaven, while the means of assisting Heaven lie with me. One must embody Heaven’s intention to benefit the people; thus, in everything that follows Heaven’s seasons to develop the earth’s resources, priority is given to what ordinary people depend upon. One must seek the practical fulfillment of the sovereign’s service to Heaven; thus, all the establishment of laws and institutions to govern affairs from beginning to end aims to secure a settled place for these people. By calling this “diligent application,” one recognizes that making resources useful and enriching livelihood…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
農事開國詩書所稱康功田功豳風七月皆是
物也故曰帝王所傳心法之要蓋本諸此噫此
禹疇箕範所以得道統之傳也歟
詩
瑟彼玉瓚黃流在中豈弟君子福祿攸降
高克謙
同考試官教諭廖批篇中發明德福相因之
意詳盡取之
同考試官教諭劉批詞意雙暢咏歌文王之
===
德宛然在目是善說詩者
同考試官教諭張批得詩人之旨
考試官學正馮批醇正
考試官學正劉批雅健
詩人咏歌聖君之德必與其德盛而福自至焉
蓋德與福相因者也有是德即有是福矣文王
以之宜詩人咏歌以彰其盛歟其旨息蓋謂惟德
動天惟天眷德必得其福者必有其德者也盍
自我文王觀之彼瑟然之玉瓚黃流必在其中
punctuated:
農事開國，《詩》《書》所稱康功、田功，《豳風》七月，皆是物也。故曰帝王所傳心法之要，蓋本諸此。噫！此禹疇箕範所以得道統之傳也歟！
詩
瑟彼玉瓚，黃流在中。豈弟君子，福祿攸降。
高克謙
同考試官教諭廖批：篇中發明德福相因之意詳盡，取之。
同考試官教諭劉批：詞意雙暢，咏歌文王之德，宛然在目，是善說詩者。
同考試官教諭張批：得詩人之旨。
考試官學正馮批：醇正。
考試官學正劉批：雅健。
詩人咏歌聖君之德，必與其德盛而福自至焉。蓋德與福相因者也，有是德即有是福矣。文王以之，宜詩人咏歌以彰其盛歟！其旨息蓋謂惟德動天，惟天眷德，必得其福者，必有其德者也。盍自我文王觀之？彼瑟然之玉瓚，黃流必在其中。
translation_en:
…founding the state through agriculture. The achievements in securing well-being and cultivating the fields praised in the Odes and the Documents, and “The Seventh Month” in the “Airs of Bin,” all concern these matters. Thus it is said that the essentials of the teaching of the mind transmitted by emperors and kings are rooted in these things. Ah! Is this why Yu’s Categories and Jizi’s Great Plan received the transmission of the succession of the Way?
Odes
“Lustrous is that jade libation ladle, with yellow sacrificial wine within. The gracious and amiable lord is he upon whom blessings and emoluments descend.”
Gao Keqian
Comment by Associate Examiner Liao, Instructor: “The essay explains fully and thoroughly how virtue and blessings are causally connected. Accepted.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor: “Both expression and thought flow freely. In singing the praises of King Wen’s virtue, it brings him vividly before our eyes. This is someone skilled in interpreting the Odes.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “It captures the poet’s intent.”
Comment by Examiner Feng, School Instructor: “Pure and correct.”
Comment by Examiner Liu, School Instructor: “Elegant and vigorous.”
When the poet sings the praises of a sage ruler’s virtue, he invariably affirms [?] that the ruler’s virtue is abundant and blessings come of themselves. Virtue and blessings are causally connected: possessing such virtue, one possesses such blessings. King Wen exemplified this; was it not fitting that the poet should sing his praises to manifest his abundance? The purport [?] is that virtue alone moves Heaven, and Heaven cherishes virtue: whoever assuredly obtains such blessings must possess such virtue. Why not consider this through our King Wen? Within that lustrous jade libation ladle, yellow sacrificial wine must be present…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
矣是蓋溫潤之質自具夫居珍之體而鬱鬯之
薦式用乎美器之陳惟器味之相須而後有廟
之享假必物品之類聚而後裸將之禮成玉瓚
不與黃流期而黃流自注焉況我文王徽柔之
懿著而為容保之光純一之誠顯而為順應之
度肅肅之際雍雍寓焉有和樂而無拂戾翼翼
之中亹亹存焉有平易而無險僻信豈弟之君
子也福祿寧不下其躬乎是蓋盛德永貞之下
有以立昭受之基而有命旣集之餘誕膺夫聿
===
懷之慶螽斯之錫胤麟趾之肖賢凡所以厚于
身厚于家者福無不備也兔罝之多才漢廣之
弘化凡所以宜于臣宜于民者福罔不極也君
子不與福祿期而福祿自至矣是則天人之相
與也其幾雖微而德福之相須也其理有定詩
人有得於觀感之際其能已於咏歌也哉考之
洪範次九曰嚮用五福威用六極而必先之以
五行五事八政五紀以建皇極而三德稽疑庶
徵因之以見必作德以斂福而福澤不降於淫
punctuated: 矣。是蓋溫潤之質，自具夫居珍之體，而鬱鬯之薦，式用乎美器之陳。惟器味之相須，而後有廟之享假；必物品之類聚，而後裸將之禮成。玉瓚不與黃流期，而黃流自注焉。況我文王，徽柔之懿著而為容保之光，純一之誠顯而為順應之度。肅肅之際，雍雍寓焉，有和樂而無拂戾；翼翼之中，亹亹存焉，有平易而無險僻。信豈弟之君子也，福祿寧不下其躬乎？是蓋盛德永貞之下，有以立昭受之基；而有命旣集之餘，誕膺夫聿懷之慶。螽斯之錫胤，麟趾之肖賢，凡所以厚于身、厚于家者，福無不備也；兔罝之多才，漢廣之弘化，凡所以宜于臣、宜于民者，福罔不極也。君子不與福祿期，而福祿自至矣。是則天人之相與也，其幾雖微，而德福之相須也，其理有定。詩人有得於觀感之際，其能已於咏歌也哉？考之《洪範》，次九曰「嚮用五福，威用六極」，而必先之以五行、五事、八政、五紀，以建皇極，而三德、稽疑、庶徵因之，以見必作德以斂福，而福澤不降於淫
translation_en:
…indeed. This is because jade, by its warm and lustrous nature, inherently possesses the substance suited to holding precious things, while the offering of aromatic sacrificial wine requires the presentation of a beautiful vessel. Only when vessel and flavor complement one another can offerings be presented in the ancestral temple; only when the appropriate objects are assembled by kind can the rite of pouring the libation be completed. The jade libation ladle makes no appointment with the yellow wine, yet the yellow wine pours into it of itself. How much more is this true of our King Wen! His admirable gentleness manifests itself as the radiance of his encompassing protection; his undivided sincerity reveals itself as the measure of his accommodating responsiveness. Within his solemnity resides harmony: there is concord and joy, with no discord or perversity. Within his reverence resides tireless diligence: there is ease and simplicity, with no treachery or crookedness. Truly he is an amiable and gracious lord. How could blessings and emoluments fail to descend upon him?

Through the enduring constancy of his abundant virtue, he established the foundation for receiving Heaven’s favor illustriously; once Heaven’s mandate had gathered upon him, he received in full the blessing of attracting all to his embrace. The bestowal of descendants celebrated in “Locusts” (Zhongsi), and the worthy offspring resembling their forebears celebrated in “The Qilin’s Hooves” (Linzhi): in all that enriched his own person and his family, no blessing was lacking. The abundance of talented men in “The Rabbit Net” (Tuju), and the far-reaching transforming influence in “The Broad Han River” (Hanguang): in all that benefited his ministers and his people, no blessing failed to reach its fullest extent. The lord makes no appointment with blessings and emoluments, yet blessings and emoluments arrive of themselves.

Such is the mutual response between Heaven and humanity. Although its workings are subtle, the mutual dependence of virtue and blessing follows a fixed principle. Having gained insight through observation and inward response, how could the poet refrain from singing praise? Examining “The Great Plan” (Hongfan), we find that its ninth division says, “Encourage through the five blessings; overawe through the six extremes of suffering.” Yet these must first be preceded by the Five Elements, the Five Personal Affairs, the Eight Affairs of Government, and the Five Regulators of Time, so as to establish the August Standard. The Three Virtues, the Examination of Doubts, and the Various Verifications follow upon these. This shows that one must cultivate virtue in order to gather blessings, and that blessings and beneficence do not descend upon the licentious…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
人也周自后稷以來世德作求罔墜厥紹是用
享祚靈長取數以類而應豈直於文王之世一
時歌咏而已哉詩可以觀於此益信
湯孫奏假綏我思成鞉鼓淵淵嘒嘒管聲
既和且平依我磬聲於赫湯孫穆穆厥
聲
汪梯
同考試官教諭廖批斂華就實而意味雋永
必有養之士也錄之
===
同考試官教諭劉批以聲之和平寫樂之美
良是而詞旨鏗然不露庶幾一倡三嘆者矣
同考試官教諭張批簡嚴得商頌體
考試官學正馮批典重不浮
考試官學正劉批雅蔚
詩人言商王作樂以格先而因詳其樂聲之美
也夫惟樂可以感神也商王有焉其知盡祭之
義者歟此祀成湯之樂也蓋曰通幽明之感者
存乎祭重神明之交者存乎樂我湯孫之祭也
punctuated:
人也。周自后稷以來，世德作求，罔墜厥紹，是用享祚靈長。取數以類而應，豈直於文王之世一時歌咏而已哉？詩可以觀，於此益信。
湯孫奏假，綏我思成。鞉鼓淵淵，嘒嘒管聲。既和且平，依我磬聲。於赫湯孫，穆穆厥聲。
汪梯
同考試官教諭廖批：「斂華就實，而意味雋永，必有養之士也。錄之。」
同考試官教諭劉批：「以聲之和平寫樂之美，良是，而詞旨鏗然不露，庶幾一倡三嘆者矣。」
同考試官教諭張批：「簡嚴，得商頌體。」
考試官學正馮批：「典重不浮。」
考試官學正劉批：「雅蔚。」
詩人言商王作樂以格先，而因詳其樂聲之美也。夫惟樂可以感神也，商王有焉，其知盡祭之義者歟？此祀成湯之樂也。蓋曰：通幽明之感者存乎祭，重神明之交者存乎樂。我湯孫之祭也，
translation_en:
…upon licentious people. From Hou Ji onward, the Zhou pursued the virtue of preceding generations without letting their inherited tradition lapse; thus they enjoyed enduring dynastic blessings. Their allotted destiny responded according to its kind [?]. Could this have been merely a subject of passing praise in song during King Wen’s reign? That the Odes enable us to observe is made still more convincing by this.
Tang’s descendant advances to invoke the ancestors, who grant fulfillment to our thoughts. The hand drums and great drums resound deeply; the pipes sound clear and high. Both harmonious and balanced, they follow the sound of our chime stones. Oh, illustrious descendant of Tang! How solemn is his music!
Wang Ti
Associate Examiner Liao, Instructor (jiaoyu), comments: “He restrains ornament and attends to substance, yet his meaning has a lingering savor. He must be a man of cultivated character. Accept this essay.”
Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor (jiaoyu), comments: “To depict the beauty of music through the harmony and balance of its sounds is indeed right. Moreover, his language and meaning resonate without being overt: this comes close to ‘one voice singing and three responding in admiration.’”
Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor (jiaoyu), comments: “Concise and dignified: it captures the style of the Hymns of Shang.”
Examiner Feng, Instructor (xuezheng), comments: “Classical and weighty, without superficiality.”
Examiner Liu, Instructor (xuezheng), comments: “Elegant and richly accomplished.”
The poet speaks of the Shang king making music to reach his ancestors and accordingly describes in detail the beauty of its sounds. Music alone can move the spirits, and the Shang king possessed this capacity. Was he not one who understood how to fulfill the meaning of sacrifice? This is the music for sacrificing to Cheng Tang. The sense is this: sacrifice enables reciprocal feeling between the unseen and visible worlds; music gives solemn weight to communion with the spirits. As for the sacrifice offered by us, Tang’s descendants…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
王所以報本而反始義至重也商人尚聲固重
祭也而温恭有恪傳恭之遠寔有以將之耳使
其不然而徒致飾於鏞鼓管磬焉抑末矣是故
無聲之樂樂之本也綴兆節奏樂之末也辨於
此而後可以語祭矣
春秋
晉荀吳帥師敗狄于大鹵昭公元年
陳錫
同考試官教諭吳批毀車崇卒是荀吳變古
===
法之失處此作能言之而文有斷制可嘉
考試官學正馮批明白正大
考試官學正劉批純暢
春秋於霸臣之攘夷而譏其取勝之非道也蓋
王者之師以全取勝者也荀吳之敗敵昧於是
矣其能免於春秋之譏歟且太原地在禹服之
內嘗聞宣王薄伐六月以爲功矣今之大鹵固
昔之太原也而狄入門庭之寇不猶昔之玁狁
乎荀吳帥師禦之正合膺懲之義使能以道制
punctuated:
王所以報本而反始，義至重也。商人尚聲，固重祭也，而温恭有恪，傳恭之遠，寔有以將之耳。使其不然而徒致飾於鏞鼓管磬焉，抑末矣。是故無聲之樂，樂之本也；綴兆節奏，樂之末也。辨於此，而後可以語祭矣。
春秋
「晉荀吳帥師敗狄于大鹵。」昭公元年。
陳錫
同考試官教諭吳批：「毀車崇卒，是荀吳變古法之失處。此作能言之，而文有斷制，可嘉。」
考試官學正馮批：「明白正大。」
考試官學正劉批：「純暢。」
春秋於霸臣之攘夷，而譏其取勝之非道也。蓋王者之師，以全取勝者也。荀吳之敗敵，昧於是矣，其能免於春秋之譏歟？且太原地在禹服之內，嘗聞宣王薄伐，六月以爲功矣。今之大鹵，固昔之太原也，而狄入門庭之寇，不猶昔之玁狁乎？荀吳帥師禦之，正合膺懲之義。使能以道制
translation_en:
…the means by which kings repay their origins and return to their beginnings: its significance is supremely weighty. The people of Shang esteemed sound, certainly because they attached importance to sacrifice; yet their warmth, humility, and reverence, extending their respect far into the past [?], were what truly sustained it. Had this not been so, and had they merely lavished ornament upon great bells, drums, pipes, and chime stones, they would have attended only to externals. Thus, music without sound is the root of music; the positions of the dancers and the regulated rhythms are its outward details. Only after distinguishing these can one discuss sacrifice.
Spring and Autumn Annals
“Xun Wu of Jin led an army and defeated the Di at Dalu.” First year of Duke Zhao.
Chen Xi
Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor (jiaoyu): “Discarding chariots and favoring infantry was where Xun Wu erred in altering ancient military methods. This essay succeeds in explaining this, and its writing displays decisive judgment. Commendable.”
Comment by Examiner Feng, Instructor (xuezheng): “Clear, upright, and dignified.”
Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor (xuezheng): “Pure and fluent.”
In recording a hegemon’s minister repelling the alien peoples, the Spring and Autumn Annals censures his failure to follow the Way in securing victory. For the army of a true king achieves victory while preserving things intact. Xun Wu, in defeating his enemy, failed to understand this. Could he escape the censure of the Spring and Autumn Annals? Moreover, Taiyuan lay within the domains regulated by Yu. We have heard how King Xuan marched forth to attack, an achievement celebrated in “The Sixth Month.” Present-day Dalu is indeed the Taiyuan of old. Were not the Di, invading like raiders entering one’s gates and courtyard, comparable to the Xianyun of old? Xun Wu’s leading an army to resist them accorded precisely with the principle of chastising offenders. Had he been able to exercise control in accordance with the Way…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
勝庶幾王者之師矣廼誤聽魏舒之言罔繼吉
甫之烈毁車而徒寧徇嬖以求其法之必行舎
正而譎甘作俑以求其敵之必勝五乘以爲伍
焉五陳以相離焉將謂以什當一可以阨險也
曾何思革車虎賁甲士恭命孰非王者車戰之
法而可以輕毁耶多方以誘之未陳而薄之將
謂以詐爲竒可以襲取也會何思止齊不愆鼓
陳而戰孰非王者用兵之法而可以他尚耶車
法毁而苟簡之習啓知徼一時之利而不知古
===
制之遂不可復矣變詐興而傾危之俗成知取
目前之捷而不知末流之漸不可制矣聖人以
爲帝王之驅夷狄非制勝之患而惟以道之難
荀吳之敗狄誠是而所以敗之之道則非也故
書敗狄譏之者以此不然均之北伐均之太原
六月也而何今昔功過之不倫若此耶抑此知
聖人之慮遠矣先王古法不容輕易故車戰法
亡天下無全勝之師中國長技晁錯之所爲惜
也井田壞於商鞅封建廢於李斯車戰毁於荀
punctuated: 勝，庶幾王者之師矣。廼誤聽魏舒之言，罔繼吉甫之烈，毁車而徒，寧徇嬖以求其法之必行；舎正而譎，甘作俑以求其敵之必勝。五乘以爲伍焉，五陳以相離焉，將謂以什當一，可以阨險也。曾何思革車虎賁，甲士恭命，孰非王者車戰之法，而可以輕毁耶？多方以誘之，未陳而薄之，將謂以詐爲竒，可以襲取也。會何思止齊不愆，鼓陳而戰，孰非王者用兵之法，而可以他尚耶？車法毁而苟簡之習啓，知徼一時之利，而不知古制之遂不可復矣；變詐興而傾危之俗成，知取目前之捷，而不知末流之漸不可制矣。聖人以爲帝王之驅夷狄，非制勝之患，而惟以道之難。荀吳之敗狄誠是，而所以敗之之道則非也。故書敗狄，譏之者以此。不然，均之北伐，均之太原、六月也，而何今昔功過之不倫若此耶？抑此知聖人之慮遠矣。先王古法不容輕易，故車戰法亡，天下無全勝之師；中國長技，晁錯之所爲惜也。井田壞於商鞅，封建廢於李斯，車戰毁於荀
translation_en:
…victory, his army might have approached that of a true king. Instead, he mistakenly heeded Wei Shu’s words and failed to continue Jifu’s glorious achievements. He abandoned the chariots and fought on foot, even executing a favored retainer to ensure that his method was implemented; he forsook upright conduct for deceit, willingly setting a pernicious precedent to ensure victory over his enemy. He organized the men of five chariots into a unit and separated them into five formations, supposing that setting ten against one would enable him to control narrow and difficult terrain. Yet did he ever consider that armored chariots, tiger-brave warriors, and armored soldiers obedient to commands all belonged to the true kings’ methods of chariot warfare? How could these be lightly discarded?

He enticed the enemy by various means and pressed the attack before they had formed their ranks, supposing that deceit employed as an unexpected maneuver would enable him to take them by surprise. Yet did he ever consider that halting in good order without error, and beating the drums to engage an enemy drawn up in formation, all belonged to the true kings’ methods of warfare? How could he favor other practices? Once the methods of chariot warfare were destroyed, habits of expedient shortcuts arose. He knew how to seek a momentary advantage but did not realize that the ancient institutions would thereafter become impossible to restore. Once deceit and trickery flourished, treacherous practices became customary. He knew how to secure an immediate victory but did not realize that their eventual development would become impossible to restrain.

The Sage held that, when emperors and kings drove back the Yi and Di, securing victory was not the concern; the difficulty lay in doing so in accordance with the Way. Xun Wu was indeed right to defeat the Di, but the means by which he defeated them were wrong. This is why the record’s statement that he “defeated the Di” censures him. Otherwise, since both campaigns were northern expeditions, both at Taiyuan and in the sixth month, why should the merits and faults of the present and the past differ so greatly? From this we recognize the far-reaching concern of the Sage.

The ancient methods of the former kings must not be lightly altered. Thus, when the methods of chariot warfare disappeared, no army under Heaven could achieve complete victory. This superior military capability of the Central States was what Chao Cuo lamented losing. The well-field system was ruined by Shang Yang; the enfeoffment system was abolished by Li Si; chariot warfare was destroyed by Xun…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
吳使先王成法不復見於後世皆功利欺詐之
徒爲之也考經所書然後知聖人垂訓之大而
慮患之遠矣
夏公會齊侯于夾谷公至自夾谷齊人
來歸鄆讙龜陰田〔俱定公十年〕
潘季馴
同考試官教諭吳批〔三田之歸孔子攝相見諸行事之實此篇斷案明白鑿鑿究極於魯史者〕
考試官學正馮批〔婉而成章〕
===
考試官學正劉批〔明粹〕
春秋序望國化强之績亦惟以禮綏之而已是
可見夾谷會而侵疆歸綏之斯來也禮之感人
有如此夫惟時魯定會齊孔子相事君也能庸
夫執禮之臣臣也克承夫秉禮之緒以故始則
齊臣獻計會夾谷而亂之以兵繼則齊君悔過
歸三田而謝之以質焉聖人序其事若曰玆役
也齊來格而我底績夫非用禮之效歟彼神人
德義禮之大者夫人所固有也舉而詔之不有
punctuated:
吳，使先王成法不復見於後世，皆功利欺詐之徒爲之也。考經所書，然後知聖人垂訓之大，而慮患之遠矣。

夏，公會齊侯于夾谷。公至自夾谷。齊人來歸鄆、讙、龜陰田。〔俱定公十年〕
潘季馴
同考試官教諭吳批〔三田之歸，孔子攝相見諸行事之實。此篇斷案明白，鑿鑿究極於魯史者。〕
考試官學正馮批〔婉而成章。〕
考試官學正劉批〔明粹。〕

春秋序望國化强之績，亦惟以禮綏之而已。是可見夾谷會而侵疆歸，綏之斯來也。禮之感人有如此！夫惟時魯定會齊，孔子相事。君也能庸夫執禮之臣，臣也克承夫秉禮之緒。以故始則齊臣獻計，會夾谷而亂之以兵；繼則齊君悔過，歸三田而謝之以質焉。聖人序其事，若曰：玆役也，齊來格而我底績，夫非用禮之效歟？彼神人德義，禮之大者，夫人所固有也。舉而詔之，不有
translation_en:
…Wu, so that the established institutions of the former kings were no longer seen in later ages: all this was the work of men devoted to profit, advantage, and deceit. Only after examining what the Classic records do we understand the greatness of the Sage’s instruction for posterity and the foresight with which he anticipated calamities.

“In summer, the Duke met the Marquis of Qi at Jiagu. The Duke returned from Jiagu. Men of Qi came to restore the lands of Yun, Huan, and Guiyin.” 〔All in the tenth year of Duke Ding.〕
Pan Jixun
Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor, comments: 〔The restoration of the three territories was concrete evidence, manifested in deeds, of Confucius’s service as acting chief minister. This essay reaches a clear judgment, firmly grounded in a thorough examination of the history of Lu.〕
Examiner Feng, School Director, comments: 〔Subtle, yet forming an accomplished composition.〕
Examiner Liu, School Director, comments: 〔Lucid and refined.〕

The Spring and Autumn Annals recounts the achievement of an eminent state in transforming a powerful one [?]: it consisted simply in winning it over through ritual propriety. This is evident in the meeting at Jiagu and the restoration of the occupied territory: win them over, and they will come. Such is the power of ritual propriety to move people!

At that time, Duke Ding of Lu met the ruler of Qi, and Confucius assisted in conducting the proceedings. The ruler could employ a minister who upheld ritual propriety, and the minister could carry forward the tradition of adhering to it. Thus, at first, a minister of Qi proposed a scheme to disrupt the meeting at Jiagu with armed men; afterward, the ruler of Qi repented of his wrongdoing, restored the three territories, and thereby gave tangible proof of his apology. In recounting these events, the Sage seems to say: “In this undertaking, Qi was brought to submit, and we accomplished our purpose. Was this not the effect of employing ritual propriety?” As for spirits and men, virtue and righteousness—the great concerns of ritual propriety [?]—these are inherent in everyone. When they are set forth and explained, is there not…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
悔悟而歸我以三田抑亦翕然丕變而不忍歸
我以女樂矣若之何得政日淺厥施未究兆足
以行而不能三年淹也豈其天之未定而不能
違歟尚賴春秋作而爲國以禮之訓昭焉又聖
人之所以定乎天也
禮記
樂正崇四術立四教順先王詩書禮樂以
造士春秋教以禮樂冬夏教以詩書
邵型
===
同考試官教諭倪批先王教人之意體認眞
切宜錄以式
考試官學正馮批文詞充贍
考試官學正劉批通暢
大臣造士之法取諸古而時其教焉夫詩書禮
樂古之道也大臣脩此以爲時教焉其曲成之
心何至哉昔者先王患士之無教也而羣之太
學焉患教之不刑也而立之樂正焉甞稽樂正
之教而知其作人之善矣是故士之業於國學
punctuated:
悔悟而歸我以三田，抑亦翕然丕變而不忍歸我以女樂矣。若之何得政日淺，厥施未究，兆足以行而不能三年淹也？豈其天之未定而不能違歟？尚賴《春秋》作，而爲國以禮之訓昭焉，又聖人之所以定乎天也。
《禮記》
樂正崇四術，立四教，順先王《詩》《書》禮樂以造士。春秋教以禮樂，冬夏教以《詩》《書》。
邵型
同考試官教諭倪批：先王教人之意，體認眞切，宜錄以式。
考試官學正馮批：文詞充贍。
考試官學正劉批：通暢。
大臣造士之法，取諸古而時其教焉。夫《詩》《書》禮樂，古之道也。大臣脩此以爲時教焉，其曲成之心何至哉！昔者先王患士之無教也，而羣之太學焉；患教之不刑也，而立之樂正焉。甞稽樂正之教，而知其作人之善矣。是故士之業於國學
translation_en:
…repent and return the three tracts of land to us; or indeed undergo a wholehearted and profound transformation and be unwilling to present us with female musicians. Why, then, when his time in government was still short and his measures had not yet been fully carried out, did the signs suffice to prompt his departure, so that he could not remain for three years? Was it that Heaven’s disposition was not yet settled, and he could not go against it? Yet fortunately the Spring and Autumn Annals was composed, making manifest the teaching that a state should be governed through ritual: this, too, was how the sage gave settled expression to Heaven’s order.
Record of Rites
“The Director of Music honors the four disciplines and establishes the four branches of instruction, following the former kings’ Odes, Documents, rites, and music to train scholars. In spring and autumn he teaches rites and music; in winter and summer he teaches the Odes and Documents.”
Shao Xing
Comment by Associate Examiner Ni, Instructor: “His understanding of the former kings’ intent in educating people is authentic and precise. This should be recorded as a model.”
