Comment by Examiner Feng, Instructor: “The composition is rich and ample in expression.”
Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: “Clear and fluent.”
The method by which a great minister trains scholars draws upon antiquity and adapts instruction to the seasons. The Odes, Documents, rites, and music constitute the Way of antiquity. A great minister cultivates these to provide seasonal instruction. How consummate is his concern to bring each person to fulfillment! In former times, the ancient kings worried that scholars lacked instruction, and therefore gathered them in the Imperial University. They worried that instruction lacked a proper model, and therefore appointed a Director of Music over them. Having examined the Director of Music’s instruction, I have come to understand his excellence in cultivating men of talent. Thus, as for scholars pursuing their studies in the state school…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
廢學焉耳時乎冬夏而詩書之敎興焉凡其迪
之典謨迪之雅頌者於此乎相傳習也詩書無
當乎冬夏而率之爲時敎者庶其養之純而無
廢業焉耳是則立敎惟古則授之者有成法施
敎惟時則學之者有專功先王之世師道立而
善人多者其率用此歟吾于是而知先王之育
材興理非徒備官也而有本焉思齊之詩詠文
王之德詳矣而必以古之人無斁譽髦斯士終
焉則文王崇敎之心可以想見而其得人以隆
===
治化者固其所也雖然周之士非獨上之人養
之士亦知自養焉後世典敎之官作新之術非
不宛然成周品式而何有周之士不終覩耶噫
爲士者可以興矣
德者性之端也樂者德之華也
曹光
同考試官敎諭倪批理明意盡深達作樂之
本者
考試官學正馮批埋致精到
punctuated:
廢學焉耳。時乎冬夏，而詩書之敎興焉。凡其迪之典謨、迪之雅頌者，於此乎相傳習也。詩書無當乎冬夏，而率之爲時敎者，庶其養之純而無廢業焉耳。是則立敎惟古，則授之者有成法；施敎惟時，則學之者有專功。先王之世，師道立而善人多者，其率用此歟？吾于是而知先王之育材興理，非徒備官也，而有本焉。《思齊》之詩詠文王之德詳矣，而必以「古之人無斁，譽髦斯士」終焉，則文王崇敎之心可以想見，而其得人以隆治化者，固其所也。雖然，周之士非獨上之人養之，士亦知自養焉。後世典敎之官、作新之術，非不宛然成周品式，而何有周之士不終覩耶？噫！爲士者可以興矣！

德者性之端也，樂者德之華也。
曹光。

同考試官敎諭倪批：理明意盡，深達作樂之本者。
考試官學正馮批：埋致精到。
translation_en:
…neglect learning, that is all. In winter and summer, instruction in the Odes and Documents flourished. All instruction through the Canons and Counsels, and through the Elegantiae and Hymns, was transmitted and practiced at these times. The Odes and Documents have no inherent correspondence with winter and summer; assigning them as seasonal instruction was intended simply to make students’ cultivation thorough and keep them from neglecting their studies. Thus, when education was established according to antiquity, teachers had settled methods; when instruction was provided according to the seasons, learners could devote themselves to particular attainments. Was it not through following this that, in the age of the former kings, the way of the teacher was established and good men were numerous? From this I understand that the former kings’ cultivation of talent and advancement of good order were not merely intended to fill official posts: they had a deeper foundation. The ode “Si Qi” (Thinking of the Worthy) describes King Wen’s virtue at length, yet necessarily concludes with “The man of old was untiring; he nurtured these outstanding scholars.” From this we can imagine King Wen’s commitment to education, and his obtaining worthy men to advance good government and moral transformation was its natural consequence. Nevertheless, the scholars of Zhou were not merely cultivated by those above them; they also knew how to cultivate themselves. In later ages, the officials responsible for education and the methods for renewing the people have closely resembled the established patterns of Zhou. Why, then, have scholars like those of Zhou never appeared? Alas! Those who are scholars should rouse themselves!

“Virtue is the manifestation of human nature; music is the flowering of virtue.”
By Cao Guang.

Comment by Associate Examiner Ni, Instructor: “The principles are clear and the meaning fully expressed: this is someone who profoundly understands the foundation of making music.”
Comment by Examiner Feng, School Director: “The reasoning [?] is precise and thorough.”

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
考試官學正劉批古雅
記者原德之所由發而著其爲樂之本也夫樂
非自外至者也性發於德而樂以彰之玆其樂
之所自來者乎記者懼作樂者之忘其本也故
爲之言曰先王之立樂也非作而致其文也此
有由本也樂敎行而可以觀德者亦以德爲樂
之本焉爾是故志和行成之謂德德顯於有而
性隱於無宜若不相管矣然有無雖分於二致
而體用實出於一原湛一之本素豫夫妙應之
===
機和順之休悉根於降衷之懿發而中者出之
至靜以洩其精妙用之顯行一全體之呈露也
用而和者本之太虛以呈其象至德之淵微一
性眞之發越也要之性者德之藏諸用德者性
之顯諸仁其猶物在中而緒見於外者矣觀德
可以知性不曰性之端乎比物飾節之謂樂樂
滯於器而德凝於道宜若不相通矣然道器雖
判於殊塗而精粗則妙於一體懿德之富有自
涵夫聲氣之元至樂之昭宣實顯乎中和之積
punctuated:
考試官學正劉批：古雅。

記者原德之所由發，而著其爲樂之本也。夫樂非自外至者也，性發於德，而樂以彰之，玆其樂之所自來者乎？記者懼作樂者之忘其本也，故爲之言曰：「先王之立樂也，非作而致其文也，此有由本也。樂敎行而可以觀德者，亦以德爲樂之本焉爾。」是故志和行成之謂德。德顯於有，而性隱於無，宜若不相管矣。然有無雖分於二致，而體用實出於一原。湛一之本，素豫夫妙應之機；和順之休，悉根於降衷之懿。發而中者，出之至靜以洩其精，妙用之顯行，一全體之呈露也；用而和者，本之太虛以呈其象，至德之淵微，一性眞之發越也。要之，性者德之藏諸用，德者性之顯諸仁，其猶物在中而緒見於外者矣。觀德可以知性，不曰性之端乎？比物飾節之謂樂。樂滯於器，而德凝於道，宜若不相通矣。然道器雖判於殊塗，而精粗則妙於一體。懿德之富有，自涵夫聲氣之元；至樂之昭宣，實顯乎中和之積。
translation_en:
Examiner Liu, an instructor, comments: “Classical and elegant.”

The author of the Record traces the source from which virtue issues and makes clear that it is the foundation of music. Music does not come from outside. Human nature manifests itself in virtue, and music makes that virtue apparent: is this not where music originates? Fearing that those who make music might forget its foundation, the author therefore says: “When the former kings established music, they did not merely fashion it to achieve its outward embellishment; it had a foundation from which it proceeded. That virtue can be discerned when musical instruction is put into practice is likewise simply because virtue is the foundation of music.” Thus, harmony of purpose and completeness of conduct are called virtue. Virtue is manifest in what has being, whereas human nature is concealed in what has no visible being; they might therefore seem unrelated. Yet although being and nonbeing are distinguished as two aspects, substance and function actually issue from a single source. The clear and undivided foundation already contains the capacity for wondrous responsiveness; the excellence of harmony and accord is wholly rooted in the goodness Heaven has bestowed within us. What issues forth and attains due measure emerges from utmost stillness to release its essence: the manifest operation of its wondrous function is the disclosure of the whole substance. What operates harmoniously is rooted in the Great Void and thereby presents its forms: the profound subtlety of consummate virtue is the unfolding of the truth of human nature. In sum, human nature is virtue concealed in functioning, and virtue is human nature manifested in benevolence. It is like something situated within whose traces appear outside. By observing virtue one can know human nature: is this not why virtue is called the outward indication of human nature?

Arranging things together and embellishing their rhythms is called music. Music is lodged in concrete instruments, whereas virtue is concentrated in the Way; they might therefore seem to have no connection. Yet although the Way and concrete instruments are assigned to different paths, the subtle and the gross are wondrously united in one whole. The abundance of excellent virtue inherently contains the source of sound and vital breath; the radiant expression of consummate music makes manifest the accumulated fullness of equilibrium and harmony…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
越之聲音以樂其象由之無聲者以奮其光八
音之克諧一德音之播比也形之動靜以治其
飾由之不顯者以發其蘊萬舞之有奕一德輝
之流動也要之盛德寓大樂于無形大樂闡盛
德于有象殆有誠於中而必形于外者矣聞樂
可以知德不曰德之華乎是則德非外鑠性其
本也樂非強作德其本也不能盡性猶難語德
不能成德猶難語樂察于此者樂其可作也已
嘗聞樂也者和也和也者性之德也求端于和
===
而樂不外是矣觀后夔典樂之教惟本之和德
而不拘拘於憂擊摶拊之間卒之和神人而舞
百獸者胥此焉出則可以知古人作樂之方矣
後世桑間濮上之音七德九功之舞非不侈其
聲容吾不知其德性爲何如也廣樂以成教者
盍亦審所尚乎
第貳塲
論
合虛與氣有性之名
punctuated:
越之聲音，以樂其象；由之無聲者，以奮其光。八音之克諧，一德音之播比也。形之動靜，以治其飾；由之不顯者，以發其蘊。萬舞之有奕，一德輝之流動也。要之，盛德寓大樂于無形，大樂闡盛德于有象，殆有誠於中而必形于外者矣。聞樂可以知德，不曰德之華乎？是則德非外鑠，性其本也；樂非強作，德其本也。不能盡性，猶難語德；不能成德，猶難語樂。察于此者，樂其可作也已。嘗聞樂也者，和也；和也者，性之德也。求端于和，而樂不外是矣。觀后夔典樂之教，惟本之和德，而不拘拘於憂擊摶拊之間。卒之和神人而舞百獸者，胥此焉出，則可以知古人作樂之方矣。後世桑間濮上之音、七德九功之舞，非不侈其聲容，吾不知其德性爲何如也。廣樂以成教者，盍亦審所尚乎？

第貳塲

論

合虛與氣，有性之名。
translation_en:
…Expressing it in sounds gives musical form to its image; proceeding from what is soundless brings forth its radiance. The harmony achieved by the eight classes of instruments is wholly the diffusion and concord of virtue’s sound. Giving it form in movement and stillness orders its outward embellishment; proceeding from what is unmanifest brings forth what it holds within. The splendid array of the wan dance is wholly the flowing radiance of virtue. In essence, abundant virtue lodges great music in the formless, while great music manifests abundant virtue in perceptible forms. This is surely a case of what is sincere within necessarily taking form without. By hearing music, one can know virtue: is music not called the flower of virtue? Thus virtue is not imposed from without: human nature is its root. Music is not forcibly contrived: virtue is its root. Without fully realizing one’s nature, it is still difficult to speak of virtue; without perfecting virtue, it is still difficult to speak of music. Those who discern this may indeed create music.

I have heard that music is harmony, and that harmony is the virtue of human nature. Seek music’s source in harmony, and music does not extend beyond this. Consider Hou Kui’s teaching as Director of Music: he based it solely on harmonious virtue, without being narrowly confined to the striking and beating of instruments [?]. That he ultimately brought spirits and humans into harmony and caused the hundred beasts to dance all proceeded from this. Here we may discern how the ancients created music. As for the later melodies of Sangjian and Pushang and the dances of the Seven Virtues and Nine Achievements, their sounds and displays were certainly lavish; yet I do not know what their virtue and nature were like. Should those who extend music to accomplish moral instruction not also examine what they esteem?

Second Session

Discourse

Through the conjunction of the void and vital force (qi), there is what is called nature.

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
者聖賢言性至明且切也而孰有辨於易
乎自夫子係易而首發於乾之彖曰各正
性命保合大和夫曰各正則固以理言之
矣而大和之保合者實有以涵畜之則大
虛之理氣化之道其所以妙合而凝者不
可以求端於天耶今夫於穆不已天之所
以為天也曷為以虛言之也蓋天覆於上
塊然一氣而已而理之所主至空而明冲
漠無朕雖其流形萬品莫不取足於天之
===
氣而天之所以為天者卒未嘗囿於其氣
而氣之本體固自若也夫安得而不謂之
虛至於氣之聚散為寒暑晝夜為雨露霜
雪為山川木石為金水火土皆變化之客
形而陰陽之精未嘗不根柢於大虛但氣
有形虛無迹而理之虛者於氣之實者見
之粲然而陳雜然而出是不可以觀道之
所在矣乎以虛為天以理言之謂之天也
以氣化為道以此理之運行非陰陽之二
punctuated: 者，聖賢言性至明且切也，而孰有辨於易乎？自夫子係易，而首發於乾之彖曰：「各正性命，保合大和。」夫曰各正，則固以理言之矣；而大和之保合者，實有以涵畜之。則大虛之理、氣化之道，其所以妙合而凝者，不可以求端於天耶？今夫於穆不已，天之所以為天也，曷為以虛言之也？蓋天覆於上，塊然一氣而已，而理之所主，至空而明，冲漠無朕。雖其流形萬品，莫不取足於天之氣，而天之所以為天者，卒未嘗囿於其氣，而氣之本體固自若也。夫安得而不謂之虛？至於氣之聚散，為寒暑晝夜，為雨露霜雪，為山川木石，為金水火土，皆變化之客形，而陰陽之精未嘗不根柢於大虛。但氣有形，虛無迹，而理之虛者，於氣之實者見之。粲然而陳，雜然而出，是不可以觀道之所在矣乎？以虛為天，以理言之謂之天也；以氣化為道，以此理之運行，非陰陽之二
translation_en:
…The sages and worthies spoke of human nature with utmost clarity and precision; yet where is it distinguished more clearly than in the Book of Changes? When the Master appended his explanations to the Changes, he first set this forth in the Commentary on the Judgment for Qian: “Each attains its proper nature and allotted destiny, preserving and uniting the Great Harmony.” To say “each attains its proper nature” is assuredly to speak in terms of principle. Yet that which preserves and unites the Great Harmony also truly nurtures and contains it. As for the principle of the Great Void and the Way of the transformations of qi, may we not seek in Heaven the source of their wondrous union and consolidation?

Now, profound and unceasing activity is what makes Heaven Heaven. Why, then, speak of it in terms of emptiness? Heaven stretches above us, simply one mass of qi; yet the principle governing it is utterly empty and luminous, still and without trace. Though Heaven gives flowing form to the myriad kinds of things, all of which draw their full provision from Heaven’s qi, what makes Heaven Heaven is ultimately never confined within that qi, while the fundamental substance of qi remains as it is. How, then, could we fail to call it empty?

As for the gathering and dispersal of qi—becoming cold and heat, day and night; rain and dew, frost and snow; mountains and rivers, trees and stones; metal, water, fire, and earth—these are all transient forms of transformation. Yet the vital essence of yin and yang is invariably rooted in the Great Void. Qi has form, whereas emptiness leaves no trace; nevertheless, the emptiness of principle becomes visible in the concreteness of qi. Brilliantly arrayed and emerging in profusion, do these not enable us to observe where the Way resides? To identify emptiness as Heaven is to call it Heaven in terms of principle. To identify the transformations of qi as the Way is to consider the operation of this principle, which cannot proceed without the two …

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
端不可也則人物之性又豈外於虛氣之
合也哉自夫性之不明於天下也守空寂
之說者以為虛即性也不知舉虛而遺氣
將病性於無矣梏於形體之小者以為氣
即性也不知舉氣而遺虛將滯性於有矣
抑孰知虛氣之相乘固性之所以為妙者
乎蓋大虛者此理之體指其未形言之也
氣化者此理之用指其未成言之也而虛
之與氣又何以知其合也蓋陰陽氣也形
===
而下者也所以一陰一陽者理也形而上
者也自理之方行而未有所立也使非附
麗於氣則大虛終歸於無物不足以立天
下之有而理之善者不可得而見矣然氣
之方出而未有所成也非大虛者為之綱
維焉則絪縕雜揉亦將物而不化矣何以
繼善成性者耶自今言之天之生物也惟
人為最靈其間有血氣知覺為禽獸者有
無血氣知覺而有生意為草木者有生意
punctuated: 端不可也，則人物之性又豈外於虛氣之合也哉？自夫性之不明於天下也，守空寂之說者以為虛即性也，不知舉虛而遺氣，將病性於無矣；梏於形體之小者以為氣即性也，不知舉氣而遺虛，將滯性於有矣。抑孰知虛氣之相乘，固性之所以為妙者乎？蓋大虛者，此理之體，指其未形言之也；氣化者，此理之用，指其未成言之也。而虛之與氣，又何以知其合也？蓋陰陽，氣也，形而下者也；所以一陰一陽者，理也，形而上者也。自理之方行而未有所立也，使非附麗於氣，則大虛終歸於無物，不足以立天下之有，而理之善者不可得而見矣。然氣之方出而未有所成也，非大虛者為之綱維焉，則絪縕雜揉，亦將物而不化矣，何以繼善成性者耶？自今言之，天之生物也，惟人為最靈。其間有血氣知覺為禽獸者，有無血氣知覺而有生意為草木者，有生意
translation_en:
…the two poles are indispensable. How, then, could the nature of human beings and other things lie outside the union of emptiness and material force (qi)? Ever since nature ceased to be clearly understood in the world, those who uphold doctrines of emptiness and quiescence have taken emptiness itself to be nature. They do not understand that, by admitting emptiness and leaving out material force, they impair their account of nature by reducing it to nonbeing. Those confined within the narrow bounds of physical form take material force itself to be nature. They do not understand that, by admitting material force and leaving out emptiness, they confine nature to being. Yet who understands that the mutual interaction of emptiness and material force is precisely what makes nature wondrous?

The Great Void is the substance of this principle (li), spoken of before it takes form; the transformations of material force are the functioning of this principle, spoken of before it reaches completion. But how do we know that emptiness and material force unite? Yin and yang are material force, belonging to what is below form; that by which there is alternately yin and yang is principle, belonging to what is above form. When principle is first operating and has not yet established anything, unless it adheres to material force, the Great Void will ultimately amount to nothing. It will be insufficient to establish the things that exist in the world, and the goodness of principle will not become visible. Yet when material force is first emerging and has not yet completed anything, unless the Great Void provides its governing framework, its dense intermingling will likewise produce mere things without transformation. How, then, could it continue as goodness and become complete as nature?

Speaking of matters as they stand, among the beings Heaven generates, human beings alone possess the greatest spiritual intelligence. Among these beings, those possessing blood, vital force, and perception are birds and beasts; those lacking blood, vital force, and perception but possessing the impulse of life are plants and trees; there are those whose impulse of life…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
已絶而但有形質臭味爲枯槁者雖分有
不同其剛柔之異稟屈伸之交禪呼吸升
降之不齊莫非性也而亦莫非氣也使有
氣焉而不本之於虛則氣滯於方而亦不
能自運矣夫惟以至虛之理而合之於氣
化之賾也則理以主氣氣以載理而性之
具於人物者隨所觸而皆應是故其在於
人也仁發爲惻隱義發爲羞惡禮發爲恭
敬智發爲是非氣爲之也其所以爲仁爲
===
義爲禮爲智者其理本至虛也由是達之
於情爲喜怒哀樂焉見之於事爲視聽言
動思焉秩之於倫爲親義序別信焉是皆
性之動也而莫非至虛之理也不然禽獸
至駁也而於君臣父子夫婦兄弟朋友亦
有各得其一曲之明者其孰使之耶又不
然草木至微也而植者自植天機自完其
孰使之耶又不然枯槁之物生意絶矣而
糟粕煨燼變化不窮其孰使之耶信乎理
punctuated: 已絶而但有形質臭味爲枯槁者，雖分有不同，其剛柔之異稟、屈伸之交禪、呼吸升降之不齊，莫非性也，而亦莫非氣也。使有氣焉而不本之於虛，則氣滯於方，而亦不能自運矣。夫惟以至虛之理而合之於氣化之賾也，則理以主氣，氣以載理，而性之具於人物者，隨所觸而皆應。是故其在於人也，仁發爲惻隱，義發爲羞惡，禮發爲恭敬，智發爲是非，氣爲之也。其所以爲仁、爲義、爲禮、爲智者，其理本至虛也。由是達之於情，爲喜怒哀樂焉；見之於事，爲視聽言動思焉；秩之於倫，爲親義序別信焉。是皆性之動也，而莫非至虛之理也。不然，禽獸至駁也，而於君臣、父子、夫婦、兄弟、朋友，亦有各得其一曲之明者，其孰使之耶？又不然，草木至微也，而植者自植，天機自完，其孰使之耶？又不然，枯槁之物，生意絶矣，而糟粕煨燼，變化不窮，其孰使之耶？信乎，理
translation_en: …has already ceased, leaving only physical form, smell, and taste, as in withered and dried things. Although their allotted portions differ, their different endowments of hardness and softness, the alternation of contraction and expansion, and the unevenness of breathing, rising, and descending are all manifestations of nature; they are also all manifestations of qi. If qi did not have its foundation in the void, it would become confined to a particular configuration and could not move of itself. Only when the principle of utmost emptiness is united with the profundities of qi’s transformations does principle govern qi and qi bear principle, so that the nature inherent in human beings and things responds to whatever it encounters. Thus, in human beings, benevolence issues as compassion, righteousness as shame and aversion to wrongdoing, ritual propriety as reverence and respect, and wisdom as discernment of right and wrong: qi brings these about. Yet what makes them benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom is their principle, which is fundamentally utterly empty. Extended into the emotions, this becomes joy, anger, sorrow, and delight; manifested in activity, it becomes seeing, hearing, speaking, acting, and thinking; ordered within human relationships, it becomes affection, righteousness, precedence, distinction, and trustworthiness. These are all movements of nature, and all are the principle of utmost emptiness. If this were not so, birds and beasts, though their endowments are most mixed, each possess some partial understanding of the relationships between ruler and minister, father and son, husband and wife, elder and younger brothers, and friends. What causes this? Again, if this were not so, plants and trees, though exceedingly insignificant, grow of themselves, their natural workings complete in themselves. What causes this? Again, if this were not so, withered and dried things have lost their vitality, yet dregs, chaff, and smoldering ashes undergo inexhaustible transformations. What causes this? Truly, principle…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之在天下無空缺不滿之處而隨氣流行
以成人物之性者未嘗止息辟則户然性
其樞也虛則能闔能闢實有是理而不可
以形求者也氣則闔之闢之有迹可見而
日用不離者也知樞之所以為樞不外於
闔闢之盡神則知性之所以為性不外於
理氣之相乘矣理不可見是謂至靜無感
性之淵源一大虛無形氣之本體所自來
也其交感不齊而知識生焉是謂感而遂
===
通性之發見一聚散有形氣之變化所以
行也惟其主於虛是故天命之性一焉而
聖愚賢不肖之分與夫歧行蠕息之類無
有乎弗同無有乎弗具者理也惟其隨於
氣是故氣質之性殊焉而天下之偏者全
者清者濁者厚者薄者邪者正者始紛紛
雜出而不可禦矣是故純粹至善固性也
剛柔純駁亦性也立於無物之先固此性
也行於有物之後亦此性也妙矣哉性之
punctuated: 之在天下，無空缺不滿之處，而隨氣流行以成人物之性者，未嘗止息。辟則户然，性其樞也。虛則能闔能闢，實有是理而不可以形求者也；氣則闔之闢之，有迹可見而日用不離者也。知樞之所以為樞，不外於闔闢之盡神，則知性之所以為性，不外於理氣之相乘矣。理不可見，是謂「至靜無感」。性之淵源，一大虛無形，氣之本體所自來也。其交感不齊而知識生焉，是謂「感而遂通」。性之發見，一聚散有形，氣之變化所以行也。惟其主於虛，是故天命之性一焉，而聖愚賢不肖之分，與夫歧行蠕息之類，無有乎弗同，無有乎弗具者，理也。惟其隨於氣，是故氣質之性殊焉，而天下之偏者全者、清者濁者、厚者薄者、邪者正者，始紛紛雜出而不可禦矣。是故純粹至善，固性也；剛柔純駁，亦性也。立於無物之先，固此性也；行於有物之後，亦此性也。妙矣哉，性之
translation_en:
…as principle exists throughout the world, there is no empty space that it does not fill; and its flowing along with material force (qi), thereby constituting the nature of human beings and other things, has never ceased. To use the analogy of a door, nature is its pivot. Being empty, it permits both closing and opening: this principle truly exists, yet cannot be sought in physical form. Material force is the actual closing and opening, whose traces are visible and which is inseparable from everyday use. If one understands that what makes a pivot a pivot lies entirely in the wondrous efficacy of opening and closing, one understands that what makes nature nature lies entirely in the interaction of principle and material force.

Principle cannot be seen: this is called “utter stillness, without stimulation.” The wellspring of nature is a single great, formless void, from which the fundamental substance of material force originates. Its interactions and responses vary, and knowledge and awareness arise from them: this is called “responding to stimulation and thereby comprehending.” Nature’s manifestation unites gathering and dispersal in perceptible form [?]; through this the transformations of material force proceed.

Precisely because it is grounded in emptiness, the nature conferred by Heaven is one. Across the distinctions between sages and fools, the worthy and the unworthy, and among creatures that walk [?] or crawl, what is everywhere the same and fully present in each is principle. Precisely because it follows material force, however, the nature of one’s physical endowment differs. Thus, throughout the world, partial and complete, clear and turbid, substantial and meager, deviant and upright endowments begin to emerge in a profusion that cannot be restrained.

Thus, purity and supreme goodness are indeed nature; hardness and softness, purity and admixture, are also nature. What stands before there are any things is indeed this nature; what operates after things exist is also this nature. How wondrous is nature’s…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
擬宋以唐介參知政事謝表熙寧元年
陳錫
同考試官教諭吳批事核而精文麗而則深
得表體
考試官學正馮批臣子忠悃之意當如此
考試官學正劉批典麗詳贍
熙寧元年某月某日伏蒙
聖恩除臣參知政事者
鈞衡佐理班聯畫省之榮鼎實叅調位近
===
紫宸之寵顧叨塵之已甚念辭避之弗容拜
命周章捫心媿汗臣誠惶誠恐稽首頓首竊以
樞機之任式典於平章
密勿之謨尤資乎協賛輪班知印毗
廟論以象三台書
勅齊銜攝
朝揆而列八座名稱實肇於乾德墫位復定
於雍熙睠此崇階宜歸碩望伏念臣性惟
拙戇質本疎庸筮仕平江謬竊理冤之譽
punctuated:
擬宋以唐介參知政事謝表，熙寧元年。
陳錫
同考試官教諭吳批：事核而精，文麗而則，深得表體。
考試官學正馮批：臣子忠悃之意，當如此。
考試官學正劉批：典麗詳贍。
熙寧元年某月某日，伏蒙聖恩除臣參知政事者。
鈞衡佐理，班聯畫省之榮；鼎實叅調，位近紫宸之寵。顧叨塵之已甚，念辭避之弗容。拜命周章，捫心媿汗。臣誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首。竊以樞機之任，式典於平章；密勿之謨，尤資乎協賛。輪班知印，毗廟論以象三台；書勅齊銜，攝朝揆而列八座。名稱實肇於乾德，墫位復定於雍熙。睠此崇階，宜歸碩望。伏念臣性惟拙戇，質本疎庸。筮仕平江，謬竊理冤之譽，
translation_en:
A model memorial of thanks on behalf of Tang Jie of the Song upon his appointment as Administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs? No: Vice Administrator of Affairs of State (canzhi zhengshi), in the first year of Xining [1068].
By Chen Xi.
Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: “The historical particulars are accurate and judiciously chosen; the writing is elegant and conforms to proper standards. It thoroughly captures the memorial form.”
Comment by Examiner Feng, Instructor: “This is how a subject should express his loyal sincerity.”
Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: “Classically elegant, detailed, and ample.”
On a certain day of a certain month in the first year of Xining, I humbly received Your Majesty’s gracious appointment as Vice Administrator of Affairs of State.
Assisting in governance at the great scales of state, I share the honor of service in the painted offices; helping to harmonize the contents of the sacrificial cauldron, I enjoy the favor of a position close to the imperial Purple Hall. I reflect that I have already presumed excessively upon offices I unworthily occupy, yet recognize that I am not permitted to decline. Receiving the appointment, I am flustered; searching my heart, I perspire with shame. Your servant, truly trembling and fearful, bows his head and knocks it upon the ground.
I humbly consider that responsibility for the central levers of government properly rests with the chief councilors; yet their diligent deliberations especially depend upon collaborative assistance. Taking turns in charge of the seal, these assisting officials support deliberations at court, mirroring the Three Terraces in the heavens. Signing imperial decrees with their titles alongside those of the chief councilors, they act for the heads of court government and rank among the Eight Seats. The title originated in the Qiande era, and the rank [?] was further settled in the Yongxi era. Such an exalted position should surely belong to a man of outstanding reputation.
I humbly reflect that my nature is awkward and blunt, my native capacity careless and mediocre. Beginning my official career in Pingjiang, I undeservedly acquired a reputation for redressing unjust cases …

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
配民昌邑甫未寬留檄之憂驟晉臺官遂當
言路恥曲學而阿世屢效狂愚期直道以
事
君自干罪謫荷生成於
大造重以護使之勤仗忠信於危波猶席清
淮之慶雖險阻艱難備嘗之矣矢沒齒於
江鄉而造次顛沛必於是焉敢貽書於政
府仰
仁皇之寬宥不次甄遷繼
===
英君之采收曲加勉
諭內省竟淪於孤迹何圖亦記於
淵衷起郡符以總憲樞徒為歲月之積職韜
鈐以扞邊圉祗貽尸素之羞惟太原之奧
區據代朔之重地誤蒙付委靡卽棄捐方
慙有負於北門遽爾超陪乎西掖
恩深莫旣感極何言茲蓋伏遇
〇〇〇〇
道協舜華
punctuated: 配民昌邑，甫未寬留檄之憂，驟晉臺官，遂當言路。恥曲學而阿世，屢效狂愚；期直道以事君，自干罪謫。荷生成於大造，重以護使之勤；仗忠信於危波，猶席清淮之慶。雖險阻艱難備嘗之矣，矢沒齒於江鄉；而造次顛沛必於是焉，敢貽書於政府？仰仁皇之寬宥，不次甄遷；繼英君之采收，曲加勉諭。內省竟淪於孤迹，何圖亦記於淵衷！起郡符以總憲樞，徒為歲月之積；職韜鈐以扞邊圉，祗貽尸素之羞。惟太原之奧區，據代朔之重地，誤蒙付委，靡卽棄捐。方慙有負於北門，遽爾超陪乎西掖。恩深莫旣，感極何言！茲蓋伏遇〇〇〇〇，道協舜華。
translation_en:
…Assigned among the people of Changyi [?], I had scarcely found relief from the anxiety of the order detaining me [?] when I was suddenly promoted to serve as a censor and thus assumed responsibility for remonstrance. Ashamed to distort learning to curry favor with the age, I repeatedly offered my rash and foolish views; hoping to serve my sovereign by the upright Way, I brought punishment and demotion upon myself. Through your vast, nurturing grace I received life anew and was further charged with the arduous duty of escorting envoys. Relying on loyalty and trustworthiness amid perilous waves, I still enjoyed the blessing of a tranquil Huai River [?]. Though I had experienced every danger and hardship, I vowed to end my days in my riverside home. Even in haste and distress I remained steadfast in this resolve: how would I dare send letters to the chief ministers?

I benefited from Emperor Renzong’s generous pardon and was selected for promotion outside the regular order. Subsequently, an illustrious sovereign took me into service and graciously bestowed encouragement and instruction. Looking within, I thought I had sunk at last into lonely obscurity; who could have imagined that I remained in your profound imperial thoughts? Raised from administering a prefecture to direct the Censorate, I merely accumulated years of service. Charged with military command to defend the frontier, I incurred only the shame of holding office idly and drawing an unearned salary. Taiyuan, that strategically sheltered region, occupies the vital territory of Dai and Shuo. Mistakenly entrusted with its charge, I was not immediately cast aside. Just as I felt ashamed of failing in my responsibility for the northern gateway, I was suddenly advanced to join the ranks of the western palace offices. Your grace is too profound to recount; my gratitude is too great for words!

This is because I have humbly had the good fortune to encounter 〇〇〇〇, whose Way accords with the splendor of Shun…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
志恢禹迹
至孝本於天縱
典學務於日新
霈兌澤以阜民尤軫一夫之不獲
極晉明而盡下尚虞片善之或遺謂綸閣之
深嚴難於獨用而政事之繁劇要在並觀
遂令疏逖之蹤亦忝延登之數先時髦而
取
召驚
===
鳳藻於
中天被
睿旨之叮嚀赫
龍光於
黼座論資校考豈云遺直之可稱揣分量能
蓋自
眷私之過厚矧
聖明奮大作之志恐莫裨於贊襄而羣工協勵
翼之休諒無庸於借聽將籲
punctuated: 志恢禹迹，至孝本於天縱，典學務於日新。霈兌澤以阜民，尤軫一夫之不獲；極晉明而盡下，尚虞片善之或遺。謂綸閣之深嚴難於獨用，而政事之繁劇要在並觀，遂令疏逖之蹤亦忝延登之數。先時髦而取召，驚鳳藻於中天；被睿旨之叮嚀，赫龍光於黼座。論資校考，豈云遺直之可稱？揣分量能，蓋自眷私之過厚。矧聖明奮大作之志，恐莫裨於贊襄；而羣工協勵翼之休，諒無庸於借聽。將籲
translation_en:
…Your ambition extends the achievements of Yu; your consummate filial devotion springs from Heaven’s endowment, and your pursuit of learning strives for daily renewal. You lavish beneficence upon the people to enrich their lives, especially mindful lest even one person fail to find his proper place. You extend your advancing radiance to all below, still fearing that even the smallest virtue might be overlooked. Considering that the secluded and august imperial drafting office can hardly depend upon one man alone, and that the complexity and urgency of government require the consideration of several perspectives, you have consequently allowed even your distant and insignificant servant to be included among those summoned and promoted.
Summoned ahead of the outstanding men of the age, I marvel at your phoenix-like literary splendor in mid-heaven; receiving the earnest injunctions of your sagely commands, I stand amid the radiant imperial favor before your embroidered throne. If my seniority and performance evaluations are examined, how could I be praised as one who preserves the uprightness of the ancients? Measuring my station and assessing my abilities, I can only attribute this to the excessive generosity of your personal favor. Moreover, Your sagely Majesty has roused your resolve to accomplish great undertakings, yet I fear I can contribute nothing toward their realization. The assembled officials work together in admirable, diligent support; surely there is no need to lend an ear to me [?]. I am about to appeal…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
第一問
周詩
同考試官教諭林批我
皇祖以詩爲教我
皇上妙契眞傳子能揚厲無遺其涵濡治化而歌詠太平者耶
考試官學正馮批皇極敷言之訓箕子以
告武王得道統之傳我
皇上心學淵源上符唐虞文武之盛此策敷陳精確必佳士也
考試官學正劉批詩可以興其功用甚大
===
觀子敷厲明悉其今之康衢順則者歟
聖人有至文之著以弘敷言之治必有至
道之凝以立建極之體何言乎文也著作
通於庶政以明教化以一風俗以經緯天
地者也何言乎道也精蘊具於一心以敘
彝倫以章物軌以綱維治理者也文不著
則不能以達政道不凝則不足以敷文夫
惟道以宅心而建其有極則敷之言也自
四達而不悖明徵而無疆矣此聖人所以
punctuated:
第一問

周詩

同考試官教諭林批：我皇祖以詩爲教，我皇上妙契眞傳。子能揚厲無遺，其涵濡治化而歌詠太平者耶？

考試官學正馮批：皇極敷言之訓，箕子以告武王，得道統之傳。我皇上心學淵源，上符唐虞文武之盛。此策敷陳精確，必佳士也。

考試官學正劉批：詩可以興，其功用甚大。觀子敷厲明悉，其今之康衢順則者歟？

聖人有至文之著，以弘敷言之治，必有至道之凝，以立建極之體。何言乎文也？著作通於庶政，以明教化，以一風俗，以經緯天地者也。何言乎道也？精蘊具於一心，以敘彝倫，以章物軌，以綱維治理者也。文不著，則不能以達政；道不凝，則不足以敷文。夫惟道以宅心而建其有極，則敷之言也，自四達而不悖，明徵而無疆矣。此聖人所以
translation_en:
First Question

Zhou Shi

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: Our imperial ancestor used poetry to teach, and our reigning emperor wondrously accords with its true transmission. You have expounded and exalted this without omission. Are you one who, steeped in the transforming influence of good government, sings of Great Peace?

Comment by Examiner Feng, Instructor: Jizi conveyed to King Wu the teaching concerning the promulgation of pronouncements on the Sovereign Ultimate, transmitting the succession of the Way. The deep sources of our emperor’s learning of the mind accord with the flourishing ages of Tang Yao, Yu Shun, and Kings Wen and Wu. This policy essay presents its arguments with precision: its author must be a worthy scholar.

Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: Poetry can stir the heart; its efficacy is very great. Your exposition is lucid and thorough. Are you a present-day counterpart of those who sang in Kangqu of following the constant norms?

When the sage manifests the highest literary expression to extend government through the promulgation of pronouncements, he must have the highest Way firmly concentrated within him, thereby establishing the substance of the supreme standard. What is meant here by literary expression? It is writing that reaches into all affairs of government, illuminating moral instruction, unifying customs, and ordering Heaven and Earth. What is meant here by the Way? Its essential profundities are fully present in the single mind, ordering the constant human relationships, making manifest the norms of things, and providing the guiding framework for government. Unless literary expression is manifest, government cannot be effectively communicated; unless the Way is firmly concentrated within, literary expression cannot adequately unfold. Only when the Way dwells in the mind and establishes its supreme standard will the pronouncements issuing from it naturally reach in all four directions without contradiction, be manifestly verified, and have no bounds. This is how the sage…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
獨觀昭曠之原而弘化於陶鈞之上者也
彼求工於聲律者藝焉爾矣烏足以語聖
人敷言之治哉猗歟休哉玆我
聖祖
皇上昭著作於詩篇妙感孚於道化者皆非淺
見陋聞所得而窺測賛揚者也蓋嘗誦典
謨而思堯舜歌雅頌而慕商周則詩之爲
敎其來遠矣自舜命官典樂設敎而曰詩
言志歌永言夫有虞盛時旣以此爲治本
===
又專官以爲之敎其所以育人才養性情
事神祇和上下而體用功效廣大深切者
豈偶然哉其在三代天子巡狩陳詩以觀
民風則載之王制以六詩敎天下則載之
周禮今皆不可槩見而僅存者孔子所刪
三百篇試取而誦之其溫柔敦厚猶能使
千載之下莫不興起則商周所以敷言弘
化者其風旨可想見矣然后夔以四德爲
敎大師以六德爲敎則聖人之躬行於上
punctuated:
獨觀昭曠之原，而弘化於陶鈞之上者也。彼求工於聲律者，藝焉爾矣，烏足以語聖人敷言之治哉！猗歟休哉！玆我聖祖、皇上，昭著作於詩篇，妙感孚於道化者，皆非淺見陋聞所得而窺測賛揚者也。
蓋嘗誦典謨而思堯舜，歌雅頌而慕商周，則詩之爲敎，其來遠矣。自舜命官典樂設敎，而曰：「詩言志，歌永言。」夫有虞盛時，旣以此爲治本，又專官以爲之敎，其所以育人才、養性情、事神祇、和上下，而體用功效廣大深切者，豈偶然哉？其在三代，天子巡狩，陳詩以觀民風，則載之《王制》；以六詩敎天下，則載之《周禮》。今皆不可槩見，而僅存者，孔子所刪三百篇。試取而誦之，其溫柔敦厚，猶能使千載之下莫不興起，則商周所以敷言弘化者，其風旨可想見矣。然后夔以四德爲敎，大師以六德爲敎，則聖人之躬行於上
translation_en:
…alone beholds the source of luminous vastness and extends transforming influence from his place above the potter’s wheel of creation. Those who seek merely to excel in tonal patterns practice only a craft; how could they be qualified to discuss the sage’s government through the dissemination of words? Ah, how glorious! Our sagely ancestor and His Majesty manifest their literary compositions in verse and wondrously inspire trust through the transforming influence of the Way. These achievements are beyond the capacity of those of shallow insight and limited learning to fathom or adequately praise.
When we recite the Canons and Counsels, we think of Yao and Shun; when we sing the Elegantiae and Hymns, we admire the Shang and Zhou. Poetry’s use in teaching thus has a long history. Shun appointed an official to direct music and establish instruction, saying: “Poetry expresses intent; song prolongs words.” In the flourishing age of Yu, poetry was already made a foundation of government, and a dedicated official was also appointed to teach it. Could it be mere chance that its substance, application, and effects were so expansive and profound in nurturing talent, cultivating human dispositions and feelings, serving the spirits of Heaven and Earth, and bringing harmony between superiors and inferiors? Under the Three Dynasties, when the Son of Heaven made tours of inspection, poems were presented so that he could observe the people’s customs: this is recorded in the “Royal Regulations.” Teaching the realm through the six kinds of poetry is recorded in the Rites of Zhou. These traditions can no longer be surveyed in their entirety; what survives is only the three hundred poems edited by Confucius. Try taking them up and reciting them: their gentleness, warmth, sincerity, and generosity can still stir everyone to moral aspiration even a thousand years later. From this we can envision the spirit and intent with which the Shang and Zhou disseminated words and extended their transforming influence. Then, too, Kui taught through the four virtues, and the Music Master taught through the six virtues; thus, as for the sage’s personal practice in his exalted position …

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
也必有其本獨藝焉已哉今考帝王之詩
莫過於皇極敷言之訓曰無偏無陂遵王
之義無有作好遵王之道無有作惡遵王
之路曰無偏無黨王道蕩蕩無黨無偏王
道平平無反無側王道正直曰會其有極
歸其有極歌咏以協其音反覆以致其意
而又歸宿以要其成則古人作詩之體備
是矣蓋先王之世敬天授時而五行順正
己檢身而五事脩豐財利民而八政舉脩
===
德致祥而五紀協以乂三德則剛柔正直
並用也以明稽疑則龜筮庶謀協同也以
驗庶徵則五氣時若也以徵福極則諸福
咸臻也是惟建其有極矣宜其著之詩篇
以敎天下者莫不是訓是行而歌咏太平
之澤不絕帝之所以帝王之所以王由此
其選也自平王東遷詩廢不講以及漢唐
而下非無作者若漢武帝秋風栢梁之句
唐太宗慶善臨朝之什魏文帝戒盈之賦
punctuated: 也，必有其本，獨藝焉已哉？今考帝王之詩，莫過於皇極敷言之訓，曰：「無偏無陂，遵王之義；無有作好，遵王之道；無有作惡，遵王之路。」曰：「無偏無黨，王道蕩蕩；無黨無偏，王道平平；無反無側，王道正直。」曰：「會其有極，歸其有極。」歌咏以協其音，反覆以致其意，而又歸宿以要其成，則古人作詩之體備是矣。蓋先王之世，敬天授時而五行順，正己檢身而五事脩，豐財利民而八政舉，脩德致祥而五紀協。以乂三德，則剛柔正直並用也；以明稽疑，則龜筮庶謀協同也；以驗庶徵，則五氣時若也；以徵福極，則諸福咸臻也。是惟建其有極矣，宜其著之詩篇以敎天下者，莫不是訓是行，而歌咏太平之澤不絕。帝之所以帝，王之所以王，由此其選也。自平王東遷，詩廢不講，以及漢唐而下，非無作者，若漢武帝《秋風》《栢梁》之句，唐太宗《慶善》《臨朝》之什，魏文帝《戒盈》之賦
translation_en:
…must have had its foundation. Could it have been merely a matter of artistic skill? Now, examining the poetry of emperors and kings, nothing surpasses the instructions proclaimed concerning the August Standard: “Without partiality or deviation, follow the king’s righteousness. Without cultivating personal likes, follow the king’s Way. Without cultivating personal dislikes, follow the king’s path.” Again: “Without partiality or faction, the king’s Way is broad and open. Without faction or partiality, the king’s Way is level and even. Without turning back or inclining to either side, the king’s Way is upright and straight.” Again: “Gather toward that standard; return to that standard.” Singing and chanting harmonize the sounds; repetition fully conveys the meaning; and a final return to the central point brings the whole to completion. Thus, the ancient manner of composing poetry is fully embodied here.

In the age of the former kings, reverence for Heaven and the promulgation of the seasons brought the Five Phases into proper order; rectifying themselves and disciplining their conduct brought the Five Personal Activities to perfection; increasing wealth and benefiting the people brought the Eight Affairs of Government into operation; and cultivating virtue and attracting auspicious signs brought the Five Divisions of Time into harmony. In governing through the Three Virtues, firmness, gentleness, and uprightness were all employed. In clarifying the resolution of doubts, divination by tortoise shell and milfoil agreed with the various counsels. In examining the manifold signs, the five atmospheric conditions followed their proper seasons. In assessing blessings and calamities, all blessings arrived together. This was indeed the establishment of the supreme standard. It was fitting that the poems they composed to teach the world should invariably inculcate and put into practice these principles, and that songs celebrating the blessings of great peace should never cease. What made emperors truly emperors and kings truly kings—their distinction—lay in this.

Since King Ping’s eastward relocation, poetry fell into neglect and ceased to be studied. Yet through the Han and Tang dynasties and thereafter, there was no lack of authors: for example, Emperor Wu of Han’s verses on the Autumn Wind and the Cypress Terrace; Emperor Taizong of Tang’s poems on Celebrating Goodness and Holding Court; and Emperor Wen of Wei’s rhapsody Admonition against Complacency…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
非帝王爲治之要道乎我
文皇所著如輯
爲善陰隲
孝順事實二書以
訓天下且各
咏以詩其題放鶉療鶴則有所謂全生不殺
有陰功窮託神人救餘命者也其題躍魚
出鯉則有所謂孝道能敦在穉年舍側出
泉誠異事者也而
===
序以一念之善通於神明非推天而驗之人
者乎大哉
皇言郁乎琬琰而皆切於民彝蓋與敷言之訓
相爲經緯非徒延光將來比榮往號而已
也肆天下家傳人誦寡過而歸極淳風熈
洽聲敎宣流天下太和者垂百八十餘年
於茲矣迨我
皇上欽明神聖應運
中興恢弘
punctuated: 非帝王爲治之要道乎？我文皇所著如輯《爲善陰隲》《孝順事實》二書，以訓天下，且各咏以詩。其題放鶉、療鶴，則有所謂「全生不殺有陰功」「窮託神人救餘命」者也；其題躍魚、出鯉，則有所謂「孝道能敦在穉年」「舍側出泉誠異事」者也。而序以「一念之善通於神明」，非推天而驗之人者乎？大哉皇言！郁乎琬琰，而皆切於民彝，蓋與敷言之訓相爲經緯，非徒延光將來、比榮往號而已也。肆天下家傳人誦，寡過而歸極，淳風熈洽，聲敎宣流，天下太和者垂百八十餘年於茲矣。迨我皇上欽明神聖，應運中興，恢弘
translation_en:
… Is this not an essential way for emperors and kings to govern? Among the writings of our Emperor Wen were such compilations as Hidden Recompense for Doing Good (Weishan yinzhi) and True Accounts of Filial Obedience (Xiaoshun shishi), two books intended to instruct all under Heaven; he also celebrated their individual accounts in verse. His poems on releasing quails and healing a crane contain the lines, “Preserving life without killing brings hidden merit,” and “In distress, appealing to a divine being to save what remains of life.” Those on leaping fish and the appearance of carp contain the lines, “Filial devotion can be earnestly practiced even in tender years,” and “A spring emerging beside the house is truly a wondrous occurrence.” And in the preface he wrote, “A single good thought communicates with the spirits.” Is this not an inference from Heaven verified in human affairs?

Great indeed are the imperial words! Resplendent as precious jade tablets, they all bear directly upon the enduring moral norms of the people. They interweave with the teachings promulgated in imperial pronouncements; they do more than merely extend his glory into the future and match the renown of former sovereigns. Thus, throughout the realm, households have transmitted them and individuals recited them, reducing their faults and returning to the highest standard. Pure customs have flourished in harmony, and his moral influence and instruction have spread far and wide. By now, this great peace throughout the realm has endured for some hundred and eighty years and more.

Now our present Emperor, reverent and enlightened, divinely sagacious, has responded to the destined time by bringing about a restoration, expanding …

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
聖業大新物覩慨然
慕古六詩之義而發爲篇章形于諷誦者尤
未易殫述是故
平臺有咏勵臣鄰也
大報有歌揚洪眷也除夕有作崇脩省也感
雨有吟恤民隱也
天藻奎章紛綸葳蕤蔚乎盛矣又嘗因儒臣進
講大學衍義感賦五言古詩十韻
君倡臣和彙爲一帙總名之曰翊學詩竊嘗伏
===
讀一二曰致治貴有本本端化自平曰正
心誠其意志定必不遷卽蕩蕩平平之義
也曰身脩本心正家國治同然曰國治乃
昭明萬邦斯協焉卽會極歸極之義也曰
於變帝堯典思齊文王篇曰萬化脩身始
朕念方拳拳卽皇建有極之義也旣又
親灑
宸翰以
賜輔臣而一時賡和之詞莫非皇極敷言之
punctuated: 聖業，大新物覩，慨然慕古六詩之義，而發爲篇章、形于諷誦者，尤未易殫述。是故平臺有咏，勵臣鄰也；大報有歌，揚洪眷也；除夕有作，崇脩省也；感雨有吟，恤民隱也。天藻奎章，紛綸葳蕤，蔚乎盛矣！又嘗因儒臣進講《大學衍義》，感賦五言古詩十韻，君倡臣和，彙爲一帙，總名之曰《翊學詩》。竊嘗伏讀一二，曰：「致治貴有本，本端化自平。」曰：「正心誠其意，志定必不遷。」卽蕩蕩平平之義也。曰：「身脩本心正，家國治同然。」曰：「國治乃昭明，萬邦斯協焉。」卽會極歸極之義也。曰：「於變帝堯典，思齊文王篇。」曰：「萬化脩身始，朕念方拳拳。」卽皇建有極之義也。旣又親灑宸翰，以賜輔臣，而一時賡和之詞，莫非皇極敷言之
translation_en:
…the sage enterprise, bringing about a great renewal for all to behold. Earnestly admiring the purport of the six forms of ancient poetry, he expressed it in compositions to be recited and chanted; these are especially difficult to recount exhaustively. Thus his verses on the Level Terrace encouraged his attendant ministers; his song on the Great Sacrifice of Recompense proclaimed Heaven’s abundant favor; his composition on New Year’s Eve promoted self-cultivation and self-examination; and his verses inspired by rain expressed concern for the people’s hidden sufferings. His celestial compositions, writings radiant as the literary constellation Kui, were abundant and luxuriant—magnificent indeed!
On another occasion, prompted by a lecture delivered by Confucian court officials on the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning (Daxue yanyi), he was moved to compose an ancient-style poem in five-character lines with ten rhymes. The sovereign initiated the verse and his ministers composed responses. These were collected in one volume, collectively entitled Poems to Aid Learning (Yixue shi). I have humbly read some of them with reverence. One passage says: “To achieve good government, what matters is a foundation; / When the foundation is correct, transformation naturally brings peace.” Another says: “Rectify the mind and make its intentions sincere; / With resolve established, one surely will not waver.” These express the meaning of “broad and expansive, even and level.” Another says: “Cultivating the person rests on rectifying the mind; / Ordering the family and state follows the same principle.” Another says: “When the state is ordered, there is radiant clarity; / The myriad states then dwell in harmony.” These express the meaning of “gathering at the ultimate standard” and “returning to the ultimate standard.” Another says: “‘Oh, how they were transformed!’—the Canon of Emperor Yao; / ‘Think of emulating him’—the ode to King Wen.” Another says: “All transformation begins with cultivating the person; / My thoughts are earnestly fixed upon this.” These express the meaning of “the sovereign establishes the ultimate standard.”
Thereafter, he personally wrote out his imperial calligraphy and bestowed it upon his chief ministers. The responding verses composed at that time were all …

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
旹我
皇上所以闡明詩敎囿天下于皇極而遠追三
百篇之轍者無不會其精深詣其純粹故
二紀以來遵道者丕變覩
聖者奕新而
大典微言揭如日星
鴻恩濊澤同乎天地所以上符
二祖遠繼唐虞三代之盛者端見於此而非漢
唐宋諸君之所敢望矣然執事猶拳拳下
===
問欲歌咏其一二用宣揚
聖明蕩蕩平平之化愚又何言哉蓋古之忠愛
之臣務賛揚其君之美凡以風天下後世
俾其習於耳浹於心而不忘也故有周盛
時濟濟多士一則曰周王壽考遐不作人
一則曰古之人無斁譽髦斯士所以咏歌
文王之德者凡以歸極也今
皇上躬親師帥以詩敎天下固已光四表而格
上下矣然豈無其本哉仰惟
punctuated: 旹，我皇上所以闡明詩敎，囿天下于皇極，而遠追三百篇之轍者，無不會其精深，詣其純粹。故二紀以來，遵道者丕變，覩聖者奕新，而大典微言揭如日星，鴻恩濊澤同乎天地。所以上符二祖，遠繼唐虞三代之盛者，端見於此，而非漢唐宋諸君之所敢望矣。然執事猶拳拳下問，欲歌咏其一二，用宣揚聖明蕩蕩平平之化，愚又何言哉？蓋古之忠愛之臣，務賛揚其君之美，凡以風天下後世，俾其習於耳，浹於心而不忘也。故有周盛時，濟濟多士，一則曰：「周王壽考，遐不作人。」一則曰：「古之人無斁，譽髦斯士。」所以咏歌文王之德者，凡以歸極也。今皇上躬親師帥，以詩敎天下，固已光四表而格上下矣。然豈無其本哉？仰惟
translation_en:
…at that time, the means by which Our Emperor elucidated the teaching of the Odes, brought all under Heaven within the Supreme Standard of sovereignty, and followed the distant tracks of the Three Hundred Odes invariably grasped their profound essence and attained their utmost purity. Thus, over these twenty-four years, those who follow the Way have been greatly transformed, and those who behold the sage have been splendidly renewed. The subtle teachings of the great canon shine forth like the sun and stars; his vast kindness and abundant beneficence equal Heaven and Earth. Here precisely we see how he accords with the Two Ancestral Emperors and carries forward the distant flourishing of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties—something the rulers of the Han, Tang, and Song could never dare hope to match.

Yet you still earnestly condescend to ask, wishing to sing of one or two of these achievements and thereby proclaim the vast and impartial transforming influence of our sagely, enlightened ruler. What more can one as ignorant as I say? Loyal and devoted ministers of antiquity sought to praise their rulers’ virtues, always intending thereby to influence all under Heaven and later generations, so that these virtues would become familiar to their ears, permeate their hearts, and never be forgotten. Thus, in the flourishing age of Zhou, with its multitude of worthy men, one ode declared: “May the king of Zhou live long! Has he not nurtured men?” Another declared: “The men of old never wearied of honoring and fostering these scholars.” Their purpose in singing the virtue of King Wen was always to bring people to the Supreme Standard.

Now Our Emperor personally serves as teacher and leader, instructing all under Heaven through the Odes. His radiance has indeed already reached the four outer bounds and extended to Heaven above and Earth below. Yet could this be without a foundation? Reverently considering…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
天縱之資獨超千古
日新之德遠邁百王首制
明倫大典一書推明統嗣之不同詳論義情
之兼盡則人極立而天下之綱常以定又
製爲
敬一之箴致謹於
郊廟天人之際益密於言行始終之常則
聖學煕而千聖之心法以傳由是以至道之凝
敷之於文則天下優游涵泳浹洽薫蒸而
===
歸于有極者孰不咏歌
聖明作人之澤於萬年也哉愚生躬逢
盛世竊伏海邦叨被
敎化有年矣思欲操觚翰以繪造化顧
廣大淵微有未易以形容者倘執事引而進之
尚當述天保鳧鷖之盛以揄揚其萬一不
敢諉於願學而未能也
第二問
邵型
punctuated:
天縱之資，獨超千古；日新之德，遠邁百王。首制《明倫大典》一書，推明統嗣之不同，詳論義情之兼盡，則人極立而天下之綱常以定。又製爲《敬一》之箴，致謹於郊廟天人之際，益密於言行始終之常，則聖學煕而千聖之心法以傳。由是以至道之凝，敷之於文，則天下優游涵泳，浹洽薫蒸，而歸于有極者，孰不咏歌聖明作人之澤於萬年也哉！愚生躬逢盛世，竊伏海邦，叨被敎化有年矣。思欲操觚翰以繪造化，顧廣大淵微，有未易以形容者。倘執事引而進之，尚當述《天保》《鳧鷖》之盛，以揄揚其萬一，不敢諉於願學而未能也。

第二問
邵型
translation_en:
…Your Heaven-bestowed gifts uniquely surpass all antiquity, and your daily renewed virtue far excels that of the hundred kings. You first composed the Great Compendium on Clarifying Human Relations (Minglun dadian), elucidating the distinction between succession to the imperial line and succession as an heir, and discussing in detail how moral duty and familial feeling could both be fully satisfied. Thus the highest standard for humanity was established, and the cardinal bonds and constant virtues of the world were settled. You also composed the Admonition on Reverent Unity (Jingyi), exercising care in the encounters between Heaven and humanity at the suburban altars and ancestral temples, and attending ever more closely to the constant principles governing speech and conduct from beginning to end. Thus sagely learning flourished, and the essential teaching of the minds of a thousand sages was transmitted. From this concentration of the supreme Way, you spread it through writings. All under Heaven dwell at ease within its influence, steeped and saturated in it, and return to the highest standard. Who among them would not sing for ten thousand years of the enlightened sage ruler’s bounty in nurturing men of talent?

I, an unworthy student, have personally encountered this flourishing age. Humbly dwelling in this coastal region, I have undeservedly received your civilizing instruction for many years. I wish to take up writing tablet and brush to depict your creative transformation; yet its breadth and profundity, its depth and subtlety, are not easily described. If you, honored examiners, should draw me forward and advance me, I shall further recount splendors such as those celebrated in “Heaven Protects” (Tianbao) and “Wild Ducks and Gulls” (Fuyi), to extol even one ten-thousandth of them. I dare not excuse myself by saying that I wish to learn but am not yet capable.

Second Question
Shao Xing

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
同考試官敎諭倪批律呂之法義理深奧子
能據實條陳辨析秋毫可以占該博之學矣
考試官學正馮批候氣以定律審音以知
樂此作敘述明確真知言哉
考試官學正劉批窮理之學
夫樂之用廣矣大矣所以同民心而出治
道者也然其作之也有本其正之也有法
政善民安天下太和此作樂之本也本自
然之氣以定律因一定之律以審音此正
===
樂之法也是故假音以宣和而不倚於音
也必求乎審音之法本和以作樂而不徒
爲和也必求乎致和之道則和以定律律
以審音比音而樂之以成樂以合天地以
和神人天下化中治於是乎成矣不狀音
爲乖戾之音而所謂和者非天地之太和
又何以作樂也哉執事發策詳究正樂之
法而終及馬遷律書之旨蓋以此也夫作
樂果有本乎樂云樂云鐘鼓云乎哉孔子
punctuated:
同考試官敎諭倪批：律呂之法，義理深奧，子能據實條陳，辨析秋毫，可以占該博之學矣。
考試官學正馮批：候氣以定律，審音以知樂，此作敘述明確，真知言哉！
考試官學正劉批：窮理之學。
夫樂之用，廣矣大矣，所以同民心而出治道者也。然其作之也有本，其正之也有法。政善民安，天下太和，此作樂之本也。本自然之氣以定律，因一定之律以審音，此正樂之法也。是故假音以宣和，而不倚於音也，必求乎審音之法；本和以作樂，而不徒爲和也，必求乎致和之道。則和以定律，律以審音，比音而樂之，以成樂，以合天地，以和神人，天下化中，治於是乎成矣。不狀音爲乖戾之音，而所謂和者非天地之太和，又何以作樂也哉？執事發策，詳究正樂之法，而終及馬遷《律書》之旨，蓋以此也。夫作樂果有本乎？「樂云樂云，鐘鼓云乎哉？」孔子
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Ni, Instructor, comments: “The principles underlying the methods of the pitch standards are profound. You have set them out point by point on a factual basis and distinguished their finest details. This reveals the breadth of your learning.”
Examiner Feng, Instructor, comments: “Observing qi to establish pitch standards, examining tones to understand music: this composition explains these matters clearly and precisely. These truly are words of understanding!”
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: “Learning that probes principles to their utmost.”
The uses of music are broad and great indeed. Through it, the people’s hearts are brought into accord and the Way of governance emerges. Yet making music has a foundation, and rectifying it has a method. Good government, a people at peace, and supreme harmony throughout the realm: these are the foundation of making music. Establishing pitch standards on the basis of naturally occurring qi, and examining tones according to fixed pitch standards: this is the method of rectifying music. Thus, to employ tones to express harmony without depending solely upon tones, one must seek the method of examining them. To make music on the basis of harmony without merely putting on a semblance of harmony, one must seek the Way of bringing harmony about. Then harmony establishes pitch standards, and pitch standards provide the basis for examining tones. The tones are arranged and performed to form music, bringing Heaven and Earth into accord and harmonizing spirits and human beings. All under Heaven are transformed toward the mean, and good order is thereby achieved. If the tones become discordant [?], and what is called harmony is not the supreme harmony of Heaven and Earth, how could music be made? This, surely, is why you gentlemen, in posing your policy question, investigate in detail the method of rectifying music and conclude by addressing the purport of Ma Qian’s (Sima Qian’s) Treatise on the Pitch Standards.
Does making music indeed have a foundation? “Music, music—is it merely bells and drums that are meant?” Confucius …

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
蓋甞言之矣作樂抑有法乎聖人旣竭耳
力焉繼之以六律正五音不可勝用也孟
子蓋甞言之矣是二者之於樂雖有先後
緩急之殊要皆不可以偏廢焉者故知正
樂之法而不知其本固不可以成樂使知
正樂而不先求聲氣之元則雖斷竹鑄鐘
窮日夜之力以較其合否亦見其徒勞焉
耳嗚呼知此可與論樂矣愚也請先窮其
法而後及其本可乎蓋自黃帝命伶倫取
===
嶰谷之竹斷兩節而吹之以聽鳳凰之鳴
其雄鳴六者屬陽爲律曰黃鐘太簇姑洗
蕤賓夷則亡射是也雌鳴六者屬陰爲呂
曰大呂夾鐘仲呂林鐘南呂應鐘是也此
律呂之法所自起也然黃帝之律豈假物
而强制者哉蓋其垂衣裳而天下治至和
浹洽鳳鳥來鳴是爲和氣之應故聽之以
制律班固所謂至治之世天地之氣合以
生風天地之風氣正則十二律定此之謂
punctuated: 蓋甞言之矣。作樂抑有法乎？「聖人旣竭耳力焉，繼之以六律，正五音，不可勝用也。」孟子蓋甞言之矣。是二者之於樂，雖有先後緩急之殊，要皆不可以偏廢焉者。故知正樂之法而不知其本，固不可以成樂；使知正樂而不先求聲氣之元，則雖斷竹鑄鐘，窮日夜之力以較其合否，亦見其徒勞焉耳。嗚呼！知此可與論樂矣。愚也請先窮其法而後及其本，可乎？蓋自黃帝命伶倫取嶰谷之竹，斷兩節而吹之，以聽鳳凰之鳴，其雄鳴六者屬陽爲律，曰黃鐘、太簇、姑洗、蕤賓、夷則、亡射，是也；雌鳴六者屬陰爲呂，曰大呂、夾鐘、仲呂、林鐘、南呂、應鐘，是也。此律呂之法所自起也。然黃帝之律，豈假物而强制者哉？蓋其垂衣裳而天下治，至和浹洽，鳳鳥來鳴，是爲和氣之應，故聽之以制律。班固所謂「至治之世，天地之氣合以生風，天地之風氣正，則十二律定」，此之謂
translation_en:
…had indeed spoken of this. Yet are there also methods for making music? “When the sage has exhausted the powers of his hearing, he follows this with the six pitch standards to regulate the five notes, and their uses are inexhaustible.” Mengzi indeed said this. Although these two aspects of music differ in their order and urgency, neither may be neglected in favor of the other. Thus, knowing the methods for rectifying music without knowing its foundation certainly cannot bring music to completion. Even if one knows how to rectify music, unless one first seeks the source of sound and vital energy, then, though one cuts bamboo and casts bells, exhausting one’s strength day and night to test whether they accord, one will merely labor in vain. Ah! With someone who understands this, one can discuss music. May I, in my humble ignorance, first investigate its methods fully and then turn to its foundation?

It began when Huangdi, the Yellow Emperor, ordered Ling Lun to take bamboo from Xiegu, cut it at two joints, and blow it, listening to the cries of the phoenixes. The male’s six cries belonged to yang and became the lü pitch standards: Huangzhong, Taicu, Guxian, Ruibin, Yize, and Wuyi. The female’s six cries belonged to yin and became the lǚ pitch standards: Dalü, Jiazhong, Zhonglü, Linzhong, Nanlü, and Yingzhong. This was the origin of the system of the twelve pitch standards. Yet were Huangdi’s pitch standards something forcibly contrived by resorting to material objects? Rather, he let his robes hang down, and the world was well governed; perfect harmony permeated everything, and phoenixes came to sing. This was a response to the harmonious vital energy, so he listened to them to establish the pitch standards. As Ban Gu said, “In an age of perfect government, the vital energies of Heaven and Earth unite to produce wind; when the winds and vital energies of Heaven and Earth are correct, the twelve pitch standards are fixed.” This is what is meant…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
也是故論其名義則黃者中之色君之服
也鐘者種也陽氣生於黃泉孳萌萬物爲
六氣元也以黃色名元氣律者著宮聲也
大呂旅也簇奏也夾助也姑辜也洗潔也
所以取其旅助黃鐘宣氣而生物者也仲
呂旅也蕤繼也賓導也林君也則法也南
任也射厭也應應也所以取其宣導陰氣
助陽而成物者也此十二律之名義也論
其起數則黃鐘之管長九十黍之廣積九
===
寸而度生焉容千二百黍積八百一十分
而量生焉重十有二銖而權衡生焉夫律
固可以制度量衡而考度量衡以一天下
之爭平天下之情聖人致和定律之本不
於是乎在耶論其測候則重室閉戸布以
緹縵實以葭灰桉律候之以動之大小遲
速驗風氣之和否此候氣之法所由施也
夫律者陽氣之動陽聲之始必聲和氣應
然後可以見天地之心聖人順時正樂以
punctuated:
也。是故，論其名義，則黃者，中之色、君之服也；鐘者，種也。陽氣生於黃泉，孳萌萬物，爲六氣元也。以黃色名元氣律者，著宮聲也。大呂，旅也；簇，奏也；夾，助也；姑，辜也；洗，潔也。所以取其旅助黃鐘，宣氣而生物者也。仲呂，旅也；蕤，繼也；賓，導也；林，君也；則，法也；南，任也；射，厭也；應，應也。所以取其宣導陰氣，助陽而成物者也。此十二律之名義也。
論其起數，則黃鐘之管長九十黍之廣，積九寸，而度生焉；容千二百黍，積八百一十分，而量生焉；重十有二銖，而權衡生焉。夫律固可以制度量衡，而考度量衡，以一天下之爭，平天下之情，聖人致和定律之本，不於是乎在耶？
論其測候，則重室閉戸，布以緹縵，實以葭灰，桉律候之，以動之大小遲速，驗風氣之和否。此候氣之法所由施也。夫律者，陽氣之動、陽聲之始，必聲和氣應，然後可以見天地之心。聖人順時正樂以
translation_en:
…such is its meaning. Thus, to discuss the meanings of their names: huang, “yellow,” is the color of the center and of the ruler’s robes; zhong, “bell,” means “seed.” Yang qi arises in the Yellow Springs beneath the earth and germinates the myriad things, serving as the origin of the six qi. Naming the pitch standard of primordial qi after the color yellow makes manifest the gong tone. In Dalu, lü means “assemble”; cu means “perform”; jia means “assist”; gu means “fault” [?]; and xian means “cleanse.” These meanings are adopted because these pitches collectively assist Huangzhong, disseminating qi and bringing things into being. In Zhonglü, lü means “assemble”; rui means “continue”; bin means “guide”; lin means “ruler”; ze means “rule”; nan means “bear”; yi means “satiate”; and ying means “respond.” These meanings are adopted because these pitches disseminate and guide yin qi, assisting yang in bringing things to completion. Such are the meanings of the names of the twelve pitch standards.
To discuss the derivation of their numerical measures: the Huangzhong pitch pipe is ninety millet-grain widths long, totaling nine cun, and from this comes the measure of length. It holds twelve hundred millet grains, totaling eight hundred and ten fen of volume, and from this comes the measure of capacity. Their weight is twelve zhu, and from this come the weight standards and the balance. Pitch standards can indeed establish measures of length, capacity, and weight. By checking these measures, one settles disputes throughout the realm and brings fairness to the dealings of its people. Does not the fundamental purpose of the sages in bringing about harmony and fixing pitch standards lie here?
To discuss their use in observation: the doors of an inner chamber are closed, reddish silk is spread out, and the pitch pipes are filled with reed-pith ash. Observations are made according to the pitch standards; the magnitude and speed of the ash’s movement reveal whether the winds and qi are harmonious. This is how the method of observing qi is put into practice. Pitch standards represent the movement of yang qi and the beginning of yang sound. Only when sounds are harmonious and qi responds can the heart of Heaven and Earth be perceived. The sages follow the seasons and rectify music so as to…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
合天地者不於是乎在耶至於律之所謂
上生下生者蓋先王因天地陰陽之氣辨
十有二辰而生十有二律其長短有度損
益有宜以陽律起數以陰律成之每三分
而損益隔八位而相生所謂娶妻生子之
說其理深矣故黃鐘損一下生林鐘林鐘
益一上生太簇循是相生至於仲呂以成
一終而所以損陽生陰益陰生陽之數無
不備焉此比次降殺之序乃陰陽消長之
===
機非巧筭者所能爲也其所謂旋相爲宮
者蓋十二律所以配十二月各有用事之
辰故得旋相爲宮然多寡有數輕重有權
以正變相運而以減半節之使黃鐘有常
尊諸律不得以相凌所謂同心一統之義
其理微矣故黃鐘爲宮則林鐘諸律以次
而應之以全分之正聲林鐘爲宮則太簇
諸律以次而應之以減半之子聲此尊卑
隆殺之法天地自然之分非拘執者所能
punctuated: 合天地者，不於是乎在耶？至於律之所謂上生下生者，蓋先王因天地陰陽之氣，辨十有二辰而生十有二律。其長短有度，損益有宜，以陽律起數，以陰律成之，每三分而損益，隔八位而相生。所謂娶妻生子之說，其理深矣。故黃鐘損一下生林鐘，林鐘益一上生太簇，循是相生，至於仲呂，以成一終，而所以損陽生陰、益陰生陽之數無不備焉。此比次降殺之序，乃陰陽消長之機，非巧筭者所能爲也。其所謂旋相爲宮者，蓋十二律所以配十二月，各有用事之辰，故得旋相爲宮。然多寡有數，輕重有權，以正變相運，而以減半節之，使黃鐘有常尊，諸律不得以相凌。所謂同心一統之義，其理微矣。故黃鐘爲宮，則林鐘諸律以次而應之，以全分之正聲；林鐘爲宮，則太簇諸律以次而應之，以減半之子聲。此尊卑隆殺之法，天地自然之分，非拘執者所能
translation_en:
…to accord with Heaven and Earth—is this not where its purpose lies? As for what pitch theory calls “upward generation” and “downward generation,” the former kings followed the yin and yang vital energies of Heaven and Earth, distinguished the twelve temporal stations, and generated the twelve pitch standards. Their lengths have prescribed measures, and their reductions and augmentations are appropriate: the numerical sequence begins with a yang pitch and is completed with a yin pitch. Each length is divided into three parts and then reduced or augmented by one part; successive pitches generate one another at an interval of eight positions. The principle behind the so-called “taking a wife and begetting a son” theory is profound indeed. Thus Huangzhong is reduced by one part to generate Linzhong downward; Linzhong is augmented by one part to generate Taicu upward. Generation proceeds in this way until Zhonglü is reached, completing one cycle. All the numerical operations by which yang is reduced to generate yin and yin is augmented to generate yang are thereby fully embodied. This ordered sequence of gradations is the working of yin and yang as they wane and wax; it is not something that clever calculators could contrive.

As for what is called “serving in rotation as gong,” the twelve pitch standards correspond to the twelve months, each having its own time of ascendancy; hence each can serve in turn as gong, the tonal center. Yet greater and lesser quantities have their numerical rules, and lighter and heavier values have their balancing measures. The regular and altered tones operate in conjunction, regulated by halving, so that Huangzhong retains its constant supremacy and the other pitches cannot encroach upon one another. The principle behind the so-called “unity of purpose under a single rule” is subtle indeed. Thus, when Huangzhong serves as gong, Linzhong and the other pitches respond in sequence with the regular tones of their full lengths; when Linzhong serves as gong, Taicu and the other pitches respond in sequence with the “child tones” produced by halving their lengths. This rule of higher and lower rank, of elevation and diminution, is a natural ordering of Heaven and Earth, something that those bound by rigid adherence cannot…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
同矣況元帝何時而汲汲於言律以審音
哉逮宋元嘉中太史錢樂之又以京房六
十律相生之法更生三百律以當三百六
十之策其法視京房爲益詳然相生之法
猶夫房也安得與古制同乎矧元嘉之時
比元帝又遠矣夫聖王制律必求聲氣之
元故太史公曰細若氣微若聲聖人因神
而存之雖妙必效言黃鐘始於聲氣之元
非律生於黍也而漢志隋書及房庶之徒
===
乃以古人皆累黍爲尺以制律而爲縱橫
長短之說其謬已甚若乃易竹用銅取其
同天下之風俗以準伐竹取其審聲音之
易達似有益於樂者然亦後代之制非古
先王之法也以至阮咸荀勗之徒雖負神
解暗解之名類恃器數之末而不求聲氣
之元已不得定律之法而況望其識制律
之意如馬遷乎宋范鎮曰樂者和氣也發
和氣者聲音也古人以有形之物傳其法
punctuated: 同矣。況元帝何時，而汲汲於言律以審音哉？逮宋元嘉中，太史錢樂之又以京房六十律相生之法，更生三百律，以當三百六十之策。其法視京房爲益詳，然相生之法猶夫房也，安得與古制同乎？矧元嘉之時，比元帝又遠矣。夫聖王制律，必求聲氣之元。故太史公曰：「細若氣，微若聲，聖人因神而存之，雖妙必效。」言黃鐘始於聲氣之元，非律生於黍也。而漢志、隋書及房庶之徒，乃以古人皆累黍爲尺以制律，而爲縱橫長短之說，其謬已甚。若乃易竹用銅，取其同天下之風俗；以準伐竹，取其審聲音之易達，似有益於樂者。然亦後代之制，非古先王之法也。以至阮咸、荀勗之徒，雖負神解、暗解之名，類恃器數之末，而不求聲氣之元，已不得定律之法，而況望其識制律之意如馬遷乎？宋范鎮曰：「樂者，和氣也；發和氣者，聲音也。古人以有形之物傳其法
translation_en:
…were the same. Moreover, in what age did Emperor Yuan live, that he should be so intent on discussing pitch standards to determine musical tones? During the Yuanjia reign of the Song dynasty, the Grand Astrologer Qian Lezhi further employed Jing Fang’s method of successively generating sixty pitch standards to generate another three hundred, corresponding to the three hundred and sixty counting stalks. His method was more elaborate than Jing Fang’s, yet its procedure of successive generation remained Jing Fang’s own. How could it be identical to the ancient system? Besides, the Yuanjia period was even further removed from antiquity than Emperor Yuan’s time.

When the sage kings established pitch standards, they necessarily sought the origin of sound and vital breath. Thus the Grand Historian said: “As fine as breath, as subtle as sound: the sage follows its spiritual workings and preserves it; though elusive, it must yield perceptible effects.” This means that the Yellow Bell pitch begins in the origin of sound and vital breath, not that pitch standards arise from millet grains. Yet the treatises in the History of the Han, the History of the Sui, and men such as Fang Shu maintained that the ancients all piled millet grains to establish a measuring foot with which to construct pitch pipes. They accordingly advanced theories about arranging the grains lengthwise or crosswise and about the resulting lengths. Their error was already grave indeed.

As for replacing bamboo with bronze, the aim was to make customs uniform throughout the realm; using a tuning standard to cut bamboo [?] was intended to make the determination of musical tones readily accessible. These practices appear beneficial to music. Nevertheless, they too were institutions of later ages, not the methods of the ancient kings. Even men such as Ruan Xian and Xun Xu, though renowned for inspired or intuitive understanding, generally relied on the secondary matters of instruments and numerical measures, without seeking the origin of sound and vital breath. They thus failed even to grasp the method of fixing pitch standards. How much less could one expect them to understand the purpose of establishing those standards as Sima Qian did?

Fan Zhen of the Song said: “Music is harmonious vital breath; what gives expression to harmonious vital breath is sound. The ancients transmitted their methods through tangible objects …

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
然後無形之聲音得而和氣可道有形者
秬黍也律也尺也龠也鬴也斛也筭數也
權衡也鐘也磬也是十物者必相合而不
相戾然後為得而馬遷律書率所不載蓋
器數之末非正樂之本聲氣之元不得則
黃鐘之律不定所謂十物者特虛器耳欲
求相合而不相戾也得乎故制律者必先
求聲氣之元以定黃鐘之管然後十二律
定而和氣可道此正樂之法不可易者舍
===
是言樂亦末矣雖然此法也非本也記曰
凡音者生人心者也治世之音安以樂其
政和聲音之道與政通矣是故政善則民
安民安則心和心和則氣和氣和則形和
形和則聲和聲和則天地之和應之卽愚
所謂百姓安樂天下大和如律書之旨是
也猶未也記又曰音者生於人心者也樂
者通倫理者也不知聲者不可與言音不
知音者不可與言樂知樂則幾於禮矣禮
punctuated:
然後無形之聲音得，而和氣可道。有形者，秬黍也，律也，尺也，龠也，鬴也，斛也，筭數也，權衡也，鐘也，磬也。是十物者，必相合而不相戾，然後為得。」而馬遷《律書》率所不載，蓋器數之末，非正樂之本。聲氣之元不得，則黃鐘之律不定，所謂十物者，特虛器耳。欲求相合而不相戾也，得乎？故制律者，必先求聲氣之元，以定黃鐘之管，然後十二律定，而和氣可道。此正樂之法不可易者，舍是言樂，亦末矣。
雖然，此法也，非本也。《記》曰：「凡音者，生人心者也。治世之音安以樂，其政和。」聲音之道，與政通矣。是故政善則民安，民安則心和，心和則氣和，氣和則形和，形和則聲和，聲和則天地之和應之。卽愚所謂百姓安樂，天下大和，如《律書》之旨是也。猶未也。《記》又曰：「音者，生於人心者也。樂者，通倫理者也。不知聲者，不可與言音；不知音者，不可與言樂。知樂則幾於禮矣。禮
translation_en:
…only then can formless sounds be properly attained and harmonious qi be conveyed. The tangible things are black millet, pitch standards, the foot measure, the yue measure, the fu measure, the hu measure, numerical calculations, weights and balances, bells, and chime stones. These ten things must agree with one another without conflict; only then is correctness attained.” Yet Sima Qian’s Treatise on the Pitch Standards generally does not record these things, for the particulars of instruments and numbers are peripheral, not the foundation of rectifying music. Unless the source of sound and qi is grasped, the pitch standard of Huangzhong cannot be established, and the so-called ten things are merely empty apparatus. Could one then hope to make them agree without conflict? Thus, anyone establishing pitch standards must first seek the source of sound and qi to determine the Huangzhong pitch pipe. Only then can the twelve pitch standards be established and harmonious qi be conveyed. This is the unalterable method for rectifying music. To discuss music while abandoning it is likewise to concern oneself with peripheral matters.
Nevertheless, this is a method, not the foundation. The Record of Rites says: “All musical tones arise from the human heart. The tones of an age of good order are peaceful and joyful, for its government is harmonious.” The way of sound and musical tones is interconnected with government. Thus, when government is good, the people are at peace; when the people are at peace, their hearts are harmonious; when their hearts are harmonious, their qi is harmonious; when their qi is harmonious, their bodily forms are harmonious; when their bodily forms are harmonious, their sounds are harmonious; and when their sounds are harmonious, the harmony of Heaven and Earth responds. This is precisely what I, in my humble view, mean by the common people being peaceful and joyful and all under Heaven enjoying great harmony, in accordance with the purport of the Treatise on the Pitch Standards. Yet this is still not all. The Record of Rites also says: “Musical tones arise from the human heart. Music brings understanding of ethical relationships and principles. With one who does not understand sounds, one cannot discuss musical tones; with one who does not understand musical tones, one cannot discuss music. To understand music is to approach an understanding of ritual. Ritual…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
蓋聞天下之道一也所以闡而明之者經
史而已矣夫經者非飾辭也體天人之撰
至精而不易者道之準也史者非備事也
持是非之衡至變而有則者道之紀也窮
經而不以道則無以極其精考史而不以
道則無以盡其變而其學也亦徒矣知此
則經史不同同歸於道固聖賢所以維世
教淑人心者也是可以泛求乎哉且鴻濛
既判書契已傳木繩棄而不行文籍於是
===
乎興矣而古今載籍之大孰有過於經史
者乎然經以載道聖賢傳心之要典史以
紀事史官一代之實錄若是乎其不侔也
及觀蘇洵謂經與史其義一其體二王通
謂聖人述史有三書詩春秋同出於史而
不可離則經與史豈各自為義者乎是故
經以道法勝矣若典謨訓誥諸篇詳于政
事即經中之史也史以事辭勝矣若朱熹
綱目謹于名分即史中之經也則經與史
punctuated: 蓋聞天下之道一也，所以闡而明之者，經史而已矣。夫經者，非飾辭也，體天人之撰，至精而不易者，道之準也。史者，非備事也，持是非之衡，至變而有則者，道之紀也。窮經而不以道，則無以極其精；考史而不以道，則無以盡其變，而其學也亦徒矣。知此，則經史不同，同歸於道，固聖賢所以維世教、淑人心者也。是可以泛求乎哉？且鴻濛既判，書契已傳，木繩棄而不行，文籍於是乎興矣。而古今載籍之大，孰有過於經史者乎？然經以載道，聖賢傳心之要典；史以紀事，史官一代之實錄。若是乎其不侔也。及觀蘇洵謂經與史其義一、其體二，王通謂聖人述史有三：《書》、《詩》、《春秋》，同出於史而不可離，則經與史豈各自為義者乎？是故經以道法勝矣，若典謨訓誥諸篇詳于政事，即經中之史也；史以事辭勝矣，若朱熹《綱目》謹于名分，即史中之經也。則經與史
translation_en:
Now, I have heard that the Way throughout the world is one, and that what expounds and illuminates it consists solely of the classics and histories. The classics are no mere embellishment of language: they embody the workings of Heaven and humankind; supremely refined and unchanging, they are the standard of the Way. The histories are no mere collection of events: they hold the balance of right and wrong; encompassing the utmost variation yet possessing governing principles, they are the ordering framework of the Way. If one investigates the classics without taking the Way as one's guide, one cannot fully fathom their subtlety; if one examines the histories without taking the Way as one's guide, one cannot fully comprehend their changes. Such study is futile. Understanding this, one sees that, though classics and histories differ, both converge upon the Way. They are indeed the means by which sages and worthies sustain moral teaching in the world and improve people's hearts. Can these be pursued superficially?

Moreover, once primordial chaos had divided and writing had been transmitted, wooden cords [?] were abandoned and ceased to be used; written records then arose. Among the great bodies of writings of antiquity and the present, what surpasses the classics and histories? Yet the classics convey the Way and are the essential texts through which sages and worthies transmit their understanding of the heart; histories record events and are the veritable records of a dynasty compiled by its historiographers. Thus they appear unequal in character. But Su Xun says that classics and histories are one in purport and two in form; Wang Tong says that the sages set forth history in three works—the Book of Documents, the Book of Odes, and the Spring and Autumn Annals—all originating in history and inseparable from it. How, then, could classics and histories each have a purport entirely their own?

Thus the classics excel in the principles of the Way. Yet such chapters as the Canons, Counsels, Instructions, and Announcements provide detailed accounts of governmental affairs: these are history within the classics. Histories excel in their accounts of events. Yet Zhu Xi's Outline and Details (Gangmu) is scrupulous about proper titles and hierarchical distinctions: this is a classic within history. Thus classics and histories…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
非互爲用者乎惟其義一是以用同用同
矣又何論其體之異哉且易書詩春秋禮
樂世所謂六經也後乃漸益其數至於十
三經者抑何經之多耶蓋伏羲堯舜文王
周公陳卦辭敘典謨采歌謠明節奏而羣
經始備至孔子則又賛易以黜誕定禮樂
以黜僭刪詩書以黜不雅脩春秋以黜不
王而六經始明自秦人焚棄而樂亡謂之
五經禮分爲三謂之七經加以孝經論語
===
謂之九經春秋分三傳合孝經論語爲一
則爲十經以六經加六緯則爲十二經而
十三經者又以三禮三傳加孝經論孟爾
雅言也然三禮備成周致治之迹三傳述
聖人筆削之情孝經陳先王至德之要論
孟記鄒魯授受之言皆足以維持世道羽
翼六經者也若六緯燬于煬帝書多不存
爾雅注于景純文皆無緒惡可與諸經並
列哉然則經之要者莫如五經而孝經論
punctuated: 非互爲用者乎？惟其義一，是以用同。用同矣，又何論其體之異哉？且《易》《書》《詩》《春秋》《禮》《樂》，世所謂六經也。後乃漸益其數，至於十三經者，抑何經之多耶？蓋伏羲、堯、舜、文王、周公陳卦辭，敘典謨，采歌謠，明節奏，而羣經始備。至孔子，則又賛《易》以黜誕，定禮樂以黜僭，刪《詩》《書》以黜不雅，脩《春秋》以黜不王，而六經始明。自秦人焚棄而《樂》亡，謂之五經；禮分爲三，謂之七經；加以《孝經》《論語》，謂之九經；《春秋》分三傳，合《孝經》《論語》爲一，則爲十經；以六經加六緯，則爲十二經。而十三經者，又以三禮、三傳加《孝經》《論》《孟》《爾雅》言也。然三禮備成周致治之迹，三傳述聖人筆削之情，《孝經》陳先王至德之要，《論》《孟》記鄒魯授受之言，皆足以維持世道、羽翼六經者也。若六緯燬于煬帝，書多不存；《爾雅》注于景純，文皆無緒，惡可與諸經並列哉？然則經之要者莫如五經，而《孝經》《論
translation_en:
…do they not serve one another? Precisely because their meaning is one, their function is the same. If their function is the same, why further discuss the difference in their forms? Moreover, the Changes, Documents, Odes, Spring and Autumn Annals, Rites, and Music are what the world calls the Six Classics. Later their number gradually increased, reaching the Thirteen Classics. Why were there so many classics? Fuxi, Yao, Shun, King Wen, and the Duke of Zhou set forth the hexagram statements, composed the canons and counsels, collected songs and ballads, and clarified musical rhythms; only then was the corpus of classics complete. When Confucius appeared, he further elucidated the Changes to reject the fabulous, settled rites and music to reject usurpation of rank, edited the Odes and Documents to reject what was improper, and revised the Spring and Autumn Annals to reject departures from the kingly way. Only then were the Six Classics made clear.

After the men of Qin burned and discarded them and the Music was lost, they were called the Five Classics. When the Rites was divided into three, they were called the Seven Classics. With the addition of the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects, they were called the Nine Classics. When the Spring and Autumn Annals was divided into its three commentaries, and the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects were counted together as one, they became the Ten Classics. Adding the six apocryphal texts to the Six Classics made the Twelve Classics. The designation Thirteen Classics, in turn, refers to the three ritual classics and the three commentaries together with the Classic of Filial Piety, the Analects, the Mencius, and the Erya.

Yet the three ritual classics fully preserve the traces of how the Zhou brought about good government; the three commentaries relate the sage’s intentions in making his inclusions and deletions. The Classic of Filial Piety sets forth the essentials of the former kings’ consummate virtue, while the Analects and the Mencius record the teachings transmitted and received in Zou and Lu. All are sufficient to sustain the moral order of the world and support the Six Classics. As for the six apocryphal texts, they were destroyed under Emperor Yang, and most no longer survive. The Erya was annotated by Jingchun, but its text is entirely without coherence. How could these be ranked alongside the classics? Thus, among the classics, none are more essential than the Five Classics, while the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
以折衷諸史而不離乎散殊之迹史不必
同于經也取其注言動公是非可以羽翼
羣經而不悖乎精微之奧則經史之體雖
殊而學之者可以異求乎哉故欲窮經者
不必索之高深也惟在崇五敎而辨三岐
焉何謂五敎經解曰溫柔敦厚詩敎也疏
通知遠書敎也潔淨精微易敎也恭儉莊
敬禮敎也屬詞比事春秋敎也於是崇之
則能達經之原矣何謂三岐朱子論蘇軾
===
陳少南因文說理爲文人之經張子韶輩
語涉空幻爲禪者之經濂洛諸子承傳有
自爲儒者之經是也於是辨之則不戾經
之旨矣若夫書敘六府曰水火金木土穀
是五行為府也皇極經世則以四時四經
分配言之曰昊天之四府者春夏秋冬之
謂也陰陽升降于其間矣聖人之四府者
易書詩春秋之謂也禮樂隆汙于其間矣
蓋天時聖經相因而成盡物盡民不出四
punctuated:
以折衷諸史，而不離乎散殊之迹。史不必同于經也，取其注言動、公是非，可以羽翼羣經，而不悖乎精微之奧，則經史之體雖殊，而學之者可以異求乎哉？故欲窮經者，不必索之高深也，惟在崇五敎而辨三岐焉。何謂五敎？《經解》曰：「溫柔敦厚，詩敎也；疏通知遠，書敎也；潔淨精微，易敎也；恭儉莊敬，禮敎也；屬詞比事，春秋敎也。」於是崇之，則能達經之原矣。何謂三岐？朱子論蘇軾、陳少南因文說理，爲文人之經；張子韶輩語涉空幻，爲禪者之經；濂洛諸子承傳有自，爲儒者之經，是也。於是辨之，則不戾經之旨矣。

若夫《書》敘六府，曰水、火、金、木、土、穀，是五行為府也。《皇極經世》則以四時、四經分配言之，曰：「昊天之四府者，春夏秋冬之謂也，陰陽升降于其間矣。聖人之四府者，易、書、詩、春秋之謂也，禮樂隆汙于其間矣。」蓋天時、聖經相因而成，盡物盡民，不出四
translation_en:
…to weigh and reconcile the various histories, while remaining within the traces of diverse particular events. Histories need not be identical to the classics. If we draw upon their recording of words and deeds and their impartial judgments of right and wrong, they can support the classics without contradicting their subtle, profound meaning. Thus, although classics and histories differ in form, can those who study them pursue different ends? Those who wish to fathom the classics need not seek in lofty profundities; they need only honor the five teachings and distinguish the three divergent paths. What are the five teachings? “Explanation of the Classics” states: “Gentleness, kindness, sincerity, and generosity are the teaching of the Odes; breadth of understanding and knowledge of the distant past are the teaching of the Documents; purity and subtle discernment are the teaching of the Changes; reverence, frugality, dignity, and respect are the teaching of the Rites; arranging words and juxtaposing events are the teaching of the Spring and Autumn Annals.” By honoring these, one can reach the source of the classics. What are the three divergent paths? Master Zhu distinguished the approach of Su Shi and Chen Shaonan, who explained principle through literary composition—the classics of literary men; that of Zhang Zishao and his fellows, whose language ventured into emptiness and illusion—the classics of Chan Buddhists; and that of the masters of Lian and Luo, whose received transmission had an authentic source—the classics of Confucian scholars. These are the three paths. By distinguishing them, one will not depart from the purport of the classics.

As for the Documents, it enumerates the six repositories as water, fire, metal, wood, earth, and grain: thus it treats the Five Phases as repositories. The Supreme Ultimate Governing the World (Huangji jingshi), however, assigns them respectively to the four seasons and the four classics, saying: “The four repositories of August Heaven mean spring, summer, autumn, and winter; yin and yang rise and descend within them. The four repositories of the sages mean the Changes, Documents, Odes, and Spring and Autumn Annals; ritual and music flourish and decline within them.” Thus Heaven’s seasons and the sages’ classics depend upon one another for their fulfillment; all things and all people fall within the four…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
府誠有如邵子之論也學者能究心於此
則經之體天德而前民用者不益會其精
耶欲考史者不必求之浩繁也惟在去五
難而執三長焉何爲五難袁崧曰煩而不
整一難也俗而不典二難也書不實錄三
難也賞罰不中四難也文不勝質五難也
於是去之則能正史之失矣何謂三長劉
知幾謂才以充之而使其不窮學以博之
而使其不偏識以辨之而使其不誣者是
===
也於是執之則能究史之全矣若夫荀悅
有五志之說蓋言達道義彰法戒通古今
著功勳表賢能也而干寶釋之以爲若體
國經野也用兵征伐忠孝貞烈也文告轉
對才力技藝也則從而書之劉知幾有三
科之說蓋言敘沿革明罪惡旌怪異也而
又自釋以爲若禮樂用舍也人物邪正古
今治忽也幽明感應禍福萌兆也則從而
書之蓋志事之書貴有體要信直之史宜
punctuated:
府，誠有如邵子之論也。學者能究心於此，則經之體天德而前民用者，不益會其精耶？

欲考史者，不必求之浩繁也，惟在去五難而執三長焉。何爲五難？袁崧曰：「煩而不整，一難也；俗而不典，二難也；書不實錄，三難也；賞罰不中，四難也；文不勝質，五難也。」於是去之，則能正史之失矣。何謂三長？劉知幾謂才以充之而使其不窮，學以博之而使其不偏，識以辨之而使其不誣者，是也。於是執之，則能究史之全矣。若夫荀悅有五志之說，蓋言達道義、彰法戒、通古今、著功勳、表賢能也。而干寶釋之，以爲若體國經野也，用兵征伐、忠孝貞烈也，文告轉對、才力技藝也，則從而書之。劉知幾有三科之說，蓋言敘沿革、明罪惡、旌怪異也。而又自釋，以爲若禮樂用舍也，人物邪正、古今治忽也，幽明感應、禍福萌兆也，則從而書之。蓋志事之書，貴有體要；信直之史，宜
translation_en:
…repositories: it is indeed as Master Shao argued. If scholars can devote their minds to this, will they not grasp still more deeply the essential meaning of how the Classics embody Heaven’s virtue and guide the people’s practical activities?

Those wishing to examine history need not seek it amid vast quantities of writings; what matters is eliminating the five difficulties and possessing the three strengths. What are the five difficulties? Yuan Song said: “Being prolix and disordered is the first difficulty; being vulgar rather than refined is the second; failing to record matters truthfully is the third; assigning rewards and punishments improperly is the fourth; and having literary expression unequal to the substance is the fifth.” By eliminating these, one can correct the failings of historical writing. What are the three strengths? They are what Liu Zhiji described as talent that supplies ample resources so that they never run out, learning that provides breadth so that the account is not one-sided, and discernment that makes distinctions so that it does not misrepresent. By possessing these, one can comprehend history in its entirety.

As for Xun Yue’s account of the five aims, these mean conveying the Way and righteousness, making models and warnings manifest, connecting past and present, recording meritorious achievements, and honoring the worthy and capable. Gan Bao explained these as matters such as organizing the capital and laying out the countryside; military operations and punitive expeditions, loyalty, filial piety, steadfastness, and heroic resolve; official proclamations and responses submitted in rotation, abilities, skills, and arts. These should accordingly be recorded. Liu Zhiji’s account of the three categories means narrating continuity and change, exposing wrongdoing, and drawing attention to strange occurrences. He himself further explained these as matters such as the adoption or abandonment of rites and music; the wickedness or uprightness of individuals and order or disorder in past and present; interactions between the unseen and visible worlds and the first portents of misfortune or good fortune. These should accordingly be recorded. For writings that record events, sound structure and attention to essentials are valued; truthful and candid histories ought to…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
別科條誠有如二家之言也學者能究心
于此則史之備監戒而昭勸懲者不益盡
其變耶雖然有本焉心者道之統會而文
之管攝也故易者言乎心之時也書者言
乎心之中也詩者言乎心之性情也禮樂
者言乎心之和敬也春秋者言乎心之好
惡也論孟者言乎心之道德也故以吾心
求六經論孟以六經論孟而觀經史則其
合此者謂之正離此者謂之叛法此而褒
===
貶者謂之公非此而褒貶者謂之私而經
史之得失瞭然無以遁其情矣此博物洽
聞者不免於玩物喪志之譏而據經以立
極觀聖以考言事變錯陳而中持衡焉夫
是以隨在皆實學也久之得意忘言得言
忘象而註脚六經筌蹄諸史亦可矣不然
斃其力於紙上之求而曰此十三經也此
二十一史也入乎耳出乎口楊雄氏所謂
說鈴也而奚益哉愚也非通經博史者也
punctuated: 別科條，誠有如二家之言也。學者能究心于此，則史之備監戒而昭勸懲者，不益盡其變耶？雖然，有本焉。心者，道之統會而文之管攝也。故《易》者，言乎心之時也；《書》者，言乎心之中也；《詩》者，言乎心之性情也；禮樂者，言乎心之和敬也；《春秋》者，言乎心之好惡也；《論》《孟》者，言乎心之道德也。故以吾心求六經、《論》《孟》，以六經、《論》《孟》而觀經史，則其合此者謂之正，離此者謂之叛，法此而褒貶者謂之公，非此而褒貶者謂之私，而經史之得失瞭然，無以遁其情矣。此博物洽聞者不免於玩物喪志之譏，而據經以立極，觀聖以考言，事變錯陳而中持衡焉。夫是以隨在皆實學也。久之，得意忘言，得言忘象，而註脚六經、筌蹄諸史亦可矣。不然，斃其力於紙上之求，而曰：「此十三經也，此二十一史也。」入乎耳，出乎口，楊雄氏所謂說鈴也，而奚益哉？愚也，非通經博史者也。
translation_en:
…distinguish categories and headings, just as those two writers have said. If scholars can devote their minds to this, will they not more fully comprehend the varied ways in which history provides warnings and makes encouragement and admonition clear? Yet there is a foundation to all this. The mind is where the Way is brought together and what governs literary expression. Thus the Changes speaks of the mind’s responsiveness to the times; the Documents, of the mind’s proper mean; the Odes, of the mind’s nature and feelings; ritual and music, of the mind’s harmony and reverence; the Spring and Autumn Annals, of the mind’s likes and dislikes; and the Analects and Mencius, of the mind’s Way and virtue. Therefore, we should use our own minds to seek understanding of the Six Classics, the Analects, and Mencius, and use these works to examine the classics and histories. What accords with this standard is called correct; what departs from it is called deviant. Praise and blame that follow this standard are called impartial; praise and blame that contravene it are called partial. The merits and faults of the classics and histories will then be plain, and their true character will have nowhere to hide.

Those of extensive learning and wide information cannot escape the reproach of losing their purpose through fascination with things. But by establishing the ultimate standard on the basis of the classics and looking to the sages to assess statements, one can hold the balance within even as events and changes present themselves in tangled profusion. Thus, wherever one turns, all becomes substantive learning. In time, one may grasp the meaning and forget the words, grasp the words and forget the images [?], and even treat the Six Classics as explanatory notes and the various histories as fish traps and rabbit snares—means that can be left behind once their purpose is achieved.
