Otherwise, one exhausts one’s strength in seeking on paper, saying, “These are the Thirteen Classics; these are the Twenty-One Histories.” What enters the ears comes straight out of the mouth: this is what Yang Xiong called “a jingle of talk.” What benefit can it bring? I, in my ignorance, am no one deeply versed in the classics or widely learned in history.

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
不忍爲悖經穢史之陋亦不敢蹈擬經譏
史之失惟執事指其迷而歸之道焉固所
願也
第四問
邵畯
同考試官教諭廖批民生休戚係守令之賢
否子於兩漢吏治知所决擇賢矣哉
同考試官教諭鄭批循吏之名盛實之衰也
此作能究王霸名實之辨可觀他日之循良矣
===
考試官學正馮批讀子之文是不以漢吏
自居志趣遠邁良可嘉尚
考試官學正劉批論治識體僅見此篇
知王霸之辨者可以達牧民之政矣知得
失之理者可以定考人之極矣夫民之仰
於治民者如子之仰於父母也父母之於
子所以使之飽煖安逸者不自以爲私而
子之飽煖安逸於父母也亦不以爲德何
者其情本相維也故治民者不以父母之
punctuated:
不忍爲悖經穢史之陋，亦不敢蹈擬經譏史之失。惟執事指其迷而歸之道焉，固所願也。

第四問
邵畯

同考試官教諭廖批：民生休戚，係守令之賢否。子於兩漢吏治知所决擇，賢矣哉！

同考試官教諭鄭批：循吏之名盛，實之衰也。此作能究王霸名實之辨，可觀他日之循良矣。

考試官學正馮批：讀子之文，是不以漢吏自居，志趣遠邁，良可嘉尚。

考試官學正劉批：論治識體，僅見此篇。

知王霸之辨者，可以達牧民之政矣；知得失之理者，可以定考人之極矣。夫民之仰於治民者，如子之仰於父母也。父母之於子，所以使之飽煖安逸者，不自以爲私；而子之飽煖安逸於父母也，亦不以爲德。何者？其情本相維也。故治民者不以父母之
translation_en:
…I cannot bear to commit the vulgar offense of violating the Classics and sullying the histories, nor dare I fall into the error of composing imitations of the Classics and disparaging the histories. That you, honored examiners, should point out my confusion and lead me back to the Way is precisely what I desire.

Fourth Policy Question
Shao Jun 邵畯

Comment by Associate Examiner Liao, Instructor: The well-being or distress of the people depends upon whether prefects and magistrates are worthy. You know how to distinguish and choose among the administrative practices of the two Han dynasties. How commendable!

Comment by Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor: When the reputation of “exemplary officials” flourishes, the substance is in decline. This composition thoroughly investigates the distinctions between true kingship and hegemony, and between reputation and substance. It gives a glimpse of the exemplary and benevolent official you may become.

Comment by Examiner Feng, Instructor: Reading your composition, I see that you do not content yourself with taking Han officials as your standard. Your aspirations reach far beyond them and are truly worthy of praise.

Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: Among these essays, this alone discusses government with an understanding of its essentials.

Those who understand the distinction between true kingship and hegemony can comprehend the governance of the people; those who understand the principles underlying success and failure can establish the ultimate standard for evaluating men. The people look up to those who govern them as children look up to their parents. When parents provide their children with adequate food, warmth, peace, and comfort, they do not consider themselves partial; when children receive these things from their parents, they likewise do not regard them as favors. Why is this? Their affections naturally bind them together. Thus those who govern the people do not regard the parents’ …

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
性而不知其爲天地之功也不知其功而
循吏之名孰爲其立之是可以觀王道矣
三代以降一變而爲春秋戰國再變而爲
秦漢於是法令刑名之說日熾言道德者
溺其職矣司馬遷以爲極之不可以不反
也故史記立例取周季王相之最賢者繫
之循吏傳以表之復取西漢守相之最酷
烈者繫之酷吏傳以別之其言曰法令者
治之具而非制治清濁之源也吁微矣班
===
固之續西漢書范曄之集東漢書蓋倣史
記凡例而爲之也今攷循吏之在西漢也
於傳僅得六人焉然文翁顯於孝景之世
王成黃霸龔遂朱邑召信臣迭盛於地節
神雀元始之間固不專在一帝也其取人
之嚴也如是豈有所遺歟不然吳公守河
南治平稱爲第一而傳不之採焉安知天
下無復有吳公者乎循吏之在東漢也於
傳僅得十二人焉然衞颯任延王渙許荆
punctuated:
性，而不知其爲天地之功也。不知其功，而循吏之名孰爲其立之？是可以觀王道矣。三代以降，一變而爲春秋戰國，再變而爲秦漢。於是法令刑名之說日熾，言道德者溺其職矣。司馬遷以爲極之不可以不反也，故《史記》立例，取周季王相之最賢者，繫之《循吏傳》以表之；復取西漢守相之最酷烈者，繫之《酷吏傳》以別之。其言曰：「法令者，治之具，而非制治清濁之源也。」吁，微矣！班固之續《西漢書》，范曄之集《東漢書》，蓋倣《史記》凡例而爲之也。
今攷循吏之在西漢也，於傳僅得六人焉。然文翁顯於孝景之世，王成、黃霸、龔遂、朱邑、召信臣迭盛於地節、神雀、元始之間，固不專在一帝也。其取人之嚴也如是，豈有所遺歟？不然，吳公守河南，治平稱爲第一，而傳不之採焉，安知天下無復有吳公者乎？循吏之在東漢也，於傳僅得十二人焉。然衞颯、任延、王渙、許荆
translation_en:
…the nature [of parents?], yet fail to recognize this as the work of Heaven and Earth. If their achievements are not recognized, who will establish their reputation as exemplary officials? Here one may discern the Way of the True King. After the Three Dynasties, one transformation brought the Spring and Autumn and Warring States periods; another brought the Qin and Han. Thereupon, doctrines of laws, ordinances, punishments, and administrative accountability grew ever more prevalent, while those who spoke of the Way and virtue were deemed remiss in their duties. Sima Qian held that, once this tendency reached its extreme, it could not but be reversed. Thus, in establishing the arrangement of the Records of the Grand Historian, he selected the worthiest ministers of kings in the late Zhou and included them in the “Biographies of Exemplary Officials” to honor them. He also selected the most cruel and ruthless governors and chancellors of the Western Han and included them in the “Biographies of Harsh Officials” to distinguish them. He said: “Laws and ordinances are instruments of government, not the source that determines whether government is pure or corrupt.” Ah, how subtle! Ban Gu, in continuing the historical record with the History of the Western Han, and Fan Ye, in compiling the History of the Eastern Han, presumably followed the organizational principles of the Records of the Grand Historian.
Now, examining the exemplary officials of the Western Han, we find only six men in their collective biography. Yet Wen Weng rose to prominence in the reign of Emperor Xiaojing, while Wang Cheng, Huang Ba, Gong Sui, Zhu Yi, and Shao Xinchen flourished in succession during the Dijie, Shenjue, and Yuanshi eras [?]. They certainly did not all belong to a single emperor’s reign. With selection so stringent, could anyone have been omitted? If not, Lord Wu, as governor of Henan, was ranked first for his peaceful and orderly administration, yet the biography does not include him. How can we know that there were no others like Lord Wu in the empire? As for exemplary officials of the Eastern Han, we find only twelve men in their collective biography. Yet Wei Sa, Ren Yan, Wang Huan, and Xu Jing…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
德政傳之循吏固矣若董宣之平生砥礪
名節蓋棺布被覆體當時畏威名者以臥
虎號之此其氣亦豪矣雖以廉能別傳可
也而曄亦列之酷吏然則黃昌殺登樓之
婦王吉繩夏月之屍其用情公私何如也
而乃與宣例論乎嗟夫史氏之意微矣何
者豈弟君子民之父母而鷹鸇之摶擊不
如烏鳥之慈兩漢吏弊方且以酷爲能其
糜爛不可勝紀彼其禁臨江王之刀筆而
===
致之死窮公孫丹之親黨而繫之獄則都
與宣之爲也而其事亦涉於酷史氏意謂
可使二子受不韙之名而不可使天下受
酷吏之禍故斷斷然列之傳首而不疑此
其立法雖嚴用意甚厚而於王霸之辨有
得其槩者亦挽回風俗之一大機也然就
其中而核之王成增戸口之政固爲僞飾
而黃霸遣吏廉事乃借烏攫之事以伺之
不涉於察乎童恢逢冤虎之訴似爲迂誕
punctuated:
德政，傳之循吏固矣。若董宣之平生砥礪名節，蓋棺布被覆體，當時畏威名者以臥虎號之，此其氣亦豪矣。雖以廉能別傳可也，而曄亦列之酷吏。然則黃昌殺登樓之婦，王吉繩夏月之屍，其用情公私何如也，而乃與宣例論乎？嗟夫！史氏之意微矣。何者？豈弟君子，民之父母，而鷹鸇之摶擊不如烏鳥之慈。兩漢吏弊，方且以酷爲能，其糜爛不可勝紀。彼其禁臨江王之刀筆而致之死，窮公孫丹之親黨而繫之獄，則都與宣之爲也，而其事亦涉於酷。史氏意謂，可使二子受不韙之名，而不可使天下受酷吏之禍，故斷斷然列之傳首而不疑。此其立法雖嚴，用意甚厚，而於王霸之辨有得其槩者，亦挽回風俗之一大機也。
然就其中而核之，王成增戸口之政固爲僞飾，而黃霸遣吏廉事，乃借烏攫之事以伺之，不涉於察乎？童恢逢冤虎之訴，似爲迂誕。
translation_en:
…their benevolent administration certainly warranted recording them among the exemplary officials. As for Dong Xuan, throughout his life he cultivated his reputation and integrity; when his coffin was closed, his body was covered with a plain cloth quilt. Those of his time who feared his formidable reputation called him the “Crouching Tiger.” His spirit, too, was heroic. He might well have received a separate biography for his integrity and ability, yet Ye also placed him among the harsh officials. Huang Chang killed a woman who climbed a tower, and Wang Ji subjected a corpse to punishment in the summer months [?]. Were their motives public-spirited or self-serving? How could they be discussed in the same category as Xuan?
Alas! The historian’s intention was subtle. Why? “The gracious gentleman is the father and mother of the people”: the striking of hawks and falcons cannot compare with the tender care of crows. Among the abuses of officialdom under the two Han dynasties, cruelty was actually regarded as competence, and the devastation it wrought was beyond recording. Denying the Prince of Linjiang writing implements and thereby bringing about his death, and pursuing Gongsun Dan’s relatives and associates to the last and imprisoning them—these were the deeds of Du and Xuan, and they too involved cruelty. The historian’s intention was that these two men might bear a discreditable name, but All-under-Heaven must not suffer the calamities inflicted by harsh officials. Thus he resolutely placed them at the head of that biographical section without hesitation. Although the standard he established was strict, his purpose was profoundly benevolent. He grasped something of the essential distinction between true kingship and hegemony; this, too, was a major means of restoring social customs.
Yet, upon scrutinizing the men included in these accounts, Wang Cheng’s achievement in increasing registered households and population was certainly a fabrication. And when Huang Ba sent an official to investigate matters discreetly, he used an incident in which a crow snatched something to keep watch on him: did this not verge on intrusive scrutiny? Tong Hui’s encounter with a tiger’s plea that it had been wrongfully accused seems fanciful and absurd…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
而孟嘗反政合浦必舉還珠之事以實之
不幾於怪乎其他形於甘棠之留固出於
兒童里社之所俎豆而希心者也然竊仁
義之似雖足以宜民於一時使以仁義之
實施之則爝火之光自息矣此漢治不免
於雜霸視古之父母斯民者可同日語哉
故牧民者以父母之心行之則渾渾悶悶
之政於是乎在矣彼風行霜烈不足以洽
化懲違視循吏何啻徑庭也方今
===
聖天子勵精圖治禮樂化洽而雍熙大和之治
遠邁兩漢又况考課之法
祖宗成憲俱在監司以時而公其激揚銓部以
時而明其黜陟固宜循吏之風遠追唐虞
之隆矣而博觀郡縣求以當
上意者蓋僅僅見豈司考課者未定取舍之極
使人不知所適從歟愚以為循之為義上
順天理下順人情之謂也類非浮薄苛刻
者之所能以今日觀之循良者難求而深
punctuated:
而孟嘗反政合浦，必舉還珠之事以實之，不幾於怪乎？其他形於甘棠之留，固出於兒童里社之所俎豆而希心者也。然竊仁義之似，雖足以宜民於一時，使以仁義之實施之，則爝火之光自息矣。此漢治不免於雜霸，視古之父母斯民者，可同日語哉？故牧民者以父母之心行之，則渾渾悶悶之政於是乎在矣。彼風行霜烈，不足以洽化懲違，視循吏何啻徑庭也！
方今聖天子勵精圖治，禮樂化洽，而雍熙大和之治遠邁兩漢。又况考課之法，祖宗成憲俱在，監司以時而公其激揚，銓部以時而明其黜陟，固宜循吏之風遠追唐虞之隆矣。而博觀郡縣，求以當上意者，蓋僅僅見。豈司考課者未定取舍之極，使人不知所適從歟？愚以為循之為義，上順天理，下順人情之謂也，類非浮薄苛刻者之所能。以今日觀之，循良者難求，而深
translation_en:
…Yet when describing Meng Chang’s reform of government in Hepu [?], they invariably cite the return of the pearls to substantiate it. Does this not verge on the fantastic? Other manifestations of affection, like the preservation of the sweet pear tree, certainly arose from the devotion of children and village communities, who offered sacrifices to these officials and aspired to emulate them. Yet appropriating the semblance of benevolence and righteousness, though sufficient to benefit the people for a time, would lose its feeble torchlight if genuine benevolence and righteousness were put into practice. Thus Han government remained mixed with the methods of hegemonic rule. Can it be spoken of in the same breath as the government of those in antiquity who acted as parents to the people? If those who shepherd the people act with a parent’s heart, government of an unassuming and unobtrusive kind will follow. Those who act like sweeping winds and biting frost cannot make moral transformation pervasive or restrain wrongdoing. How vastly they differ from exemplary officials!
Today our sagely Son of Heaven devotes his energies to good government. The transforming influence of rites and music extends everywhere, and his harmonious, peaceful rule far surpasses that of the two Han dynasties. Moreover, the established statutes of our imperial ancestors governing evaluations of officials remain intact. If the surveillance officials impartially censure and commend at the prescribed times, and the Ministry of Personnel clearly determines demotions and promotions at the prescribed times, the conduct of exemplary officials should surely approach the ancient flourishing of the ages of Yao and Shun. Yet, surveying the prefectures and counties broadly, one finds scarcely any who meet His Majesty’s intentions. Could it be that those responsible for evaluations have not established an ultimate standard for acceptance and rejection, leaving people uncertain what to follow? In my humble view, the meaning of “exemplary” is to accord above with Heaven’s principles and below with human feelings. This is generally beyond the capacity of the frivolous and harsh. Judging by present conditions, exemplary and good officials are hard to find, while those who are severe…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
文者難辨也今夫廉幹華藻之吏人人而
知之矣反是而簡靜而悃愊日計不足月
計有餘固勤於民事者也苟非詳察而優
養之其不以不職考者鮮矣當是時縱有
陽城之心勞兒寬之課殿夫安得而用之
今夫貪墨酷暴之吏人人而知之矣外是
而飾行而文姦迎合鍛鍊巧詆誣服固厚
於虐民者也苟非徐觀而救正之其不以
稱職考者鮮矣當是時卽有訊鼠之張湯
===
蝮鷙之殷周又安得而黜之然則明好惡
之分示趨向之的容外求乎孔子曰君子
之德風也小人之德草也何者感應之機
在我也是苟考人者以深文爲忌以循良爲
尚而有聲於郡縣者請
璽書褒美增秩加官不少靳焉使天下之爲守
令者曉然知
上所以惇元元之意而以過刻爲戒是使人之
循於我也而天下之人亦以父母斯民爲
punctuated: 文者難辨也。今夫廉幹華藻之吏，人人而知之矣。反是而簡靜而悃愊，日計不足，月計有餘，固勤於民事者也。苟非詳察而優養之，其不以不職考者鮮矣。當是時，縱有陽城之心勞、兒寬之課殿，夫安得而用之？今夫貪墨酷暴之吏，人人而知之矣。外是而飾行而文姦，迎合鍛鍊，巧詆誣服，固厚於虐民者也。苟非徐觀而救正之，其不以稱職考者鮮矣。當是時，卽有訊鼠之張湯、蝮鷙之殷周，又安得而黜之？然則明好惡之分，示趨向之的，容外求乎？孔子曰：「君子之德風也，小人之德草也。」何者？感應之機在我也。是苟考人者以深文爲忌，以循良爲尚，而有聲於郡縣者，請璽書褒美，增秩加官，不少靳焉，使天下之爲守令者曉然知上所以惇元元之意，而以過刻爲戒，是使人之循於我也。而天下之人亦以父母斯民爲
translation_en:
…those who apply the law with excessive severity are difficult to distinguish. Now, officials known for integrity, competence, and literary brilliance are recognizable to everyone. By contrast, those who are unassuming, quiet, and utterly sincere, whose achievements seem insufficient when reckoned by the day but more than sufficient when reckoned by the month, are indeed diligent in the people's affairs. Unless they are carefully examined and generously nurtured, few will escape being rated unfit for office. Under such circumstances, even someone with Yang Cheng's devoted exertions, or Ni Kuan's bottom-ranking performance assessment, could hardly be employed.

Now, corrupt, rapacious, cruel, and violent officials are recognizable to everyone. Beyond these, however, are those who embellish their conduct and disguise their wickedness, curry favor and fabricate cases, ingeniously frame accusations and force false confessions. These are indeed deeply engaged in oppressing the people. Unless they are observed patiently and their conduct corrected, few will fail to be rated fit for office. Under such circumstances, even a Zhang Tang who interrogated a rat, or a viper-like and predatory Yin Zhou [?], could hardly be dismissed.

Then, to make clear the distinction between what is approved and disapproved, and to show the goal toward which officials should strive, can one seek the answer elsewhere? Confucius said: “The virtue of the gentleman is wind; the virtue of the petty man is grass.” Why is this? Because the impulse that elicits a response lies with us. Thus, if those who assess others shun excessive legal severity and esteem conscientious, benevolent administration, then, for officials who have earned a good reputation in the prefectures and counties, they should request sealed imperial letters of commendation and unstintingly grant increases in rank and advancement in office. This will enable prefects and county magistrates throughout the realm to understand clearly the sovereign's intention to care generously for the common people, and to guard against excessive harshness. In this way, we cause others to follow our example. And people throughout the realm will likewise take acting as father and mother to these people as their…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
心惟知養和氣以待造化之自定則化續
羔羊而陋兩漢於不足者非所以風之哉
然此
國家已試之效也顧操柄者力行何如耳執
事以爲何如
第五問
陳錫
同考試官教諭吳批觀拯荒一策切中機宜
經國遠猷端有望于子矣
===
考試官學正馮批此策裕國計濟時艱籌
畫俱善是有志于用世者
考試官學正劉批湖以西水災爲劇子以
蠲租恤民爲對剴切著明經濟之學於此試之
通天下之變者達其權而已矣識天下之
幾者定其經而已矣夫事幾之乘也其變
每生於無常而圖理之道其法必期於可
久故相時以計其變則權宜審而無妄動
之弊先時以察其幾則經畫周而無臨事
punctuated:
心，惟知養和氣，以待造化之自定，則化續《羔羊》，而陋兩漢於不足者，非所以風之哉？然此國家已試之效也，顧操柄者力行何如耳。執事以爲何如？

第五問
陳錫

同考試官教諭吳批：觀拯荒一策，切中機宜，經國遠猷，端有望于子矣。

考試官學正馮批：此策裕國計、濟時艱，籌畫俱善，是有志于用世者。

考試官學正劉批：湖以西水災爲劇，子以蠲租恤民爲對，剴切著明，經濟之學於此試之。

通天下之變者，達其權而已矣；識天下之幾者，定其經而已矣。夫事幾之乘也，其變每生於無常，而圖理之道，其法必期於可久。故相時以計其變，則權宜審而無妄動之弊；先時以察其幾，則經畫周而無臨事
translation_en:
…their guiding concern, knowing only to nurture harmonious influences and await the natural settling of the processes of creation. Then their transforming influence would carry forward that celebrated in “The Lamb” and make the achievements of the two Han dynasties seem paltry and inadequate. Would this not be a means of influencing them by example? Yet these are results already demonstrated by our state; it remains only to see how vigorously those who wield authority put these measures into practice. What is your judgment, honored examiner?

Fifth Question
Chen Xi

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: On reading this policy essay on relief from famine, I find that it precisely addresses the circumstances and the measures they require. We may indeed look to you for far-reaching plans for governing the state.

Comment by Examiner Feng, School Instructor: This policy essay offers sound planning both for enriching the state's finances and for relieving the difficulties of the times. Its author has the ambition to serve the world.

Comment by Examiner Liu, School Instructor: Flooding has been especially severe west of the lake. Your answer proposes remitting land taxes and relieving the people; it is pertinent, incisive, and clear. Here your learning in statecraft is put to the test.

To comprehend the changes of the world is simply to understand appropriate expedients; to discern the first stirrings of events in the world is simply to establish enduring principles. When incipient circumstances present themselves [?], the changes they bring often arise unpredictably; yet the methods by which one seeks orderly government must be designed to endure. Thus, if one assesses the times and plans for their changes, expedient measures will be carefully considered, without the harm of rash action; if one anticipates events and examines their first stirrings, planning will be comprehensive, without, when affairs arise, …

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之失此善於裕民者必窮源探本而不爲
一朝一夕之計者其所慮者遠也不然患
生而爲之謀事至而爲之備吁亦晩矣執
事念兩浙之水災而追論乎往事誠有見
於古今之效而欲以捄之者也爲下爲民
之心切矣承學不敏敢不悉心以對夫兩
浙古揚州之地厥田下下厥賦下上上錯
自錢鏐捍海以來富庶甲於天下我
太祖奄有一統邃土宇而版圖之屹然爲東南
===
一財府也
京師軍國百萬之需多倚辦焉然天下形勢
東南爲最下兩浙跨有吳越襟海帶江地
故多水迺者淫雨浹旬江湖竝溢歲登不
給民食滋艱司牧者可晏然已哉崇寛恤
之議者必曰請蠲征矣然
國家經費不容輕損況恃此以捄嗷嗷待哺
之民其可及乎廣賑貸之策者必曰散儲
積矣而郡縣儲蓄未之前聞欲賴升合之
punctuated: 之失。此善於裕民者，必窮源探本，而不爲一朝一夕之計者，其所慮者遠也。不然，患生而爲之謀，事至而爲之備，吁，亦晩矣！執事念兩浙之水災，而追論乎往事，誠有見於古今之效，而欲以捄之者也。爲下爲民之心切矣！承學不敏，敢不悉心以對？夫兩浙，古揚州之地，厥田下下，厥賦下上上錯。自錢鏐捍海以來，富庶甲於天下。我太祖奄有一統，邃土宇而版圖之，屹然爲東南一財府也。京師軍國百萬之需，多倚辦焉。然天下形勢，東南爲最下。兩浙跨有吳越，襟海帶江，地故多水。迺者淫雨浹旬，江湖竝溢，歲登不給，民食滋艱，司牧者可晏然已哉？崇寛恤之議者，必曰請蠲征矣。然國家經費，不容輕損，況恃此以捄嗷嗷待哺之民，其可及乎？廣賑貸之策者，必曰散儲積矣。而郡縣儲蓄，未之前聞，欲賴升合之
translation_en:
…errors when affairs arise. Thus, those skilled at enriching the people must trace matters to their source and investigate their foundations, rather than devise plans merely for a day or an evening: their concerns extend far into the future. Otherwise, to devise plans only after trouble has arisen and make preparations only when events are upon us—alas, that is already too late! You, honored sir, are concerned about flooding in Liangzhe and therefore examine past events. You have indeed discerned the results of measures ancient and modern and wish thereby to bring relief. Your concern for those below and for the people is profound! Though I am an unworthy student, how could I dare not devote my whole mind to answering?

Liangzhe occupies the territory of ancient Yangzhou, whose fields were ranked “lower-lower” and whose tax assessment was “lower-upper, with higher assessments intermixed.” Since Qian Liu built defenses against the sea, its wealth and population have ranked foremost in the realm. Our Taizu brought all under unified rule, extended his territory [?], and incorporated this region into the imperial registers and maps; it stood firmly as a treasury of the southeast. The capital’s military and state requirements, amounting to millions, depend largely upon its provision. Yet, in the configuration of the realm’s terrain, the southeast lies lowest. Liangzhe spans Wu and Yue, with the sea at its breast and the river as its girdle; its land is therefore abundantly watered. Recently, incessant rain continued for ten days, and rivers and lakes overflowed together. The year’s harvest was insufficient, and the people’s difficulty in obtaining food grew more severe. Can those charged with shepherding them remain complacent?

Those who advocate leniency and relief will certainly say that exemption from taxation should be requested. Yet the state’s regular revenues cannot lightly be reduced. Moreover, if we rely upon this to save the people crying out for food, can relief reach them in time? Those who promote policies of relief grants and loans will certainly say that accumulated stores should be distributed. Yet we have heard of no reserves in the prefectures and counties. To hope to rely upon a few sheng and ge of…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
入以濟其衆其可得乎夫旱乾水溢天之
數也所以弭其災而救其患者人之責也
在昔聖人於水旱之來不委之適然之數
而圖惟救濟者恒兢兢焉故雖歷九年之
水七年之旱而國無捐瘠者蓄積多而預
備具法制立而機宜審也詎恃蠲貸之令
以苟幸於一時已哉嘗考漢武帝有逋貸
之蠲矣吳嘉禾有逋賦之寬矣晋惠帝有
戶調絹綿之除矣唐宣宗有免度支鹽鐵
===
之議矣宋高宗有免官司債負和買役錢
之令矣然皆名而已耳是數君者豈誠不
知民生之當念哉備之不豫處之不審則
其勢不得不然而其間又有不欲盡免
而權宜於其中者如宋哲宗時令諸路屢
年負欠以十分爲率每年帶納一分似便
民矣及蘇軾訪問濠壽父老又有豐年不
如凶年之說蓋以天災流行苟非太甚民
雖乏食猶可節縮以聊生若豐年舉催積
punctuated: 入以濟其衆，其可得乎？夫旱乾水溢，天之數也；所以弭其災而救其患者，人之責也。在昔聖人於水旱之來，不委之適然之數，而圖惟救濟者恒兢兢焉。故雖歷九年之水、七年之旱，而國無捐瘠者，蓄積多而預備具，法制立而機宜審也。詎恃蠲貸之令，以苟幸於一時已哉？嘗考漢武帝有逋貸之蠲矣，吳嘉禾有逋賦之寬矣，晋惠帝有戶調絹綿之除矣，唐宣宗有免度支鹽鐵之議矣，宋高宗有免官司債負、和買、役錢之令矣。然皆名而已耳。是數君者，豈誠不知民生之當念哉？備之不豫，處之不審，則其勢不得不然。而其間又有不欲盡免而權宜於其中者，如宋哲宗時，令諸路屢年負欠，以十分爲率，每年帶納一分，似便民矣。及蘇軾訪問濠壽父老，又有豐年不如凶年之說。蓋以天災流行，苟非太甚，民雖乏食，猶可節縮以聊生；若豐年舉催積
translation_en:
…could such meager receipts suffice to relieve the multitude? Drought and overflowing waters belong to the allotted course of Heaven; mitigating their disasters and rescuing those who suffer is a human responsibility. When floods and droughts came, the sages of old did not leave matters to the workings of chance, but constantly applied themselves with anxious diligence to devising relief. Thus, even after nine years of flooding or seven years of drought, none within the realm were abandoned to starvation: reserves were abundant, preparations complete, institutions established, and measures carefully suited to circumstances. How could they merely have relied on orders for remissions and relief loans, hoping to scrape through the moment?

I have examined the precedents: Emperor Wu of Han remitted overdue loans; during the Jiahe reign period of Wu, tax arrears were reduced; Emperor Hui of Jin abolished household levies of silk fabric and silk floss; under Emperor Xuanzong of Tang, remissions involving the Revenue Section and the Salt and Iron Monopoly administration were proposed; and Emperor Gaozong of Song issued orders remitting debts owed to government offices, compulsory purchases, and service-exemption payments. Yet these were all benefits in name alone. Could these rulers truly have failed to understand that the people's livelihood deserved their concern? Their preparations were not made in advance, and their handling of affairs was insufficiently considered, so circumstances inevitably brought them to this pass.

Among them were also those unwilling to remit everything, who instead adopted expedients. Under Emperor Zhezong of Song, for example, it was ordered that accumulated arrears throughout the circuits be divided into ten portions, with one portion paid each year alongside current dues. This seemed advantageous to the people. Yet when Su Shi questioned the elders of Hao and Shou, he heard the saying that a good harvest year was worse than a bad one. For when natural disasters spread, provided they were not too severe, people could economize and eke out a living even if food was scarce; but in a good harvest year, when collection was pressed for all accumulated…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
負奉宣匪人則閭閻反以多事而所收不
償所出又不若凶歲之可支也民何由被
實惠哉宋自紹興以後役煩賦重極力寬
之民病猶未甦也而朱熹上封事有遷延
一分以待蠲放之議者蓋宋初舊法凡催
理官物數及九分諸司卽行停止版曹亦
置不問州縣得其贏餘以相補助貧民亦
得遷延以待蠲除較之虛文無實所謂黃
紙放白紙取者不亦相去遠哉由是觀之
===
人君之治國也猶醫之治病也緩則治其
本亟則治其標今兩浙之民病亦亟矣誠
司牧者所當軫念也顧
國賦旣不可缺則蠲負其可恃乎嘗稽之宋
紹興間因湖秀水災欲除下戶積欠慮恐
侵損歲支輒於內庫撥補似恤民者然湖
秀一隅侵損未多補給尚易若舉天下而
出內帑給之不知當時又將何以處之耶
又嘗稽之唐矣玄宗蠲免七年以前逋負
punctuated: 負，奉宣匪人，則閭閻反以多事，而所收不償所出，又不若凶歲之可支也。民何由被實惠哉？宋自紹興以後，役煩賦重，極力寬之，民病猶未甦也。而朱熹上封事，有遷延一分以待蠲放之議者，蓋宋初舊法，凡催理官物，數及九分，諸司卽行停止，版曹亦置不問。州縣得其贏餘以相補助，貧民亦得遷延以待蠲除。較之虛文無實，所謂黃紙放、白紙取者，不亦相去遠哉？由是觀之，人君之治國也，猶醫之治病也：緩則治其本，亟則治其標。今兩浙之民病亦亟矣，誠司牧者所當軫念也。顧國賦旣不可缺，則蠲負其可恃乎？嘗稽之宋紹興間，因湖秀水災，欲除下戶積欠，慮恐侵損歲支，輒於內庫撥補，似恤民者。然湖秀一隅，侵損未多，補給尚易；若舉天下而出內帑給之，不知當時又將何以處之耶？又嘗稽之唐矣，玄宗蠲免七年以前逋負。
translation_en:
…arrears, if those entrusted with carrying out the proclamation are unsuitable, households instead face increased trouble, and what they receive does not make up for what they expend. They are then less able to get by than in a year of poor harvests. How can the people obtain any real benefit?

From the Shaoxing reign onward, labor obligations under the Song were onerous and taxation heavy. Even strenuous efforts to ease them had not yet relieved the people's distress. In a sealed memorial, Zhu Xi proposed allowing payment of one tenth to be deferred pending remission. Under an old rule dating from the early Song, once collection of payments due to the government reached nine tenths, the various offices immediately ceased collection, and the Ministry of Revenue likewise left the matter alone. Prefectures and counties could use their surpluses to make up one another's shortfalls, while poor households could defer payment pending remission. Was this not far removed from empty paperwork without substance—the practice described as “remitting on yellow paper, collecting on white paper”?

Seen in this light, a ruler's governance of his state resembles a physician's treatment of illness: when the condition is mild, treat its root; when urgent, treat its symptoms. The distress of the people of Liangzhe is now urgent indeed, and those charged with governing them must surely take it to heart. Yet since the state's tax revenues cannot fall short, can remission of arrears be relied upon?

I have examined an instance from the Shaoxing reign of the Song. Because of flooding in Huzhou and Xiuzhou, the authorities wished to cancel the accumulated arrears of lower-category households. Fearing that this would diminish the funds available for annual expenditure, they transferred funds from the Inner Treasury to make up the shortfall. This seems to have shown solicitude for the people. Yet Huzhou and Xiuzhou formed only one small area: the revenue loss was not great, and replenishing it was still easy. Had the entire realm been involved, with funds drawn from the Inner Treasury to cover it, I do not know how they would then have dealt with the situation.

I have also examined the Tang precedent: Xuanzong remitted arrears dating from before the seventh year…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
當時稱爲異數然寬貸之舉止爲貧民若
果貧民欠負盡數免之以蘇疲困亦何不
可但膏脂已竭於無告而惠澤翻及於姦
豪中間雖究已收未收之等亦誰肯自陳
其弊哉善乎宋臣趙善防有云貧民下戶
每歲二稅但有重納未甞拖欠朝廷蠲放
利歸攬戶鄉胥而小民未甞霑恩乞明詔
自今郊霈惟減次年賦稅其目前殘零務
依數納足則貧民實被寬恩官賦亦易催
===
理此治標之策與朱熹遷延一分之說皆
足以甦民困而善於通變者矣然亦豈可
以常恃也哉王制曰三年耕必有一年之
食九年耕必有三年之食以三十年之通
制國用雖有凶旱水溢民無菜色今不豫
之於粟米狼戾之時而顧行之於十室九
空之日亦無及矣毋亦於所以固邦本者
加之意焉可乎吾浙本水鄉十日之霖大
浸也一月之旱赤土也是故按圖籍以尋
punctuated:
當時稱爲異數，然寬貸之舉止爲貧民。若果貧民欠負，盡數免之，以蘇疲困，亦何不可？但膏脂已竭於無告，而惠澤翻及於姦豪。中間雖究已收未收之等，亦誰肯自陳其弊哉？善乎宋臣趙善防有云：「貧民下戶，每歲二稅，但有重納，未甞拖欠。朝廷蠲放，利歸攬戶鄉胥，而小民未甞霑恩。乞明詔，自今郊霈，惟減次年賦稅，其目前殘零，務依數納足，則貧民實被寬恩，官賦亦易催理。」此治標之策，與朱熹遷延一分之說，皆足以甦民困，而善於通變者矣。然亦豈可以常恃也哉？
王制曰：「三年耕，必有一年之食；九年耕，必有三年之食。以三十年之通，制國用，雖有凶旱水溢，民無菜色。」今不豫之於粟米狼戾之時，而顧行之於十室九空之日，亦無及矣。毋亦於所以固邦本者加之意焉，可乎？吾浙本水鄉，十日之霖，大浸也；一月之旱，赤土也。是故按圖籍以尋
translation_en:
…At the time, this was acclaimed as an exceptional favor. Yet such relief was intended solely for the poor. If the arrears were truly owed by poor people, what objection could there be to remitting them entirely to relieve their exhaustion and distress? But the helpless have already been drained of their last resources, while the benefits instead reach unscrupulous local magnates. Even if an inquiry distinguishes between sums already collected and those not yet collected, who would willingly disclose his own abuses? Well did the Song official Zhao Shanfang 趙善防 [?] say: “Poor people and households in the lowest assessment categories suffer duplicate exactions of the two annual taxes, but have never been in arrears. When the court remits taxes, the benefit goes to tax-collection contractors and township clerks, while the common people receive none of its bounty. I request an explicit edict that, henceforth, acts of grace accompanying the suburban sacrifices should reduce only the following year’s taxes. All outstanding balances currently due should be paid in full according to the assessed amounts. Then the poor will actually receive generous relief, and official taxes will also be easier to collect.” This remedy for the symptoms, together with Zhu Xi’s proposal to defer a portion of the payment [?], can relieve the people’s distress; both are skillful adaptations to circumstances. Yet how could they be relied upon indefinitely?
The “Royal Regulations” chapter says: “Three years of cultivation must provide food reserves for one year; nine years of cultivation must provide food reserves for three years. State expenditure is regulated by reckoning across thirty years, so that even when severe drought or flooding occurs, the people show no signs of hunger.” If preparations are not made when grain lies in abundance, but measures are attempted only when nine households out of ten stand empty, it is already too late. Might we not devote greater attention to what secures the foundation of the state? Our Zhejiang is inherently a region of waterways: ten days of continuous rain bring extensive flooding; a month of drought leaves the earth bare. Therefore, by consulting maps and registers to seek out…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
詔令則中和致而位育之功成矣又何民瘼之
弗蘇哉此固書生之談而非俊傑之識時
也幸與進之
punctuated: 詔令，則中和致，而位育之功成矣，又何民瘼之弗蘇哉？此固書生之談，而非俊傑之識時也。幸與進之。
translation_en: …the imperial edicts, then equilibrium and harmony will be attained, and the work of setting Heaven and Earth in their proper places and nurturing all things will be accomplished. What suffering among the people would then remain unrelieved? These are admittedly the words of a mere scholar, rather than the insight of an outstanding man who understands the times. I hope you will favor me by allowing me to advance.

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
浙江鄉試錄後序
凡三年類士而鄉試之事竣
而錄其文與名氏以
獻遵
制也人臣以人事君之義也錄成
前後有序主司者旣選士而
序其事以寓規也士之得與
===
玆選蓋古司徒之所論而升
之者歌鹿鳴而燕之則旣待
以古之嘉賓矣而曷以規之
恒情時異則志易以渝勢遷
則塞易以變而况於入官之
始也可不愼歟嘉靖己酉秋
八月浙江鄉試錄成學正劉
punctuated:
浙江鄉試錄後序

凡三年類士而鄉試之，事竣而錄其文與名氏以獻，遵制也，人臣以人事君之義也。錄成，前後有序，主司者旣選士而序其事以寓規也。士之得與玆選，蓋古司徒之所論而升之者。歌《鹿鳴》而燕之，則旣待以古之嘉賓矣，而曷以規之？恒情，時異則志易以渝，勢遷則塞易以變，而况於入官之始也，可不愼歟？嘉靖己酉秋八月，浙江鄉試錄成，學正劉
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Zhejiang Provincial Examination

Every three years, scholars are assembled and examined in the Provincial Examination. When the proceedings are concluded, their compositions and names are recorded for presentation to the throne. This follows imperial regulations and fulfills the duty of a subject to serve his sovereign by providing worthy men. Once the record is completed, it has a preface and a postface: having selected the scholars, those presiding over the examination recount the proceedings to convey admonition. The scholars admitted to this selection are like those whom the Minister of Education in antiquity assessed and advanced. By singing “The Deer Call” and feasting them, we have already treated them as the honored guests of antiquity. But how should we admonish them?

It is ordinary human nature that, as times change, aspirations readily waver, and as circumstances shift, dispositions [?] readily change. How much more so at the outset of entering official service! Can one fail to be cautious? In autumn, in the eighth month of the jiyou year of Jiajing [1549], the Record of the Zhejiang Provincial Examination was completed. Instructor Liu …

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
皇上御極敦正文體崇雅黜浮
明詔之頒有曰士大夫學術不正
以致文章政事日趨詭異而聖
賢大學之道不明關係治理要
非細故夫
聖聖相承用人圖治而惟君子是
求惟聖賢大學之道是講謂
===
徒取其文已乎自鄉舉里選
之法廢雖豪傑之士崇德而
勵行不以文進則不能大行
於天下故文也者士君子所
以行道之階耳雖然文外無
道道外無文古三物之敎曰
六德六行六藝莫非道也根
punctuated:
皇上御極，敦正文體，崇雅黜浮。明詔之頒有曰：「士大夫學術不正，以致文章政事日趨詭異，而聖賢大學之道不明，關係治理，要非細故。」

夫聖聖相承，用人圖治，而惟君子是求，惟聖賢大學之道是講，謂徒取其文已乎？自鄉舉里選之法廢，雖豪傑之士，崇德而勵行，不以文進，則不能大行於天下。故文也者，士君子所以行道之階耳。雖然，文外無道，道外無文。古三物之敎，曰六德、六行、六藝，莫非道也。根
translation_en:
His Majesty, upon ascending the throne, rectified literary style, upholding elegance and rejecting superficiality. A promulgated imperial edict declared: “The learning of scholar-officials is unsound, causing their writings and conduct of government to grow daily more aberrant, while the Way of the sages and worthies, as taught in the Great Learning, remains obscure. This bears upon good government and is certainly no trifling matter.”

Successive sage sovereigns have employed men in pursuit of good government, seeking only gentlemen of virtue and attending only to the Way of the sages and worthies taught in the Great Learning. Could one say that they selected men merely for their writing? Since the abolition of the system of recommending men from townships and selecting them from villages, even outstanding men who esteem virtue and diligently cultivate their conduct cannot put the Way widely into practice throughout the realm unless they advance through writing. Writing is therefore the step by which a gentleman gains the means to practice the Way. Nevertheless, outside writing there is no Way, and outside the Way there is no writing. The three categories of instruction in antiquity—the six virtues, the six forms of conduct, and the six arts—were all expressions of the Way. Rooted…

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
於心沛而爲辭合華實而一
之是故可以傳可以經世斯
無愧於文無愧於錄矣否則
飾辭以倖進畔於道者也其
如文何始繼科之應聘而至
也嘗自計兩浙爲東南巨藩
自昔以文獻先天下者豈以
===
文之不式爲慮惟明之未至
不免爲靡麗所眩而牝牡驪
黃之外無得焉是則可慮也
爾多士固嘗以此自慮乎盍
亦反其本矣蓋天之所以與
我者古今一而已德行文藝
胥此焉出而何有餘不足之
punctuated:
於心沛而爲辭，合華實而一之，是故可以傳，可以經世，斯無愧於文，無愧於錄矣。否則，飾辭以倖進，畔於道者也，其如文何？
始繼科之應聘而至也，嘗自計：兩浙爲東南巨藩，自昔以文獻先天下者，豈以文之不式爲慮？惟明之未至，不免爲靡麗所眩，而牝牡驪黃之外無得焉，是則可慮也。爾多士固嘗以此自慮乎？盍亦反其本矣！蓋天之所以與我者，古今一而已，德行文藝胥此焉出，而何有餘不足之
translation_en:
…rooted in the heart, pouring forth into words, uniting outward refinement and inner substance as one. Thus writing can be transmitted to posterity and serve to order the world; it then merits its standing as literature and its inclusion in this record. Otherwise, to embellish one's words in hopes of gaining advancement by good fortune is to depart from the Way. What, then, becomes of literature?
When I, Jike, first arrived in response to the invitation, I reflected: the Two Zhe form a great province of the southeast, which since ancient times has led the realm in its writings and worthy men. Why should I worry that its writing might fail to meet the standards? My only concern was that my discernment might fall short, leaving me dazzled by ornate beauty and unable to perceive anything beyond such outward features as a horse's sex and colour. This indeed was cause for concern. Have you, the assembled scholars, ever examined yourselves with this same concern? Why not return to the root? What Heaven has bestowed upon us has been the same from antiquity to the present. Virtue, conduct, literary accomplishment, and cultivated skills all issue from this source; how, then, could there be any excess or deficiency …

title: 嘉靖二十八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
日當有仰而稱之曰此聖賢
之實學也此君子之所作用
也而果出於今日浙藩之所
錄焉主司者豈不與有光榮
乎哉願相與圖之
湖廣襄陽府均州儒學學正
馮繼科謹序
punctuated:
日，當有仰而稱之曰：「此聖賢之實學也，此君子之所作用也，而果出於今日浙藩之所錄焉。」主司者豈不與有光榮乎哉？願相與圖之。

湖廣襄陽府均州儒學學正馮繼科謹序。
translation_en:
… day [?]. There should be those who look up in admiration and declare: “This is the genuine learning of the sages and worthies; this is what the gentleman puts into practice. And it has indeed emerged among those selected in the present examination in Zhejiang.” Would those presiding over the examination not also share in its glory? May we strive together toward this end.

Preface respectfully composed by Feng Jike, Instructor at the Confucian School of Junzhou, Xiangyang Prefecture, Huguang.
